title: Machine learning and multi−scale descriptor frameworks for accelerated discovery of CO2 electrocatalysts
abstract: Electrocatalytic CO2 reduction is central to sustainable fuel and chemical production, facilitating the conversion of greenhouse gases into valuable products. Progress in this field is hindered by complex reaction pathways, competing intermediates, and a high−dimensional design space, posing challenges for mechanistic understanding and material selection. Modern catalyst design increasingly relies on systematic, principle−driven approaches that link physicochemical properties to catalytic performance. Machine learning has emerged as a powerful data−centric methodology, accelerating discovery and revealing hidden patterns in extensive catalyst datasets. This review examines the role of machine learning in electrocatalytic CO2 reduction, emphasizing descriptor frameworks that connect catalyst structure with reactivity and selectivity. It considers key sources of CO2RR − related data−computed, measured, or literature−based−and analyzes strategies for constructing and validating electronic and thermodynamic descriptors. By highlighting case studies, we illustrate how machine learning models predict performance trends and screen catalysts across diverse composition spaces, offering mechanistic insights overlooked by traditional methods. We prioritize the reliability and interpretability of descriptor−based models to guide researchers in effectively utilizing machine learning in CO2RR and reshaping rational electrocatalyst discovery principles.

title: Techno-economic optimization and cycle schedule analysis of poly-bed VPSA process for CO2 capture from natural gas combustion emissions using parallel Bayesian optimization with ANN ensembles
abstract: Vacuum pressure swing adsorption (VPSA) processes stand out among CO2 capture technologies for their low energy requirement, environmental sustainability, and operational flexibility. Most existing VPSA-based CO2 capture studies have focused on coal-fired flue gas (~15% CO2). However, the ongoing shift toward natural gas-fired power plants, which emit flue gas with lower CO2 concentrations (< 10% CO2), highlights the need for systems optimized for dilute CO2 streams. Moreover, previous studies have largely been limited to small-scale systems with simplified cycle configurations, restricting their industrial applicability. This study optimizes the operating conditions and cycle configurations of industrial-scale poly-bed VPSA processes for CO2 capture by introducing a novel parallel batch multi-objective Bayesian optimization framework utilizing artificial neural network ensembles. The optimization considered three objectives of CO2 purity, recovery, and total annualized cost (TAC), with a focus on the role of pressure equalization (PE) steps in minimizing energy consumption during desorption. A pronounced trade-off was found: adding PE steps enhances CO2 purity and recovery and lowers energy consumption, but raises TAC. Notably, the optimization results indicated that incorporating three or more PE steps was essential for achieving optimal performance. Global sensitivity and techno-economic analyses were conducted to identify key variables and to examine the effects of PE steps, CO2 emission penalties, and electricity prices. To rationalize the need for PE steps, a net CO2 recovery was introduced to consider both process-level CO2 recovery and indirect CO2 emissions associated with energy consumption. This study provides a comprehensive optimization framework that balances energy efficiency, cost, and separation performance, contributing to the sustainable design of next-generation VPSA systems for low-concentration CO2 flue gas.

title: Active learning-driven multi-objective design of high-entropy alloy catalysts for saline water electrolysis
abstract: Saline water electrolysis has emerged as a promising strategy for sustainable hydrogen production due to the abundance of seawater resources. However, commercialization is hindered by reliance on precious-metal catalysts and the difficulty of maintaining selective reaction pathways under saline conditions. Here, we introduce a high-entropy alloy (HEA) catalyst design strategy enabled by an active learning, multi-objective framework that simultaneously optimizes activity, selectivity, and cost. By combining Gaussian process regression with the expected improvement acquisition, we efficiently explore the vast compositional space of HEAs using only a limited number of density functional theory calculations, achieving high predictive accuracy at ∼1.2% of the computational cost of full-space exploration. Computational results reveal distinct optimal compositions for seawater electrolysis. Cu-rich HEA compositions at the anode maximize oxygen evolution reaction activity while effectively suppressing the competing chlorine evolution reaction, providing a cost-effective alternative to conventional noble-metal-based catalysts. In addition, Ni-rich compositions exhibit hydrogen evolution reaction activity comparable to that of pure Pt while significantly reducing precious-metal content at the cathode. Overall, this active learning-driven, multi-objective protocol accelerates HEA discovery for seawater electrolysis and is readily transferable to other electrochemical energy-conversion and catalyst-design problems requiring simultaneous optimization of multiple competing objectives.

title: Inverse design of water-stable MOFs for CO2 capture from wet flue gas via AI-based descriptor engineering and theoretical investigation using DFT
abstract: Water-stable metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) for CO2 capture from wet flue gas face critical challenges, such as competitive H2O adsorption and humidity-induced structural degradation. This study presents an artificial intelligence (AI)-based descriptor engineering for inverse design framework integrating the Cascaded Tabular Generative Adversarial Network (CasTGAN) and Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network (TabPFN) to accelerate the discovery of high-performance water-stable MOFs. Analysis of the CoRE MOF 2019 dataset using correlation and mutual information methods identified pore confinement parameters (pore volume and largest cavity diameter) and framework electronegativity (metallic percentage and weighted electronegativity) as critical selectivity determinants under humid conditions. CasTGAN demonstrated superior synthetic data quality and enabled realistic MOF descriptor engineering, achieving a Fréchet inception distance of 0.017, which was lower than that of conventional GAN (1.384). Moreover, TabPFN achieved exceptional predictive accuracy (R2 of 0.959 and 0.943 for CO2/H2O and CO2/N2 selectivity, respectively), outperforming other AI models. SHAP-based explainable AI validated key descriptor contributions and guided systematic screening to identify five promising candidates: OKAYEG, OHIHET, QOKCID, QUXRIM, and ZERQOE. Density functional theory confirmed the preference of OKAYEG and QOKCID on CO2 binding (−39.48 kJ/mol and − 42.08 kJ/mol) over competing H2O (+3.82 kJ/mol and + 4.2 kJ/mol) and N2 (−30.12 kJ/mol and − 25.17 kJ/mol). This study showed that a lack of open metal sites, small pore size, and unique structural orientation enhance the CO2 uptake capacity of OKAYEG over H2O and N2. This integrated computational pipeline offers a transformative approach for the rational design of water-stable MOFs under realistic industrial flue gas conditions.

title: Electrochemical construction of Turing-patterned plasmonic MOF substrate for machine learning-assisted SERS analysis of volatile organic compounds
abstract: Plasmonic MOF materials offer a promising solution to the low affinity of volatile organic compounds (VOC) toward conventional pure-metal surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) substrates. However, the widely adopted bottom-up synthesis approaches often suffer from the irregular aggregation of metal nanostructures, impairing signal reproducibility, and the formation of flexible MOF with ligand defects, compromising selectivity. Here, we report a purely electrochemical top-down strategy to fabricate a Turing-patterned plasmonic MOF SERS substrate, in which the electrochemically sculptured Turing-patterned Ag enables highly reproducible Raman signal amplification, while the subsequently current-grown rigid ZIF-8 layer—with restricted ligand dynamics—selectively enriches volatile organic compounds via hierarchical porosity and non-covalent interactions. Notably, the Turing-patterned Ag@ZIF-8 enables instantaneous readout of the molar ratios of chloroform, benzene, and benzaldehyde in the gaseous mixtures solely by their Raman intensity ratios. By integrating spectral collection via portable Raman spectrometers with machine learning-assisted spectral analysis, we can readily distinguish colorectal cancer-related VOC profiles from healthy ones in simulated breath samples with an accuracy up to 94.0%. This work presents a novel practical approach for constructing low-cost, high-performance plasmonic MOF SERS substrates, advancing point-of-care diagnostics by leveraging SERS technique and artificial intelligence.

title: Modeling of crystallization processes using physics-informed neural networks and in-situ image analysis
abstract: Accurate determination of crystal size distribution (CSD) and kinetics is crucial for understanding and controlling crystallization. This study presents a hybrid framework integrating a crystal segmentation model (CSM) with a physics-informed neural network (PINN). The CSM, based on a YOLO instance-segmentation backbone, converts raw process images into structured CSDs and distinguishes crystals from bubbles. These CSDs and process variables are then input into a PINN that embeds the population balance equation (PBE) as soft constraints to predict CSD evolution and infer growth and nucleation kinetics directly from experimental visuals. Across multiple cooling runs, the framework accurately reconstructs full CSDs and extracts interpretable kinetic parameters. The results demonstrate that computer vision can serve as a virtual sensor providing high-quality data for PINNs, enabling physically consistent learning from experiments and advancing crystallization process modeling and control.

title: Engineered ZrFe-MOF@PtSn core–shell nanozymes enable ultrasensitive Cas12a-mediated miRNA biosensing for machine learning-aided gastric cancer diagnosis
abstract: Circulating miRNAs (e.g., miR-155 and miR-21) hold great potential as biomarkers for gastric cancer (GC) diagnosis, yet their extremely low abundance in body fluids and high sequence homology pose substantial challenges for clinical applications. Herein, an ultrasensitive electrochemical biosensing platform has been developed for precise detection of GC-associated miRNAs based on engineered core-shell nanozymes and a cascade enzymatic amplification strategy. Specifically, a miRNA-initiated SDA enabled CRISPR/Cas12a amplification strategy (miSCAS) was designed to achieve automatic signal amplification in a single-tube setup. Subsequently, the activated Cas12a cleaved the sensing-interface hairpin probes, thereby exposing the phosphate groups. Simultaneously, the ZrFe-MOF@PtSn core-shell nanozymes were synthesized by in situ growth of a ZrFe-MOF shell onto the PtSn core. This engineered architecture not only endows the nanozyme with stronger catalytic activity but also utilizes the Zr element in the ZrFe-MOF shell to form Zr-O-P bonds with the phosphate groups exposed by the probe, thereby achieving efficient amplification cascade integration of nanozyme catalysis and miSCAS. Benefiting from the synergistic signal enhancement of ZrFe-MOF@PtSn nanozymes and miSCAS, the developed biosensing method achieved an attomolar-level limit of detection (1.349 aM for miR-155 and 1.428 aM for miR-21) and demonstrated high agreement with the gold standard RT-qPCR (R2 > 0.96) in clinical sample validation. Crucially, the integration of a Lasso machine learning model enabled intelligent classification, significantly improving the accuracy of the biosensor in diagnosing GC based on dual-target current response values to 98%. This work deeply integrated nanozyme catalysis, Cas12a-based cascade amplification, and machine learning to construct a universal miRNA biosensing system, which provided a translational strategy for the precise diagnosis of GC.

title: Interpretable machine learning guides rational design of dual-site catalysts for synergistic aerobic oxidation of benzylamine
abstract: Efficient heterogeneous catalysts play a pivotal role in the aerobic oxidation of benzylamine to imine. However, conventional “trial-and-error” approaches for catalyst development are often cost-prohibitive and labor-intensive. The advent of interpretable machine learning (ML) offers a transformative solution, enabling the accelerated discovery and rational design of high-performance catalysts. Herein, we developed an interpretable XGBoost model to decode the relationship between feature descriptors and catalytic performance. Leveraging this model, we rapidly pinpointed optimal catalyst compositions with exceptional activity. Guided by these insights, we synthesized a cost-effective dual-site catalyst, FeNP-FeSA@NC-800, which demonstrated outstanding performance with complete conversion of benzylamine and 98% selectivity for imine under mild conditions (90 °C, 8 h). Moreover, the catalyst exhibited broad substrate compatibility and excellent recyclability. Control experiments and theoretical calculations revealed that the synergistic interplay between dual active sites is key to the enhanced catalytic efficiency. Specifically, the coexisting Fe nanoparticles (FeNP) effectively modulated the d-band center of Fe single atoms (FeSA), optimizing the adsorption capacity for oxygen and benzylamine, thereby accelerating the aerobic oxidation of benzylamine.

title: An integrated self-powered platform featuring acid responsive MOF probes for machine learning based early warning of lung cancer
abstract: The early and precise diagnosis of lung cancer is crucial for improving patient prognosis. This study constructs an integrated cluster based on bioinformatic design and matrix-derived energy supply for building in vitro and in vivo detection models. Through bioinformatic analysis, the highly expressed miRNA-21 in lung cancer is identified as a key biomarker. A metal-organic framework (MOF) is employed to encapsulate natural enzymes, leveraging its acid-responsive properties for controlled enzyme release. The material surface is modified with an aptamer specifically targeting miRNA-21, enabling the cluster to actively seek out and bind to the target. Innovatively, the system utilizes glucose in clinical body fluids as an endogenous fuel, converting chemical energy into electrical energy through enzyme-catalyzed redox reactions to achieve self-powering operation, thereby driving electrochemical signal output. Simultaneously, the fluorophore-modified aptamer enables synchronous fluorescence signal output, making it suitable for different clinical detection scenarios. Finally, the collected signal data are integrated with a machine learning algorithm to construct a early-warning model for lung cancer. This work establishes a streamlined pipeline from biomarker discovery to predictive clinical analysis.

title: Nanostructured composite E-nose for selective exhaled nitric oxide detection and machine learning-assisted respiratory disease diagnosis
abstract: Detection of fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) in exhaled breath is essential for monitoring respiratory diseases. Despite significant progress in NO sensing, achieving sub- parts-per-billion (ppb) detection in complex environments remains challenging. Here, we introduce a highly sensitive and selective NO sensor composed of gallium nitride nanowires (GaN-NWs) coated with zinc oxide (ZnO) and cadmium sulfide (CdS) nanoparticles (CZ-GaN-NWs). The integration of ZnO and CdS onto GaN-NWs strategically enhances sensing performance through interfacial charge transfer and surface redox reactions, leading to resistance modulation upon NO adsorption. The optimized C2Z2-GaN-NWs sensor demonstrates a 3.96-fold increase in response compared to bare GaN-NWs. It offers exceptional sensitivity with a detection limit of 2 ppb and a high signal-to-noise ratio in highly humid exhaled breath, surpassing the performance of current state-of-the-art NO sensors. Sensor arrays are further employed to enable pattern recognition capable of discriminating between simulated biomarkers and controlled breath. Validated through exhaled breath analysis, the sensor successfully distinguishes between healthy individuals and those with respiratory diseases. Moreover, advanced machine learning models accurately predict NO concentrations and classify disease stages. The proposed e-nose breath sensor offers a reliable, non-invasive solution for the early diagnosis and monitoring of respiratory diseases.

title: Design of dual-atom catalysts for CO2 reduction to C2 products: From synergistic mechanisms to machine learning guidance
abstract: Single-atom catalysts (SACs) have garnered significant attention due to their maximized atomic utilization and intrinsic catalytic activity. However, their application—particularly in multi-electron pathways—is often constrained by low metal loading and the geometric isolation of active sites. In contrast, dual-atom catalysts (DACs) offer a compelling solution by enhancing site density and fostering neighboring synergistic effects. These proximal sites provide a versatile platform for breaking scaling relations, rendering DACs an ideal strategy for facilitating CC coupling. Here, we comprehensively review the design and application of DACs for electrochemical CO2 reduction (CO2RR) to C2 products. We first elucidate the reaction mechanisms, contrasting the “single-site dilemma” of SACs with the synergistic advantages of DACs. Furthermore, we examine the critical role of machine learning (ML) in accelerating catalyst discovery, highlighting its capability to efficiently navigate the vast compositional space for rational design. Finally, we summarize existing challenges and outline future directions for bridging the gap between laboratory-scale research and industrial applications.

title: Data-driven inverse design for magnesium hydroxide precipitation: Coupling CFD–PBM with deep learning to control hexagonal platelets morphology formation and particle size distribution
abstract: Magnesium hydroxide precipitation is a key industrial process whose outcome strongly depends on operating conditions, hydrodynamics, and supersaturation dynamics, ultimately affecting particle morphology and particle size distribution (PSD). In this work, a mechanistic and data-driven inverse design framework is proposed by coupling Computational Fluid Dynamics and Population Balance Modelling (CFD-PBM) with deep learning techniques to identify precipitation kinetics and predict particle characteristics under different semi-batch feeding strategies. A neural-network-based surrogate model is employed to infer kinetic parameters governing nucleation, growth, and agglomeration directly from experimentally measured characteristic particle sizes, drastically reducing the computational burden associated with traditional optimization loops. The identified kinetic parameters are shown to be transferable across operating conditions and reactor configurations, enabling accurate predictions without re-calibration. The proposed CFD-PBM model successfully captures the effect of supersaturation generation rate on particle morphology, distinguishing between globular primary particles formed under rapid supersaturation buildup and hexagonal platelet-like structures obtained under slower supersaturation conditions. Shape effects are accounted for through morphology-dependent shape factors, demonstrating that particle shape primarily influences the quantitative magnitude of characteristic sizes while preserving qualitative trends. Model predictions are in good agreement with experimental data within the observed variability. Overall, this study provides a robust and computationally efficient framework for the mechanistic interpretation of magnesium hydroxide precipitation, offering new opportunities for morphology and PSD control through the integration of CFD-PBM modelling and advanced machine learning techniques.

title: Machine learning-driven MOF-on-MOF luminescent array for multiplexed biomarker recognition in depression diagnostics and information anticounterfeiting
abstract: The global burden of depression urgently requires precision diagnostics capable of overcoming the high misdiagnosis rate associated with symptom-based assessments. Concurrent recognition of interrelated biomarkers in body fluid is capable of improving diagnostic accuracy but remains technically challenging. However, it is remains technically challenging due to the structural similarity between the targets and their susceptibility to interference from complex matrices. To address these limitations, a machine learning (ML)-driven MOF-on-MOF (metal-organic framework) intelligent luminescent array was developed. This array leverages programmable heteroepitaxial growth to architecturally integrate distinct luminescent MOFs into a single hierarchical structure. This design enables precise spatial confinement of tunable emission centers, facilitating effective multi-channel signal generation. The multi-luminescent centers combine its multiple signal generation capabilities to convert spectral response datasets into interpretable diagnostic outputs of four biomarkers of depression via ML algorithms. This array sensor not only demonstrated low detection limits for the biomarkers but also realized nearly 100% accuracy for recognition of biomarkers, highlighting its potential for both sensitive detection and selective identification of biomarkers in serum and urine samples. The applicability of this sensor platform can also be extended to fingerprint and security code for anticounterfeiting. The integration of programmable MOF heterostructures with multi-channel signal emphasizing the critical role of multi-biomarker profiling in enhancing diagnostic accuracy and enabling personalized therapeutic monitoring.

title: Unraveling the early-stage hydration mechanism of tricalcium silicate via machine learning potentials
abstract: Portland cement (PC), the most widely used construction material globally, requires a deep understanding of its hydration mechanisms to improve its performance, with tricalcium silicates (C3S) playing a central role in determining its fundamental properties. Due to the limitations of experimental methods and the slow, inaccurate nature of traditional molecular dynamics, it is challenging to characterize reactions occurring over large temporal and spatial scales. To overcome these challenges, we used a high-precision and efficient neuroevolution potential (NEP-MLP). For the first time, we achieved atomistic-scale early-stage dynamic simulations of the complete C3S hydration process, improving computational efficiency by seven orders of magnitude compared to ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD). Our findings show that hydration begins with surface hydroxylation, followed by inward proton transfer, calcium dissolution through two coordination mechanisms, and the formation of calcium hydroxide (CH) clusters. Calcium silicate hydrate (C-S-H) gel formation occurs through both low-energy and high-energy pathways, with matrix pitting effects enhancing deep-layer reaction kinetics. This study establishes a new paradigm for cement science by bridging the atomic and engineering scales. This paradigm shift, which integrates data and physics, not only advances the field toward predictive development but also provides a foundation for designing durable, low-carbon cementitious materials for century-scale projects.

title: From selection to design: Reshaping aptamer discovery with artificial intelligence
abstract: Nucleic acid aptamers are emerging as powerful “chemical antibodies,” namely synthetic oligonucleotide ligands that emulate antibody-like molecular recognition while retaining the programmability and scalability of chemical synthesis, for precision medicine. Yet their clinical translation has been historically bottlenecked by the stochastic nature of classical discovery methods like SELEX. This trial-and-error paradigm is labor-intensive and often fails to identify binders with optimal therapeutic properties. The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is currently driving a fundamental paradigm shift from empirical screening to rational engineering. This review synthesizes the rapid evolution of this landscape, framing High-Throughput SELEX not merely as a selection tool, but as a critical data engine fueling computational discovery. We categorize current AI frameworks into two distinct paradigms: predictive architectures that decipher complex sequence-structure-function rules from noisy datasets, and generative models (e.g., VAEs, diffusion models, and inverse folding) that enable the de novo design of binders targeting specific geometries. Furthermore, we highlight translational breakthroughs in AI-designed biosensors and chemically optimized therapeutics. Finally, we discuss current challenges in data sparsity and interpretability, outlining a roadmap toward closed-loop ecosystems, that is, iterative design–test–refine workflows in which computational design, experimental validation, and model updating are continuously linked, to accelerate the development of next-generation molecular tools.

title: Unveiling the electronic regulation mechanism via a combined DFT-machine learning strategy to screen high performance single-atom catalysts on black phosphorus monolayer for LiS batteries
abstract: Lithium‑sulfur batteries (LiS), despite their high theoretical energy density, suffer from polysulfide shuttling and sluggish redox kinetics. Single-atom catalysts (SACs) offer a promising route to address these issues, but their development is impeded by both the vast chemical space and insufficient understanding of how local electronic structure controls interfacial processes. Herein, a synergistic computational strategy integrating density functional theory (DFT) with machine learning (ML) is presented to efficiently screen and design high performance SACs, using transition metal atoms anchored on black phosphorus monolayer (TM-BP) as a model system. The combined approach identifies Ti-BP, V-BP and ML-predicted Hf-BP as exceptional electrocatalysts with optimal polysulfide binding and accelerated kinetics. The underlying catalytic mechanism is further deciphered through systematic electronic structure analysis, revealing that d-p orbital hybridization plays a critical role in regulating adsorption behavior and charge transfer. Furthermore, a unique “aggregation-donation-feedback” interfacial electron transfer mechanism is proposed, which clearly elucidates the complete electronic process of Li2S on the catalyst surface, from adsorption and activation to eventual decomposition, thereby explaining the origin of catalytic activity at the quantum mechanical level. By employing the SISSO algorithm, an interpretable, low-dimensional descriptor is derived that quantitatively correlates the Li2S decomposition barrier with intrinsic properties of the metal centers, establishing a generalizable principle for catalyst design. This work establishes an efficient DFT-ML synergistic screening framework, which not only accelerates the discovery of single-atom electrocatalysts but also provides a rational design pathway for high performance cathode hosts in LiS batteries.

title: Stability-aware, transferable discovery of metal-organic frameworks for selective adsorption of C6 alkane isomers by machine learning
abstract: Separation of C6 alkane isomers is a key yet energy-intensive step in petroleum refining because they exhibit highly similar physicochemical properties. Here we develop a stability-aware, transferable discovery workflow to identify metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) capable of shape-selective (SS) or inverse shape-selective (IS) adsorption of C6 isomer mixtures comprising n-hexane (n-hex), 2-methylpentane (2mp), and 2,3-dimethylbutane (23dmb). We first perform computational screening on the CoRE-MOF-2024 database with 14,500 MOFs and reveal distinct SS/IS schemes governed by pore confinement and cavity-guest matching. To translate separation performance into practical viability, we then shortlist MOFs with thermal, activation and mechanical stabilities. Guided by these screening results, we train high-fidelity machine learning (ML) classifiers that achieve receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) ≥ 0.90 and robust accuracy (0.88–0.91), enabling rapid prioritization beyond the screened set. For the more extensive and diverse ARC-MOF database with 270,000 MOFs, we identify two experimentally actionable candidates that surpass training-set benchmarks, achieving TSN(SS) = 15.17 and TSN(IS) = 2.57. This study establishes a generalizable, stability-aware ML paradigm for accelerating the digital discovery of deployable MOFs for challenging hydrocarbon separations and other industrially important applications.

title: Advances in methane sensor development: From fundamentals to field deployment and future perspective
abstract: Methane plays a dual role in modern society, serving as a valuable energy resource while also being a major contributor to climate change and a serious safety hazard due to its explosivity. As a result, the ability to reliably detect and quantify methane is critical across a wide range of sectors, including mining, oil and gas, agriculture, and waste management. Over the past decades, a diverse array of methane sensing technologies has been developed to address these needs, spanning laboratory-scale devices, field-deployable sensors, and large-area monitoring platforms. This review examines these technologies from a practical, application-driven perspective, covering their underlying sensing principles, material systems, performance characteristics, and typical deployment contexts. Point sensors such as catalytic pellistors, non-dispersive infrared sensors, and chemiresistive devices remain central to localized safety monitoring and leak detection, where fast response and robust operation are essential. At larger spatial scales, mobile and fixed open-path optical techniques enable real-time monitoring of methane over distances ranging from tens of meters to several kilometres, while airborne and satellite-based hyperspectral imaging now plays an increasingly important role in identifying large emission sources and validating regional and global emission inventories. Rather than viewing these approaches in isolation, this review frames methane detection as a complementary, multi-scale sensing hierarchy, in which different technologies address distinct but interconnected monitoring challenges. Particular attention is given to the trade-offs that currently limit widespread deployment, including selectivity, long-term stability, environmental interference, and cost. Finally, emerging trends in sensor integration, data fusion, and the coupling of sensing platforms with Internet of Things (IoT) infrastructure and AI-based analytics are discussed as key enablers for scalable, real-time methane monitoring and more effective emission mitigation strategies.

title: Deep learning and process simulation-enabled discovery of high-performance MOFs for CO2/CH4 separation: An integrated molecular-to-process screening framework
abstract: Identifying suitable materials for industrial gas separation from a vast pool of candidates and performing preliminary process-level assessment of their separation potential remain challenging and time-consuming tasks. This study proposes a new end-to-end ultrafast screening framework for identifying optimal metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) for CO2/CH4 separation processes, using deep learning-based MOF property prediction. The proposed framework integrates molecular-level and process-level MOF screening evaluations. In the molecular-level, prescreening of the MOFs was conducted considering the physical descriptors of the MOF structures. Then, a lattice constant-hybridized graph neural network (GNN) was developed to predict CO2 and CH4 adsorption uptakes by combining global structural information with local atomic representations, overcoming the limited receptive field of standard GNN. The predicted uptakes enable pressure swing adsorption (PSA) process simulations to determine process-level metrics, including CH4 recovery and CO2 working capacity. The framework was applied to experimentally reported MOFs across three industrial scenarios with varying methane concentrations: landfill gas, biogas and coalbed methane. The proposed framework identified promising optimal MOF solutions for each application to enhance separation efficiency, including 290 for landfill gas, 42 for biogas, and 33 for coalbed methane. Structural analysis of top-performing MOFs provides recommended property ranges including pore limiting diameter of 5.12 ± 1.50 Å and volumetric surface area of 1183 ± 551 m2/cm3 that can guide adsorbent design. The techno-economic analysis demonstrates that the identified MOF-based PSA reduces separation cost by up to 51% and improves energy efficiency by up to 28% compared to conventional separation processes. This proposed screening framework provides a fast tool for narrowing large MOF databases to a manageable set of promising candidates, linking molecular-level prediction with process-level and techno-economic screening indicators that can guide subsequent rigorous evaluation.

title: Synergizing machine learning and self-assembly to hypercrosslinked polymers-based carbon nanotubes for supercapacitors
abstract: Rapid carbon-neutral industrialization has significantly increased the demand for high-performance supercapacitors. Porous carbon materials have received great attention for their tunable structures and hierarchical porosity, which can be optimized to enhance capacitance. However, further research is needed to elucidate the relationship between pore size, morphology, doping ratio, and performance for practical energy storage applications. To address this challenge, we propose an effective strategy that combines theoretical predictions with in-situ self-assembly of hypercrosslinked polymers (HCPs) to design optimal electrode materials. Machine learning identifies key features of carbon materials, while density functional theory calculations confirm the strong K+ adsorption energy (−0.33 eV) from heteroatom incorporation. Guided by these insights, nitrogen, sulfur, and oxygen-doped HCPs with tubular morphology are synthesized via the Friedel-Crafts reaction to meet the identified criteria. Further pyrolysis forms a heteroatom-enriched porous carbon nanotube with a hierarchical structure. It exhibits exceptional performance, achieving a high capacitance of 812.43 F g−1 at 0.3 A g−1 in a 6 M KOH solution, along with remarkable cycling stability, retaining 99.84% of its capacitance after 10,000 cycles at 10 A g−1. This work provides a robust strategy for the rational design of porous carbon for energy storage, leveraging advanced theoretical predictions and assembly techniques.

title: Normal/inverse sandwich structure series-engineered layer-dependent double-atom catalysts featuring bridge-bonded dual‑oxygen ligands for bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysis: Machine learning-based layer-rich extended exploration and constant-potential frontier orbital analysis
abstract: The urgent demand for efficient bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysts motivates innovative structural designs beyond conventional planar configurations. We propose a vertically stacked dual‑oxygen-bridged bilayer architecture (TMN4-2O-TMN4@C16N3) where oxygen ligands mediate interlayer charge transfer to optimize d-band and tailor adsorption of oxygen intermediates. By integrating density functional theory (DFT) with machine learning (ML), we screened 256 bilayer configurations, identifying exceptional bifunctional catalysts such as CoN4-2O-MoN4@C16N3 (ηOER = 0.49 V, ηORR = 0.36 V), outperforming IrO2/Pt benchmarks. ML predictions achieve high accuracy with mean absolute errors of 0.09 V (OER) and 0.11 V (ORR) against independent DFT validation. Crucially, constant-potential frontier orbital analysis revealed electrode-potential-driven Fermi level shifts and orbital rehybridization, decoding dynamic adsorption mechanisms beyond neutral DFT. Extension of the machine learning framework to 768 single-layer, trilayer, and quadlayer configurations enabled high-throughput exploration of expanded structural space (ultimately extending to 1024 layer-dependent configurations), with predictions rigorously validated by independent DFT calculations. While single-layer TMN4@C16N3 suffers from high OER/ORR overpotentials due to strong oxygen intermediate binding and resultant energy barriers, the trilayer structure achieves significantly lower overpotentials through optimized pathways; performance gains saturate at quadlayers as catalytic behavior becomes governed by adjacent-layer electronic coupling and diversified charge transfer pathways, highlighting the diminishing returns and critical layer-interaction synergy in layer-dependent catalyst design. This work establishes a scalable DFT-ML workflow for accelerating the discovery of oxygen-bridged electrocatalysts across diverse architectures, with the descriptor-based ML framework readily extendable to cost-effective TM combinations for practical applications.

title: Estimating dense-packed zone height in liquid–liquid separation: A physics-informed neural network approach
abstract: Separating liquid–liquid dispersions in gravity settlers is critical in chemical, pharmaceutical, and recycling processes. The dense-packed zone height is an important performance and safety indicator but it is often expensive and impractical to measure due to optical limitations. We propose a framework to estimate phase heights by combining a PINN model with readily available volume flow measurements, without requiring phase height measurements during deployment. To this end, a physics-informed neural network (PINN) is first pretrained on synthetic data and physics equations derived from a low-fidelity (approximate) mechanistic model to reduce the need for extensive experimental data. While the mechanistic model is used to generate synthetic training data, only volume balance equations are used in the PINN, as incorporating droplet coalescence and sedimentation submodels would be computationally prohibitive. The pretrained PINN is then fine-tuned with scarce experimental phase height and flow-rate data to capture the actual dynamics of the separator. We then deploy the differentiable PINN as a predictive model in an Extended Kalman Filter inspired state estimation framework, enabling the phase heights to be tracked and updated using flow-rate measurements only. We first test the two-stage trained PINN by forward simulation from a known initial state against the mechanistic model and a non-pretrained PINN. We then evaluate phase height estimation performance with the filter, comparing the two-stage trained PINN with a two-stage trained purely data-driven neural network. All model types are trained and evaluated using ensembles to account for model parameter uncertainty. In all evaluations, the two-stage trained PINN yields the most accurate phase-height estimates.

title: Machine learning integrated spirulina peptide hydrogel microneedle patches for spatiotemporal sensing mercury in marine matrices
abstract: Protein-based functional hydrogels have attracted wide attention due to their biocompatibility, tunable structures, and functional diversity. We developed a novel spirulina peptide–functionalized hydrogel (SPP), integrating the intrinsic fluorescence of natural peptides with a highly hydrated, mechanically flexible polymer network. Spirulina peptides were embedded into a dual-network hydrogel, preserving fluorescence while maintaining high hydration and mechanical performance. Acting as both Hg²⁺-selective fluorescent probes and structural components, the SPP exhibits pronounced fluorescence quenching upon Hg²⁺ exposure, enabling sensitive detection with a linear range of 50–150 μg/L and a detection limit of 4.3 μg/L. Engineered into microneedle arrays, the developed hydrogel showed enhanced adhesion and interfacial adaptability on soft, curved, and moist surfaces. Meanwhile, fluorescence signals can be rapidly digitized via smartphone and analyzed with convolutional neural networks, achieving up to 97.73% quantification accuracy under complex interfaces. This study presents a versatile strategy for efficiently incorporating natural protein functionalities into hydrogel networks, offering a promising platform for biointerface materials and intelligent protein-based functional systems.

title: Optimizing aromatics yield-selectivity trade-off in zeolite-catalyzed biomass fast pyrolysis using machine learning
abstract: Catalytic fast pyrolysis of biomass to aromatic hydrocarbons is an attractive valorization technology to produce high-value chemicals and biofuels. However, process optimization to produce desired products remains challenging due to reaction complexity. Herein, we present a data-driven approach to address this issue. A literature dataset of ZSM-5-based catalysts, including promoted and unpromoted systems is compiled, resulting in 254 datapoints and subjected to data-mining. A random forest model with uncertainty quantification is devised to predict the aromatic hydrocarbon yield, and benzene, toluene, and xylene (BTX) selectivity. The models achieved comparable performance ( R 2 > 0.80) and feature-importance analysis identified feedstock composition, catalyst total acidity, catalyst-to-biomass ratio, and space velocity as key drivers of performance metrics. Given the inherent trade-off between aromatic yield and BTX selectivities, an optimization framework was devised to screen over 20,000 promoted-zeolite and reaction condition combinations, uncovering Cu, Ga, Sn, and Zr promoted-ZSM-5 as Pareto-optimal catalysts. Lastly, motivated by challenges encountered during data collection and model limitations in out-of-box predictions, we urge the community to report biomass fast pyrolysis protocols in standardized manner, and provide effective guidelines for the cause. Our study provides a predictive toolkit to identify promising catalytic systems and optimize biomass fast pyrolysis performance while improving machine readability.

title: Single atom anchored covalent organic framework assisted with machine learning for high-throughput pesticides discrimination
abstract: The excessive use of modern pesticides poses significant risks to the environment and human health, yet their high-throughput discrimination in complex samples remains challenging. In this study, we report a functional material of single atom anchored covalent organic frameworks (COFs) based on self-assembly of COFs and iron porphyrin (COFs–Hemin) that has atomic Fe-N catalytic site, exhibiting highly efficient oxidase-like (OXD-like) and peroxidase-like (POD-like) activities and enabling efficient reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation without external energy input. COFs–Hemin with desired functional groups and nanozyme activity is employed to construct a colorimetric sensor array that successfully classifies five representative pesticides in fresh apple samples with high-throughput capability. Furthermore, integrating with a machine learning algorithm of multilayer perceptron (MLP) model that can discriminate mono-component and multicomponent mixtures of multiple pesticides, COFs–Hemin demonstrates excellent performance in surface water samples with a 95.7% classification accuracy and area under the curve (AUC) values exceeding 0.93 across all pesticide categories. The strategy that integrates single atom anchored COFs and machine learning delivers a reliable tool for high-throughput discrimination of multiple pesticides in environmental monitoring and food safety.

title: Unifying CO2 diffusion mechanisms in diamine-functionalized metal–organic frameworks via quantum-accurate machine learning dynamics
abstract: Diamine-functionalized M2(dobpdc) metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) (dobpdc4- = 4,4'-dioxidobiphenyl-3,3'-dicarboxylate; M = Mg, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Zn) exhibit exceptional CO2 capture, yet their CO2 diffusion behavior has remained difficult to rationalize across pore sizes, loadings, and functionalization. Here we resolve this gap by combining diffusion measurements with quantum-accurate machine-learning-potential molecular dynamics (MLP-MD) to establish a unified, loading-dependent mechanism for CO2 transport in Mg2(dobpdc) MOFs. Our MLPs reproduce density functional theory energetics and forces, enabling converged diffusion coefficients and microscopic trajectories. By comparing Mg2(dobdc), Mg2(dobpdc), and Mg2(dotpdc), we show that at low uptake CO2 is transiently trapped near open Mg sites, producing suppressed diffusivity in both MLP-MD simulations and diffusion measurements. With increasing uptake, the progressive saturation of these strong adsorption sites screens their trapping potential, leading to a rise in diffusion coefficients for Mg2(dobpdc) and Mg2(dotpdc), quantitatively consistent with experiments. Diamine functionalization further accelerates CO2 transport by limiting access to open Mg sites and introducing cooperative CO2–diamine interactions. Finally, the same MLPs accurately predict CO2 adsorption isotherms via grand canonical Monte Carlo. Together, the experimentally validated MLP-MD framework reveals how pore size and diamine functionalization synergistically govern CO2 diffusion, providing design rules for high-capacity MOFs with improved mass transport.

title: Ba- and Mg-promoted Ni/g-C3N4 for efficient CO2 methanation using in-house data machine learning
abstract: Methanation is one of the solutions for decreasing carbon emissions and synthetic green fuels production, being a potentially large-scale option for CO 2 utilization. However, thermodynamics in conventional reaction conditions limit the CO 2 conversion. In this work, alkaline-earth-metal modified nickel nanoparticles supported on graphitic carbon nitride (g-C 3 N 4 ) were tested in a fixed-bed reactor, being a compelling route for atmospheric CO 2 methanation. The use of g-C 3 N 4 as a support offers a more sustainable and environmentally friendly alternative to conventional oxide materials, while maintaining competitive catalytic performance with lower Ni loading and milder activation conditions. The catalysts were synthesized using two synthesis approaches: pre-incorporation and co-impregnation with Ni and Ba or Mg into the g-C₃N₄ lattice. The catalysts were characterised using N 2 physisorption, XRD, H 2 -TPR, CO 2 -TPD, TPR, Raman and XPS. The catalyst, where first incorporating the alkaline-earth metal into the g-C 3 N 4 support (Ni/g-C 3 N 4 -Mg), exhibited the best overall performance, achieving a 17-fold increase in CO 2 conversion (from 3 to 51%) and a substantial enhancement in CH 4 selectivity (from 13 to 94%) compared to the undoped catalyst at 325 °C. The Mg-promoted catalyst has better-dispersed Ni nanoparticles, stronger metal-support interaction, greater proportion of metallic Ni species and more moderate basic sites than Ni/g-C 3 N 4 . Mg incorporation also creates Lewis basic sites and increases overall CO 2 adsorption sites on the eg-C 3 N 4 support. The linked Mg dopant and eg-C 3 N 4 synergy drives high activity and stability for low-temperature CO 2 methanation. The catalyst prepared by pre-incorporating the alkaline-earth Ba into the g-C 3 N 4 (Ni/g-C 3 N 4 -Ba) exhibits degraded textural properties and basicity. The presence of barium promotes the stabilization of ferromagnetic Ni clusters. However, the intense signals from Ni + single sites justify the catalyst's performance. Overall, the increased surface nitrogen concentration and the higher proportion of metallic Ni species are clearly beneficial for CO₂ activation and hydrogenation, underscoring their pivotal role in enhancing catalytic activity. In summary, these results highlight the crucial role of promoter choice in CO₂ hydrogenation catalysts, with Mg or Ba-doped Ni/g-C₃N₄ presenting an effective route for methane synthesis. An in-house dataset (71 CO 2 methanation runs) was used to train a Random Forest model to predict CH 4 yield from six controllable descriptors. The model ranked temperature, metal identity, and support-promoter loading as the main drivers and, through surrogate-based screening, identified an optimum at 350 °C over Ni/g-C 3 N 4 promoted with Mg on the support (CSP = 1.0 mmol) without a metal promoter.
