title: Dual-objective protein language model for discovery of non-hemolytic antimicrobial peptides from the bee-melectin sequence space
abstract: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are the natural defense molecules of the innate immune system, and have emerged as promising alternatives to conventional antibiotics owing to their broad-spectrum activity and low resistance potential. However, their clinical translation is hindered by proteolytic degradation and slow discovery pipelines. To address this, we developed a ProtBERT-based dual-objective machine learning (ML) framework and applied it to a constrained library of 20,000 peptide variants (6–12 residues) derived from the 18-residue bee-venom AMP, Melectin. The model was trained on curated datasets (∼25,000) to simultaneously screen for high antimicrobial potency and minimal hemolytic toxicity. This targeted approach identified 16 hit candidates, from which two lead peptides emerged, each containing at least four mutations relative to known sequences. The optimized peptides exhibited potent activity against methicillin-resistant S. aureus and P. aeruginosa, while demonstrating negligible hemolysis. The D-enantiomer of the lead peptide demonstrated efficacy against drug-resistant strains within serum-rich media. In 3D-spheroid infection models, the peptides demonstrated strong antimicrobial activity and low cytotoxicity, reflecting the promise of host-defense peptides and ML-guided strategies for scalable AMP discovery.

title: Deep learning-assisted intelligent fluorescence sensor incorporating perovskite quantum dots with dual-recognition imprinting polymers for ultrasensitive and high-selectivity kanamycin detection
abstract: Kanamycin (KANA) overuse threatens public health, necessitating precise and portable detection approaches. To address this challenge, a ratiometric fluorescence sensor (TB-Eu-MOFs@MIPs@CsPbBr₃-Rb) was innovatively developed for ultrasensitive and selective detection of KANA. This sensor integrated oriented molecular imprinting on TB-Eu-MOFs with in-situ encapsulation of CsPbBr₃-Rb perovskite quantum dots. High-affinity imprinting layer featuring covalent/non-covalent dual-recognition sites boosted the precise identification of TB-Eu-MOFs@MIPs@CsPbBr₃-Rb to KANA. Thanks to synergistic dual-mechanism of dynamic quenching and electron transfer, water-resistant CsPbBr₃-Rb (520 nm) underwent pronounced fluorescence quenching upon exposure to KANA, boosting sensitivity. Conversely, the red fluorescence (620 nm) of TB-Eu-MOFs remained unaffected. Given inherent merits, TB-Eu-MOFs@MIPs@CsPbBr₃-Rb demonstrated exceptional suitability for ratiometric fluorescence profiling of KANA, featuring a linear range of 0.075–24.000 μg/mL, a detection limit of 22.5 ng/mL, a superior imprinting factor (6.66), ultra-fast response (2 min), attractive green-yellow-pale pink-red transformation, and satisfactory recoveries (90.00–98.43%). Intriguingly, by integrating a deep learning-driven smartphone device, the proposed sensor achieved on-site identification, concentration classification, and quantitative assay of KANA, demonstrating commendable precision and desirable recoveries (90.47–109.85%) in tap water, milk, and chicken. Accordingly, the deep learning-driven fluorescence sensor exhibited portability, feasibility, high selectivity, and sensitivity, offering a powerful tool for on-site food safety and environmental monitoring with high practicality.
keywords: Ratiometric fluorescence and deep learning-assisted intelligent detection

title: Elucidating the dual role of fulvic acid in Cu2+ adsorption on Mn-modified algal biochar through density functional theory and machine learning analyses
abstract: Cu2+ contamination in aquatic environments poses serious ecological and health risks, requiring efficient, sustainable remediation strategies. In this study, Mn-modified algal biochar was prepared and used as a model adsorbent to elucidate fulvic-acid (FA)-mediated Cu2+ adsorption in a ternary system. Characterization analyses revealed that Mn modification substantially increased the specific surface area, mesopore volume, and oxygen-containing surface functional groups, thereby enhancing Cu2+ affinity. Batch experiments demonstrated a pronounced FA “dual effect”: at a low concentration of 10 mg·L−1, FA markedly enhanced Cu2+ adsorption capacity up to 211.6 mg·g−1 through ternary surface complexation and increased negative surface charge, whereas a higher concentration of 20 mg·L−1 inhibited adsorption through competitive complexation in solution and surface-site blockage. Kinetic and isotherm analyses indicated dominant chemisorption, best described by the pseudo-second-order and Langmuir models, respectively. Density functional theory calculations clarified the microscopic mechanism, supporting preferential Cu2+ anchoring by MnO and carboxyl sites on the biochar followed by FA bridging to form stable ternary complexes. An extreme gradient boosting machine-learning model achieved strong predictive performance (R2 = 0.941 on the test set), with FA concentration and pH identified as the most influential factors. The major contribution of this work is not only the observation of FA concentration-dependent behavior, but also the identification of a DFT-supported Cu-bridged ternary complexation pathway and the ML-based quantification of key environmental controls. These findings provide mechanistic insights into FA-mediated Cu2+ adsorption and support Mn-modified algal biochar as a promising, sustainable adsorbent for heavy-metal remediation in surface water.

title: A fully adaptive automated system for nanoparticle washing enabled by vision and language AI
abstract: Self-driving laboratories are reshaping materials discovery by combining automated experimentation with AI-driven decision-making. However, the lack of automation in key preprocessing steps such as nanoparticle (NP) washing, remains a major barrier to achieving full experimental autonomy. Effective automation of NP washing requires visual adaptivity to detect subtle changes in the appearance of dispersions or precipitates, and cognitive adaptivity, to handle failure cases like incomplete sedimentation or phase separation. These demands make NP washing uniquely challenging despite its apparent simplicity. We introduce a fully integrated NP washing platform that combines computer vision with a large language model (LLM) to enable intelligent, end-to-end preprocessing in self-driving labs. The system employs YOLACT for real-time robotic manipulation and latent mask R-CNN for uncertainty-aware image segmentation, achieving 100% task success across 60 trials and accurately processing 45 diverse precipitate images. A retrieval-augmented LLM autonomously generates and continuously refines washing protocols based on cognitive feedback from failure detection. The platform was validated on NiFe layered double hydroxides, IrRu nanoparticles, and CdSe/CdS quantum dots. Electrochemical and photoluminescence analyses demonstrated that the automated washing achieves a quality comparable to manual processing. This work represents a critical step toward fully autonomous, closed-loop experimentation by bridging synthesis and characterization through intelligent preprocessing.

title: Dual-enhancement strategy for high-performance multimodal hydrogel sensors in deep learning-assisted speech recognition systems
abstract: Conductive hydrogels under large deformation often suffer from stress concentration and pronounced hysteresis, compromising their mechanical integrity and sensing reliability. Here, we propose a dual-reinforcement strategy to develop a multimodal hydrogel sensor based on amphiphilic polymer chains and MXene nanosheets. The reinforced hydrophobic micelles integrate hydrophobic association, triple hydrogen bonding, and π–π stacking to mitigate stress concentration and hysteresis, while MXene introduces nanoscale confinement and strong interfacial interactions, enhancing elastic recovery and reducing energy dissipation. The resulting hydrogel exhibits excellent stretchability (>1000% elongation), high toughness (2.75 MJ m-3), low hysteresis (4.1% at 400% strain), an ultralow detection limit (0.1%), and stable sensitivity (GF = 1.16) over a wide strain range (0.1-500%) with outstanding fatigue resistance (10,000 cycles). It also enables multimodal sensing of deformation and temperature (TCR=-2.13%°C-1), and can monitor environmental perturbations such as wind and hail impact. Combined with a deep learning framework, the sensor achieves 97% recognition accuracy for language-related inputs. Moreover, its intrinsic biodegradability reduces environmental impact. These features highlight its promise for healthcare monitoring, AI interfaces, and electronic skin systems.

title: Deep learning-driven strategies for the de novo design of membrane-targeting narrow-spectrum antimicrobial peptides
abstract: As the global antimicrobial resistance (AMR) crisis continues to escalate, narrow-spectrum antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) have emerged as an important direction in precision anti-infective research. However, current AMPs design strategies remain largely focused on the optimization of broad-spectrum activity, and a systematic framework centered on pathogen-specific membrane interfaces is still lacking. This review focuses on deep learning (DL)-driven de novo design of membrane-interface-centered, or membrane-targeting, narrow-spectrum AMPs. It first delineates the conceptual boundaries among selectivity, targeting, specificity, and narrow-spectrum activity, and systematically summarizes exploitable differences at the cellular membrane level. It then further discusses how membrane-associated differences can be translated into programmable constraints within DL models, on the basis of which four major design routes are summarized. Subsequently, a multi-objective evaluation framework is established, and the workflow for AMPs validation across four distinct levels is outlined. Ultimately, in view of the current state of the field and its future development, targeted questions and methodological recommendations are proposed, with the aim of providing a clearer theoretical framework and methodological reference for more advanced AMPs design.

title: Crystal field splitting energy mediated d-band center regulation in transition metal for enhancing plasma/persulfate degradation of metronidazole: Experiments, theoretical calculation and machine learning study
abstract: Modulating the d-band center of transition metals by doping engineering is an efficient strategy to enhance their catalytic efficiency. However, there remains a lack of systematic theoretical explanation for how doping engineering modulates the d-band center and activates antibonding orbitals at the electronic structure scale. Herein, using α-Fe2O3 (αFO) as a model transition metal, machine learning, density functional theory calculations and experimental characterization were integrated to elucidate the doping induced d-band center shifts. The results reveal that dopants modulated the crystal field splitting energy of transition metals, which in turn tailors the d-band center, thereby enhancing the catalyst's ability to activate the antibonding orbitals of reactive species. This mechanism rationalized the efficient degradation of metronidazole observed in the Cu-αFO/DBD/persulfate process. Furthermore, to elucidate the degradation mechanism at the molecular level, this study investigated the structure-activity relationship, specifically how the molecular structure of the pollutants and the catalytic system influence the degradation efficiency. The data revealed the correlation between molecular properties (e.g., dipole moment and energy of the lowest unoccupied molecular orbital) and degradation kinetics. The proposed d-band center modulation and antibonding orbital activation mechanism provides both a theoretical foundation and a practical pathway for the rational design of high performance transition metal catalysts.

title: Machine learning-optimized coarse-grained simulations reveal multicomponent solvent-regulated phase separation for precise control of porous polymers
abstract: Precise control of pore structures in porous polymers is critical for optimizing their functional performance. Although third solvent-assisted phase separation has been experimentally demonstrated to promote pore interconnectivity and structural tunability, the molecular mechanisms governing this process remain largely unresolved. Here, we develop a machine learning-assisted dissipative particle dynamics (DPD) force fields that bridges all-atom-level accuracy and coarse-grained efficiency through data-driven force field generation. By training on structural descriptors derived from all-atom simulations, the optimized DPD force fields reliably reproduce intermolecular interactions in multicomponent solvent systems. Applying this optimized force field to polylactic acid ternary solvent systems, we reveal how the third solvent modulates phase separation behavior and propose a quantitative solvent-selection principle based on polarity and interaction energy. Experimental validation confirms the predictive capability of the model in guiding pore morphology control. Together, these results provide molecular-level insights and a practical framework for multicomponent solvent engineering, offering a pathway toward the rational fabrication advanced porous polymer materials with precisely controllable structures.

title: Synthesis of highly active binary alloy acidic oxygen evolution catalysts assisted by machine learning
abstract: Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) is promising for green hydrogen production, but its oxygen evolution reaction (OER) suffers from high overpotential and catalyst corrosion. While transition metal alloys exhibit excellent catalytic activity, traditional experiments and density functional theory (DFT) calculations are inefficient for exploring the vast binary alloy space. Machine learning enables rapid prediction and optimization by mining DFT data to map material properties with catalytic performance. Herein, this study integrates machine learning methods, including ABR, GBR, and other ensemble models, with DFT calculations to rapidly screen of acidic OER catalysts based on binary transition metal systems. Based on model predictions, we utilize electrodeposition and Joule heating techniques to synthesize FeRu alloy in a short period of time and perform experimental validation. The as-synthesized FeRu alloy exhibits exceptional bifunctional activity, requiring ultralow overpotentials of 171 mV (OER) and 47 mV (hydrogen evolution reaction) to achieve 10 mA cm−2 in acidic media. This catalyst reaches a current density of 1 A cm−2 at only 1.65 V in PEMWE. DFT calculations confirm that alloying optimizes electronic structure and reduces the rate-determining step (RDS) energy barrier, providing theoretical support for its excellent activity and stability. This work establishes a closed-loop framework that integrates data mining with experimental validation to shorten catalyst research and development cycles. It provides an efficient approach for screening and optimizing high-performance acidic PEMWE catalysts and facilitates the industrialization of green hydrogen production via PEMWE.

title: Machine learning-assisted modeling of tandem catalytic polymerization for tailoring comb-branched polyolefin elastomers
abstract: Polyolefin elastomers are widely utilized due to their unique combination of thermoplastic processability and rubber-like elasticity. Among them, comb-branched polyolefin elastomers (CPOEs) synthesized via tandem catalytic polymerization (TCP) of ethylene and α-olefin feature amorphous backbones with long polyethylene (PE) side chains, enabling elevated melting temperatures even at high α-olefin incorporation. Because TCP integrates ethylene homopolymerization with terpolymerization of ethylene, 1-octene, and PE macromonomers (PEMs), kinetic modeling is essential for tailoring CPOE chain structures while simultaneously controlling PEM incorporation and residual content. Herein, a kinetic model based on the method of moments was developed, with an orthogonalization algorithm employed to reduce the number of parameters requiring estimation. Direct coupling of the kinetic model with differential evolution (DE) optimization using a conventional ODE solver proved computationally intensive for parameter estimations. A large-scale training dataset was generated from the kinetic model with parameter ranges aligned to literature values and experimental observations, substantially reducing the need for expensive experimental data. The ML-assisted model was validated against experimental results. Systematic analyses of catalyst concentrations, 1-octene concentration, and polymerization times elucidated their impacts on CPOE chain structure, providing mechanistic insights for CPOE design. Overall, this study demonstrates a practical ML-assisted strategy for kinetic modeling of complex polymerization systems and provides a powerful tool for rational CPOE chain structure engineering and data-driven polymer product development.

title: Molecular characterization and chlorination reactivity of microplastics-derived dissolved organic matter revealed by ultrahigh-resolution mass spectrometry and machine learning
abstract: Microplastics-derived dissolved organic matter (MPs-DOM) comprises a chemically heterogeneous pool of dissolved organic compounds released during the environmental degradation of microplastics. Despite growing interest in the environmental implications of MPs-DOM, its molecular composition and reactivity are still poorly characterized. In this study, Fourier-transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FT-ICR MS) was employed to characterize MPs-DOM released from polystyrene (PS), polyamide (PA), and poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT), as well as their transformation products formed during chlorination, and a reactivity prediction model was developed based on reaction networks. The results showed that all microplastics released MPs-DOM under dark conditions, while UV irradiation altered MPs surface functional groups and the molecular composition of the released MPs-DOM, leading to differences in chlorination reactivity between the dark and UV conditions. CHO dominated DOM derived from PS and PBAT, whereas PA-DOM was relatively enriched in CHNO compounds, indicating that MPs-DOM exhibited high molecular complexity and source dependent characteristics. Both aging and chlorination induced pronounced molecular transformations, leading to a significant increase in O/C ratios. The reaction network analysis linked 111 chlorine-containing DBP molecules to 127 precursors, including 122 polymer-specific precursors, with 63, 23, and 35 detected in PS, PA, and PBAT, respectively. A machine learning model based on extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) successfully identified double bond equivalent (DBE) and nominal oxidation state of carbon (NOSC) as the primary molecular features associated with highly reactive MPs-DOM, achieving an overall prediction accuracy of 73.53%. This work provides a molecular-level understanding of the composition, formation mechanisms, and chlorination behavior of MPs-DOM, improving our understanding of the environmental behavior and potential risks associated with MPs-DOM.

title: Bioinspired hierarchically structured liquid metal-composited eutectogel for energy conversion and intelligent perception
abstract: Inspired by the hierarchical structure of brain’s blood vessels and neural networks, which enables synergistic trade-offs among multiple properties, we developed a structural biomimetic strategy to create liquid metal (LM)-initiated polymerizable deep eutectic solvents (PDES) eutectogels. In this design, the polymerizable hydrogen bond donor forms polymer chains that mimic vascular walls and provide mechanical support, while the hydrogen bond acceptor enables ion transport for signal transmission, analogous to neurotransmitter-mediated communication. LM acts as a ”growth factor” to induce the formation of a biomimetic hierarchical network in PDES-based eutectogels. Specifically, LM introduces ionic coordination bonds to construct a hierarchical supramolecular network, while simultaneously serving as a conductive filler to establish an ion-electron conductive network, with interfacial modification promoting the dissociation of hydrogen bond acceptors. Consequently, the resulting eutectogels achieve a balanced combination of mechanical strength, ultrastretchability ((451.8 kPa, 1106%) ~substantially outperforming LM-free PDES eutectogels), high elasticity (energy dissipation rate <15% within 500% strain), and excellent ionic conductivity (~31.19 mS cm-1). This strategy effectively overcomes the practical application limitations of PDES eutectogels arising from their insufficient mechanical performance and low ionic conductivity. Furthermore, based on this platform, a ”dynamic-static” self-powered system enables low-grade heat and mechanical energy conversion into electricity while serving as a supercapacitor (SC) electrolyte for energy storage. Integrated with a convolutional neural network (CNN), the PDES-LM20 eutectogel enabled multi-channel gesture recognition with 99.5% accuracy for ten gestures. This work bridges structural biomimicry and functional synergy, advancing integrated gel platforms for energy conversion, storage, and intelligent perception.

title: “Tensile strain + X” multimodal sensors: Decoupling, anti-interference, and applications
abstract: Conventional flexible strain sensors can only detect mechanical deformation, which limits their ability to perceive multiple physical stimuli in complex scenarios such as health monitoring and human–robot interaction. To overcome this limitation, ”tensile strain + X” multimodal sensors that integrate strain sensing with other modalities (e.g., pressure, temperature, humidity, magnetic field, and bioelectricity) have emerged as a promising solution. This review provides a systematic overview of recent progress in these sensors, with an emphasis on decoupling strategies and anti‐interference methodologies. According to the output signal type and decoupling principle, existing devices are classified into four categories: single‐output, multi‐output, structurally/spatially separated, and algorithm‐assisted decoupling. Single‐output sensors exploit polarity, temporal, or amplitude differences for signal separation under constrained conditions. Multi‐output sensors achieve inherent crosstalk freedom via heterogeneous signals (e.g., electro‐optical, resistance‐voltage). Structural/spatial separation physically isolates sensing units through modulus modulation or modular design. Algorithm‐assisted decoupling employs frequency‐domain filtering, matrix algebra, and data‐driven models (e.g., LSTM, CNN) to reconstruct individual physical quantities from mixed signals. Key anti‐interference strategies, including intrinsically insensitive materials, encapsulation layers, and temporal/scenario separation, are also discussed. The applications of these sensors have expanded from limb motion monitoring to sports rehabilitation, simultaneous respiration‐behavior tracking, human‐machine interaction, and structural health monitoring. Finally, future directions are outlined, focusing on intrinsically decoupling materials, edge intelligence, and multimodal fusion for robotics and embodied intelligence. This review offers a comprehensive framework that guides the design of next‐generation intelligent multimodal sensors.

title: Structure-resolved adsorption of PFAS on humic substances: A combined study of molecular dynamics, explainable machine learning, and experiments
abstract: Understanding the adsorption behavior of PFAS on humic substances (HS) is critical for predicting their environmental fate and developing effective remediation strategies. Here, we integrate molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, experimental characterization, and explainable machine learning (XAI) to resolve PFAS interactions with HS at the molecular level. Based on 410 PFAS structures, MD-derived adsorption energies reveal a clear structure-dependent adsorption trend, with a strong negative correlation (Pearson's |r| > 0.72) between molecular weight and adsorption energy magnitude. Machine learning models show robust predictive performance (R2 > 0.88), enabling accurate adsorption-energy prediction across structurally diverse PFAS. SHAP analysis reveals that PFAS adsorption onto HS is governed by a synergistic interplay of multiple molecular descriptors rather than any single molecular property. Molar refractivity, Kappa3, Number of hydrogen bond acceptors, and molecular weight emerge as the most influential descriptors, highlighting the coupled roles of electronic polarizability, molecular topology, conformational adaptability, and size in controlling adsorption. In contrast, descriptors associated with polarity and hydration tendency are more closely linked to migration behavior. Adsorption experiments and complementary spectroscopic and microscopic characterizations consistently confirmed stronger fluorine accumulation and greater compaction of the HS matrix induced by long-chain PFAS. Overall, the results converge on a unified molecular picture in which larger, more polarizable, and structurally adaptable PFAS are preferentially retained, whereas smaller and more hydration-favored PFAS remain comparatively mobile. This work provides a physics-informed and interpretable framework for predicting PFAS transport in heterogeneous organic environments.

title: Machine learning-assisted screening of efficient homogeneous catalysts for the aerobic reaction of aromatic hydrocarbons
abstract: The ligand modification of the catalyst is a promising strategy to enhance the yields of the aerobic reaction of aromatic hydrocarbons. The approach of machine learning incorporating high-throughput density functional theory (DFT) calculations successfully achieves the efficient screening and design of catalysts. In this work, the impact of ligands on catalyst activity was investigated. The results reveal how ligands influence the catalyst's properties and structure, which subsequently affects its reaction activity. A unique descriptor, φ, which is the ratio of nonpolar and surface area, was identified using ML for predicting yields and efficiently capturing catalytic activity trends for a variety of ligands (R2 = 0.999, error < 1%). The optimal catalyst, Cat II (cobalt bis(2-ethylhexanoate)), was selected by ML, which exhibits the highest yield (22.81 mol%). The kinetic model achieves great predictive ability for the variation in compound concentration under different conditions. The strategy incorporates ML, experimentation, and reaction kinetics, offering significant insights into catalyst screening, modifications, aerobic reaction, and modeling of aromatic hydrocarbons.

title: ELEVATE-LNP: Empty lipid nanoparticle enabled validation and AI-guided therapeutic evaluation for efficient formulation optimization for mRNA delivery
abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have emerged as a leading platform for mRNA delivery, particularly following the success of SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccines. However, identifying effective LNP formulations remains time-consuming because of the large and complex multicomponent formulation space. Here, we present ELEVATE-LNP an Empty-LNP-Enabled Validation and AI-Guided Therapeutic Evaluation platform by integrating a high-throughput parallelized microfluidic preparation with physicochemical characterization and machine learning for mid-stream and downstream LNP formulation optimization when ionizable lipids are shortlisted. A broad formulation space comprising four ionizable lipids, different helper lipids, lipid ratios, and process conditions was first screened using empty LNPs to identify formulations with desirable particle size and polydispersity index (PDI). Machine-learning analysis was then used to determine the formulation and process parameters associated with empty-LNP properties. Selected candidates were subsequently evaluated following mRNA encapsulation by assessing particle size, PDI, encapsulation efficiency, cell viability, and transfection performance. The results revealed lipid-dependent relationships between formulation parameters and the physicochemical properties of empty LNPs. Six features were strongly associated with particle size, while eleven features contributed to variations in PDI. GFP expression in CFBE cells demonstrated that SM-102-based LNPs achieved higher transfection efficiency than CKK-E12-based formulations. In a separate CFTR mRNA evaluation, DOPC-containing LNPs produced higher CFTR protein expression than their DSPC-containing counterparts. By integrating empty-LNP prescreening with subsequent payload-based validation, the ELEVATE-LNP workflow reduces the number of candidates and the amount of nucleic acid required for functional testing. The platform therefore provides a practical approach for narrowing lipid-ratio and formulation-condition spaces within preselected ionizable lipid systems.

title: AI-driven de novo protein design coupled with high-throughput screening: Challenges and opportunities
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming protein engineering from an empirical discipline into a predictive and data-driven paradigm, accelerating the development of next-generation biocatalysts. Nevertheless, a significant gap remains because generative models can propose candidate proteins far more rapidly than laboratories can experimentally them, and computational novelty does not guarantee the performance under most of the process conditions. This review examines recent advances in AI-assisted protein engineering, highlighting how generative models, protein language models, and structure-prediction frameworks are reshaping enzyme discovery, design, and optimization. The evolution from conventional rational design and directed evolution to modern data-centric workflows built on the Design–Build–Test–Learn (DBTL) cycle is explored. Major AI architectures, such as transformers, diffusion models, variational autoencoders, and generative adversarial networks, are evaluated for their ability to generate novel protein structures and functional sequences. Most importantly, we summarize machine learning approaches for predicting enzyme activity, substrate specificity, catalytic efficiency, thermostability, solubility, and functional annotation, which facilitate candidate prioritization and reduce the experimental burden. Reported predictive performance reaches an R2 of 0.69 for turnover number and a Pearson coefficient of 0.84 for stability change, while computational triage eliminates 50% to 80% of the design pool before synthesis. Because sequence-function relationships are inherently nonlinear, a single metric optimization is unreliable. We therefore discuss current limitations, arising from data scarcity, model interpretability, cross-family transferability, developability, and the lack of standardized benchmarks. Future perspectives are provided on integrating multimodal biological data, foundation models, and autonomous experimentation to enable scalable biocatalyst development and accelerate the transition toward AI-driven sustainable biomanufacturing.

title: Physics-informed surrogate modeling and optimization of Zn–Co substituted Ba–W ferrite/CNT/TPU composites for microwave absorbers
abstract: Achieving thin, target-specific microwave absorbers remains challenging because absorber performance is governed by the coupled interplay among complex permittivity, complex permeability, and thickness, while the direct linkage between target absorption behavior, electromagnetic-property spectra, and realizable material compositions is often limited. Here, we present a physics-informed optimization framework based on Zn–Co substituted Ba–W ferrite/CNT/TPU composites, in which magnetic and dielectric responses can be tuned in a decoupled manner. Co substitution in Ba–W ferrite selectively shifts the magnetic-loss frequency through anisotropy-controlled ferromagnetic resonance, whereas CNT loading independently modulates the dielectric response without significantly perturbing the magnetic behavior. Exploiting this decoupled tunability, complex permittivity and permeability were modeled separately using Kramers–Kronig-consistent spectral representations, namely a hybrid Cole–Cole model and a Gaussian–Dawson master-curve model, and then integrated into a differential-evolution-based optimization loop. This framework transformed discrete experimental datasets into a physically constrained continuous composition space, enabling continuous prediction of composition-dependent electromagnetic properties and target-specific optimization of absorber composition and thickness. As representative demonstrations, a 1.9 mm-thick absorber achieved full X-band absorption below −10 dB, whereas a 1.5 mm-thick absorber achieved nearly full Ku-band absorption below −10 dB with a measured −20 dB EAB of 3.76 GHz. Both absorbers were fabricated as 12 × 12 cm specimens and successfully validated by free-space RL measurements. This study provides an integrated framework that connects absorber performance, electromagnetic-property prediction, and material composition within a physically grounded optimization scheme.

title: Unveiling the structural basis of Adeno-associated virus CNS tropism via geometric protein language modeling
abstract: Adeno-associated virus (AAV) capsid engineering enables tissue-selective gene delivery; however, identifying variants with enhanced central nervous system (CNS) tropism remains challenging. Notwithstanding the success of directed evolution approaches, it often faces practical limitations, including the substantial loss of library diversity during cloning and packaging, production biases that confound functional selection, and difficulties in assessing production fitness independently of tissue tropism. Moreover, this process requires extensive animal experimentation and iterative selection cycles, making it resource-intensive and time-consuming. Here, we developed a machine learning framework that simultaneously predicts both capsid production fitness and tissue-specific enrichment, providing capsid-residue-level biological interpretation that could be used rationally to identify CNS-targeting AAV variants. We performed in vivo directed evolution of AAV9 by replacing residues at the surface-exposed loops of VR-IV and VR-VIII, subjecting libraries to two rounds of systemic selection in mice, and quantifying tissue-specific enrichment across multiple CNS and peripheral tissues. Meanwhile, by integrating protein-language model embeddings and AlphaFold-derived structural features into attention-based neural networks, our framework achieved high predictive accuracy while providing residue-level biological interpretation. Structural validation confirmed a significant correlation between the predicted binding affinity and CNS enrichment. Moreover, this study demonstrates that high-performing tissue-targeting variants possess residues enriched in glycine, serine, and arginine, exhibiting broader charged surfaces, larger hydrophobic patches, and greater solvent accessibility. This computational framework enables capsid residue-level biological interpretation based on experimental data, which could potentially improve variant selection accuracy and reduce experimental time and animal use, establishing a foundation for rational identification of CNS-targeting variants in future studies.

title: Machine learning-assisted descriptor screening of high-entropy alloy-based catalysts for CO2 methanation
abstract: Carbon dioxide hydrogenation provides a route for converting CO 2 into methane (CH 4 ), but the large compositional space of high-entropy alloy (HEA)-based catalysts complicates empirical catalyst selection. In this study a literature-derived dataset of 251 observations was analysed using machine learning to evaluate composition-derived atomic and electronic descriptors together with surface, synthesis, and reaction variables. XGBR achieved random-split test R 2 values of 0.95 for CO 2 conversion and 0.91 for CH 4 selectivity, whereas intrinsic-descriptor-only models achieved R 2 values of 0.37 and 0.69, respectively, showing that full-model performance arises from combined catalyst and process information. SHAP and partial-dependence analyses identified reaction temperature and composition-derived descriptors including weighted Pauling electronegativity (EN), weighted atomic radius (R), and ΔR as influential model features. Weighted Pauling EN above approximately 1.2, smaller weighted atomic radii (R), and low ΔR were associated with favourable model predictions within the present dataset. These relationships are interpreted as empirical screening trends rather than direct mechanistic thresholds. NSGA-II and fuzzy logic analysis defined descriptor space screening regions, and more than 205 million five-element compositions were enumerated, of which 4,811,467, or 2.35%, satisfied the property window criteria. Experimental assessment showed lower apparent activation energies than Ni/Al 2 O 3 for several HEA-based formulations, with AlCdMgCoNi achieving 45 kJ mol −1 compared with 75 kJ mol −1 for the reference. However, the synthesized catalysts were multiphase, CH 4 selectivity remained below 60% at atmospheric pressure, and selectivity predictions transferred poorly to the experimental systems. These limitations indicate that surface-sensitive descriptors and descriptors capturing the local chemical environment are required for selectivity-focused catalyst design. Therefore, the framework is supported primarily as an activity-oriented screening and property-space narrowing approach.

title: AI-accelerated discovery of a high-entropy garnet electrolyte with a flattened Li-ion energy landscape for practical solid-state batteries
abstract: The vast compositional space of high-entropy materials makes the discovery of superior solid electrolytes extremely challenging. Here, we introduce a hybrid artificial intelligence (AI) framework that synergistically combines unsupervised learning with crystal graph convolutional neural networks (CGCNN) in a dual-stage screening architecture. This approach navigates >1800 potential Zr-site doped Li7La3Zr2O12 (LLZO) compositions, first partitioning them into 21 distinct groups via unsupervised clustering, then focusing on a high-potential group (G19) for precise CGCNN prediction of band gaps and Li+ diffusion barriers. This AI-identified optimal high-entropy electrolyte, Li7La3Zr0.4Cr0.4Mo0.4Sn0.4Ta0.4O12 (HE-LLZO), would otherwise require years of trial-and-error. Entropy stabilization lowers the synthesis temperature to 920 °C and suppresses detrimental Li2CO3/LiOH surface formation. Bond valence site energy (BVSE) calculations, supported by solid-state NMR and geometric phase analysis, reveal that the high-entropy configuration introduces moderate lattice distortion (dσ = 0.104 Å) and significantly flattens the 3D Li+ migration energy landscape, reducing the macroscopic diffusion barrier from 1.060 eV (pristine LLZO) to 0.777 eV. Consequently, HE-LLZO achieves a high ionic conductivity of 1.05 × 10−3 S cm−1, a low activation energy of 0.287 eV, and an expanded electrochemical window of 4.81 V. All-solid-state cells with Ta-doped NCM811 cathodes retain 92.5% capacity after 250 cycles, and flexible pouch cells (NCM90|SE|Li-alloy) deliver 200.1 mAh g−1 with 86% retention after 200 cycles, demonstrating practical viability. This work establishes a generalizable, AI-guided paradigm for accelerating the discovery of high-entropy solid electrolyte toward high-energy-density batteries.

title: Physics-informed data-driven topology-supported precursor screening strategy for designing all-organic polyimide dielectrics with deep traps and wide-temperature-range
abstract: The development of high-power electronics demands polymer dielectrics with high thermal stability and dielectric performance. However, most materials suffer performance degradation in harsh environments due to increased electrical conductivity. Herein, a physics-informed data-driven topology-supported precursor screening strategy was proposed to design quasi-branched polyimides (QbPIs) with enhanced energy density (Ue) and charge-discharge efficiency (η) at elevated temperatures. By constructing automated screening workflow, key descriptors involving HOMO-LUMO gap (Gap) and dielectric constant (εr) were sufficiently evaluated to form multi-parameter ranking framework, in which melamine was identified as the optimal topological center for constructing QbPIs with tunable topological ratios (0–2.5%). Notably, the resulting star-shaped topological structure effectively regulates charge transport and dielectric behavior through a cooperative mechanism. It increases the Gap, introduces deep-level traps, and stabilizes the Ag/dielectric interface, which together suppress conduction loss and charge injection, effectively disrupting long-range charge-transport pathways. The optimized QbPI-1.75 exhibited outstanding capacitive performance, delivering 5.39 J cm−3 (Ue) with 94% (η) at 25 °C, and retaining 3.29 J cm−3 with 78.41% at 200 °C, far exceeding that of pure PI (1.35 J cm−3, 87.6% η at 25 °C). This work establishes a fundamental structure-property relationship for topological PIs and provides a facile design strategy applicable to other high-temperature polymer dielectrics.

title: Explainable reinforcement learning designs a LRP1-targeted BBB-penetrating peptide with spatial selectivity for glioblastoma therapy
abstract: Efficient drug delivery across the blood-brain barrier (BBB) remains a formidable challenge. While peptide-mediated transcytosis is promising, the rational de novo design of BBB-penetrating peptides lacks systematic principles. Here, we developed a novel multi-receptor, explainable, and uncertainty-aware reinforcement learning framework that integrates multi-task affinity prediction with physicochemical constraints for the de novo design of BBB-penetrating peptides. By integrating multivalent transcytosis datasets and physicochemical constraints, our model generates highly feasible, BBB-permeable candidates. Experimental validation of a representative generated peptide, 1 L, demonstrated that it drives robust nanoparticle transcytosis without compromising vascular integrity. Mechanistically, 1 L specifically targets the LRP1 receptor, orchestrating active endothelial endocytosis and vesicular trafficking. In vivo, 1 L-conjugated nanoparticles achieved profound brain parenchymal accumulation with a unique spatial selectivity—enriching in the cortex and striatum while bypassing limbic septal nuclei, thereby offering a potential “spatial selectivity pattern”, outperforming several established LRP1-targeted systems in brain parenchymal delivery. Systemic administration of 1 L-nanotherapeutics significantly suppressed tumor progression and prolonged survival in an orthotopic glioblastoma model without systemic toxicity. This AI-driven paradigm provides a powerful, generalizable strategy for designing precision neurotherapeutics.

title: Integrating machine learning and CFD-derived hydrodynamics for predictive scale-up of combined cooling and antisolvent crystallization
abstract: Scale-up of crystallization processes remains a major challenge due to the complex interplay between operating conditions, hydrodynamics, and particle-level phenomena. This study presents an interpretable machine learning framework for predicting product particle size distributions (PSD) in a combined cooling and antisolvent crystallization process across laboratory and pilot scales. Partial least squares (PLS) regression models with bootstrapping-based uncertainty quantification were constructed using three categories of input variables: (i) operating conditions alone, (ii) operating conditions with empirical hydrodynamic descriptors, and (iii) operating conditions with both empirical and CFD-derived hydrodynamic descriptors. At small scales (400 mL, 500 mL, and 3 L), both (ii) and (iii) improved predictive accuracy relative to (i), with consistent performance across train–test splits. For extrapolation to mid-scale (5 L) and large-scale (100 L) crystallizers, only models including CFD-derived hydrodynamic features provided accurate predictions, demonstrating their critical role in scale-up. The variable importance scores of the PLS models revealed the key operational and hydrodynamic factors that influence PSD predictions across scales. The proposed framework offers a generalizable digital design tool aiding scale-up of crystallization processes, integrating mechanistic hydrodynamic insights with machine learning to enable predictive, data-efficient, and interpretable scale-up.

title: Electron beam and protease–induced modifications of ECM protein hydrogels: Collagen- and elastin-specific structural insights via fast green staining and fluorescence lifetime CLSM
abstract: Collagen–elastin hydrogels have gained increasing attention as versatile extracellular matrix-based biomaterials for tissue engineering, drug delivery, and regenerative medicine. Their tunable mechanical properties, inherent biocompatibility, and responsiveness to external cues make them ideal yet complex systems for biomedical applications. Recent studies have demonstrated that high-energy electron beam irradiation offers a reagent-free approach for crosslinking collagen-elastin hydrogels, enabling precise modulation of network density, mechanical behavior, and thermo-responsiveness under sterilizing conditions. To better understand and visualize the effects of electron beam treatment and enzymatic degradation on the microarchitecture of these hybrid materials we employed fluorescence lifetime-based confocal laser scanning microscopy combined with Fast Green staining. This technique enabled the simultaneous differentiation of collagen and elastin subnetworks at the fibrillar level and facilitated the investigation of the behavior of individual protein components during radiation-chemical processing, enzymatic degradation, and combinations thereof. Electron beam treated and untreated gels were exposed to selective enzymatic degradation using trypsin and elastase, providing insights into the proteolytic stability of the individual matrix components. Lifetime based imaging revealed significant differences in collagen and elastin susceptibility to enzymatic cleavage following electron beam treatment. To support the analysis, machine learning-based segmentation was applied, with a primary focus on voxel-wise classification using the 3D pixel classifier in AIVIA, allowing for a volumetric and spatially resolved characterization of the datasets. The findings highlight the potential of fluorescence lifetime-based confocal laser scanning microscopy and machine learning-based image analysis for characterization of extracellular matrix-mimetic biomaterials and their dynamic remodeling behavior, with implications for optimizing scaffold design in bioengineering applications.

title: Molecular engineering of CRISPR biosensors: From rational design to AI acceleration
abstract: The CRISPR/Cas system integrates programmable target recognition with diverse catalytic activities and versatile signal transduction mechanisms, rendering it a powerful platform for molecular detection. The performance of CRISPR/Cas-based sensors is largely determined by the properties of their core molecular components, including guide RNAs (gRNAs), Cas proteins, and signal output elements. Therefore, molecular engineering of these components represents a critical strategy for enhancing target recognition, catalytic efficiency, detection sensitivity, specificity, and overall signal fidelity. Such engineering primarily relies on rational design to regulate sensing performance, including (i) gRNA sequence and structure optimization; (ii) Cas protein engineering via site-specific mutations or functional domain fusions; and (iii) modification of signal probes. These strategies collectively enable the rational design of CRISPR/Cas sensors with tailored performance for diverse applications. With the advancement of artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning and deep learning have expanded the capabilities for designing and analyzing CRISPR/Cas components. Protein language models and computer vision further support the prediction of gRNA activity and off-target effects, the discovery and functional optimization of Cas proteins, and the intelligent analysis of detection signals. These approaches enable more efficient and accurate CRISPR/Cas system development. This paper systematically reviews molecular engineering strategies for CRISPR/Cas sensing elements at three levels: gRNAs, Cas proteins, and signal output. We discuss how rational and AI-assisted approaches leverage sequence, structural, molecular interaction, and experimental data to optimize sensing performance. AI-assisted methods are further highlighted for their potential to reduce screening costs, narrow the design space, and improve engineering efficiency. In closing, we highlight the key challenges and outline future perspectives for realizing CRISPR sensing platforms that combine high sensitivity, specificity, robustness, and broad adaptability.

title: Machine learning assisted identification of MOF-derived ZnO/In dual gas sensor activated by blue light at near room temperature
abstract: Efficient discrimination of multiple volatile organic compounds using a single metal-oxide semiconductor sensor at near room temperature remains challenging. Herein, MOF-derived In-doped ZnO engineered with abundant defects and porous structure exhibits superior dual-gas sensing performance under blue-light activation at near room temperature, making it particularly well-suited for machine-learning-driven gas identification. Among the In-doped samples, comprehensive SEM, TEM, and BET analyses, together with XPS, PL, EPR, EIS, and transient photocurrent measurements, demonstrated that ZnO/In-0.1 achieved the optimal balance among surface area, oxygen vacancy (Ov), and photogenerated carrier transfer. Under 450 nm irradiation at approximately 60 °C, it delivered Δresponses of 527 and 509 to 10 ppm triethylamine (TEA) and N-butanol, respectively, with response times of 57 and 80 s and theoretical detection limits of 6.72 and 5.53 ppb, while exhibiting negligible responses in the dark. RandomForest achieved 97.8% held-out classification accuracy for gas-composition classes, while XGBoost predicted the concentrations of both gases with an overall R2 of 0.956. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations showed that In incorporation lowered the Ov formation energy, introduced defect and band-tail states, and strengthened the adsorption of TEA (−1.8253 eV) and N-butanol (−1.1814 eV). The enhanced sensing performance arises from composition-structure-function coupling among optimized In loading, defect-rich porous structure, sub-bandgap carrier activation, and preferential target-gas adsorption, providing a strategy for intelligent visible light activated dual-gas sensing.

title: Interfacial polarity regulation enables robust self-healing conductive elastomers for wearable motion recognition
abstract: Flexible strain sensors must withstand repeated deformation while preserving mechanical integrity, autonomous repairability, and stable signal transduction. Conductive polymer composites, however, often suffer from filler aggregation and fragile conductive networks, making it difficult to reconcile strength, self-healing capability, and sensing reliability. Here, we report an interfacial polarity regulation strategy to construct a self-healing conductive elastomer composed of furan-functionalized carbon nanotubes and Diels–Alder-crosslinked epoxidized natural rubber (ECNT). Molecular simulations, together with spectroscopic and morphological analyses, reveal that the furan-regulated interface generates localized polar domains and accessible interaction sites, thereby promoting nanotube dispersion and interfacial coupling within the elastomer matrix. The optimized ECNT-2 composite achieves a tensile strength of 7.74 MPa, an elongation at break of 467%, and a self-healing efficiency above 90% after thermal treatment. Enabled by dynamic conductive-network reconstruction and reversible covalent crosslinking, the elastomer sensor delivers a gauge factor of 3.76, response/recovery times below 180/140 ms, and stable piezoresistive signals under cyclic deformation. It reliably monitors large joint motions and subtle physiological activities, including finger bending, elbow flexion, coughing, and smiling. Coupled with a one-dimensional convolutional neural network, the sensor achieves window-level validation accuracies of 100% for representative motions and 98.7% for finger gestures, supporting robotic-hand teleoperation. This work links molecular-level polarity engineering with intelligent wearable sensing, offering a rational route to robust self-healing conductive elastomers for adaptive human-machine interfaces.

title: The cathode–electrolyte interphase meets artificial intelligence: From formation and evolution mechanisms to data-driven interphase design
abstract: The commercialization of high-energy, high-voltage lithium-ion and next-generation batteries hinges on how precisely the cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI) can be understood and controlled. Far from being a static boundary, the CEI is a dynamic, compositionally heterogeneous reaction zone in which oxidative decomposition products of the electrolyte accumulate, rearrange, and continuously evolve with cycling. This review (i) establishes the fundamentals of CEI formation, structure, and growth kinetics; (ii) surveys interphase behavior across cathode families—Ni-rich NCM/NMC, high-voltage spinels, Li-rich oxides, sodium/zinc/dual-ion systems, and solid-state cells; (iii) organizes stabilization strategies spanning electrolyte additives, solvation engineering, surface coating and doping, artificial CEIs, and dry-electrode processing; and (iv) compares advanced characterization tools including cryo-EM, in situ TEM, XPS/ToF-SIMS, and EIS/DRT. The review also examines AI and machine-learning approaches relevant to CEI research, including machine-learning interatomic potentials, physics-informed learning, electrolyte and additive screening, multiscale imaging and computational analysis, and battery-level diagnostics. We close by presenting an integrated experiment–simulation–AI framework for data-driven interphase analysis and design.

title: Machine learning strategies integrating knowledge transfer and a cascaded framework: Guiding the discovery of NIR-II organic cocrystals
abstract: Organic cocrystals represent a highly promising class of photothermal materials operating in the near-infrared second (NIR-II) window. However, efficient identification and rational design remain challenging due to the vast chemical space and the complex, nontrivial relationships between molecular structures and functional properties. In this work, we develop a cascaded dual-task (C2T) machine learning (ML) framework that effectively links cocrystal-formability recognition (M1) with NIR-II absorption identification (M2) through feature knowledge transfer. We constructed the first hierarchical organic cocrystal database, comprising 2,648 cocrystal samples and 128 NIR-II cocrystals. By integrating RDKit and PaDEL descriptors to generate dual-representation molecular features, a dual-task prediction model is established. Under small-sample conditions, both M1 and M2 achieve high predictive accuracies (>92%) and demonstrate strong generalization capabilities. Guided by the model, we discover and experimentally validate the DPQ cocrystals, which exhibits intense NIR-II absorption (up to 1200 nm) and efficient photothermal behavior (~120℃@1024 nm). Moreover, multiscale theoretical calculations combined with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based model interpretability elucidate the structure-property relationships from molecular architecture to macroscopic performance. This work demonstrates the potential of ML for precise cocrystal design and efficient performance identification under small-sample conditions, paving the way for ML-accelerated development of functional molecular materials.

title: Vacancy–metal–site coupling in defective MgO-supported single-atom catalysts for CO2-to-CO reduction: DFT screening assisted by multimodal transfer learning
abstract: Defective oxide supports provide reactive vacancy sites for CO2 activation, but strong initial activation alone does not guarantee favorable CO2-to-CO thermodynamics because downstream intermediate stabilization must also be optimized. Here, vacancy–metal–site (VMS) coupling in defective MgO-supported single-atom catalysts is systematically investigated by integrating density functional theory (DFT), descriptor-guided screening, multimodal transfer learning, and computational hydrogen electrode (CHE) analysis. The target-domain MgO-Ov-TM space, where Ov denotes a surface oxygen vacancy and TM denotes a transition-metal single atom, contains 120 configurations constructed from 20 3d/4d transition-metal dopants and six representative adsorption environments. DFT calculations reveal that oxygen vacancies promote CO2 bending and charge redistribution, whereas favorable CO2-to-CO thermodynamics require coordinated regulation of *COOH formation and *CO stabilization by metal identity and local adsorption environments. To enrich promising candidates, a Vacancy–Metal–Site Multimodal Transfer Learning (VMS-MTL) framework was adapted from graph–text transfer-learning strategies by integrating geometry-aware graph embeddings pretrained on the Open Catalyst 2020 (OC20) dataset with structured chemical-text representations. VMS-MTL achieved mean absolute errors (MAEs) of 0.219 eV for Eads of CO and 0.363 eV for |d-band center|, recovering eight of nine DFT-screened candidates within the top-15 out-of-fold (OOF) rankings. Subsequent CHE analysis identified Sc-T-Mg_Def, corresponding to a Sc atom coupled with the defect-neighboring Mg top site, as the most thermodynamically favorable configuration within the investigated MgO-Ov-TM space, with a limiting free-energy change (ΔGmax) of 0.316 eV. Further analysis shows that strong initial CO2 activation is not directly correlated with thermodynamic favorability, revealing a system-specific Sabatier-type trade-off. These findings establish VMS coupling as a framework linking vacancy-assisted activation with metal/site-regulated intermediate stabilization, while multimodal transfer learning enables data-efficient candidate enrichment before detailed DFT/CHE analysis.

title: Machine learning-guided design of glycosaminoglycans composite fiber scaffolds for neuro-osteogenic regeneration
abstract: Repairing large bone defects caused by trauma or disease poses a significant clinical challenge. Glycosaminoglycans (GAGs), major components of organic matrix, play a crucial role in osteogenesis. Here, we report a machine learning (ML)-guided strategy for enhancing the design of osteogenic multicomponent GAGs. First, we constructed a dataset of 169/173 data for cell differentiation and viability of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) cultured on different GAGs formulations to build an optimal formulation screening model through random forest (RF) and XGBoost (XGB) algorithms. We efficiently screened 59 good GAGs from 10,000 formulations generated in the whole space that own maximized cell differentiation and viability through the model. Based on cell mineralization activity, secondary screening identified 3 optimal formulations (GAG3–5). Based on these formulations, optimal formulation GAGs adsorbed into magnesium doped amino modified mesoporous bioactive glass (MBG) as the core, nerve growth factor (NGF) adsorbed into silk fibroin (SF) as the shell to form a composite fiber MBG/GAG@SF/NGF scaffold through coaxial electrospinning. Interestingly, we observed that MBG/GAG3,5@SF/NGF scaffolds promoted the osteogenesis process by activating the Bone morphogenetic protein 2 (Bmp2)/Smad and p-Erk1/2 signaling pathways in vitro . Furthermore, we found that MBG/GAG3,5@SF/NGF scaffolds enhanced the neurogenesis process in vitro . Intriguingly, we also observed that MBG/GAG5@SF/NGF scaffold effectively guided functional bone regeneration accompanied with enhanced neurogenesis and angiogenesis in mouse cranial defect model in vivo . This study not only provides an efficient MBG/GAG5@SF/NGF composite fiber multifunctional scaffold for bone defect repair but also establishes a scalable paradigm for ML-guided screening of bioactive formulations.

title: AI-accelerated hybrid reactive-nonreactive molecular dynamics simulation for polymer cross-linking
abstract: Molecular dynamics simulation based on reactive forcefield enables atomic-scale investigation of polymer cross-linking processes but is limited by high computational cost. In polymer cross-linking simulations, a large fraction of simulation time is spent in chemically inactive stages, during which the continuous use of a reactive forcefield is inefficient. In this work, an artificial intelligence-accelerated hybrid reactive-nonreactive molecular dynamics framework is developed, which adaptively switches between reactive and non-reactive forcefields to improve computational efficiency while maintaining chemical accuracy. A machine learning model is trained on reactive molecular dynamics trajectories to predict continuous reaction probability using physically interpretable structural, chemical, and energetic descriptors extracted from simulation outputs. This probabilistic criterion enables reliable identification of low-reactivity states and stable forcefield switching without manually defined heuristic rules. The proposed approach is applied to the cross-linking process of epoxy as a representative example. Compared with full reactive forcefield simulations, the hybrid approach achieves up to 80% reduction in computational cost. Structural and mechanical properties of the cross-linked epoxy network obtained from the hybrid simulations show excellent agreement with full reactive forcefield results and experimental reference data. This work provides a framework that accelerates polymer cross-linking simulations while preserving key reaction chemistry, network evolution, and final material properties. Using epoxy-amine cross-linking as a representative case, the study establishes a proof-of-concept strategy for coupling chemically faithful reactive sampling with efficient nonreactive relaxation. The framework may be extended to other reaction-relaxation systems after system-specific descriptor construction, threshold calibration, and independent validation.

title: AI-assisted molecular and materials discovery in chemistry and chemical engineering: A methodological and bibliometric review
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is advancing molecular and materials discovery by linking chemical data with predictive modeling, inverse design, reaction planning, experimental optimization, and increasingly integrated laboratory workflows. This review critically examines AI-assisted molecular and materials discovery from methodological, bibliometric, application-oriented, and chemical engineering perspectives. We first outline the core workflow for reliable chemical machine learning, covering data acquisition and curation, chemical representation, model construction, and evaluation, with particular attention to data regimes, generalization, uncertainty, applicability domains, interpretability, and experimental validation. A bibliometric analysis of Web of Science Core Collection records retrieved from 1 January 2016 to 10 April 2026, with 2026 treated as partial-year coverage, contextualizes the evolution and interconnection of major research themes. Four application directions are examined: property prediction and virtual screening; reaction planning, reaction engineering, and process optimization; generative inverse design; and large language model (LLM)-enabled multimodal and increasingly automated workflows. Across these directions, we compare method suitability and validation strength and distinguish computational prediction and generation from prospective experimental validation, closed-loop optimization, and autonomous experimentation. Translation to chemical engineering practice is evaluated in terms of reactor and operating constraints, transport phenomena, scale-up, process control, process safety, and techno-economic feasibility. Finally, challenges are organized into four categories: data, representation, model, and deployment, with emphasis on representative datasets, chemically and physically constrained representations, realistic validation, uncertainty-aware decisions, and tighter integration of computation, experiment, and process engineering.

title: Physics-informed neural network reconstructions of free surfaces and flow fields from sparse data in turbulent regimes, with applications in stirred tanks
abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are a promising meshless framework for fluid dynamics, capable of solving both forward and inverse problems, and incorporating observational data into the model. However, their application to coupled multiphase turbulent flows remains limited, particularly in industrial inverse problems, where measurements may be sparse, expensive, and are often devoid of turbulence values. In this work, we develop a PINN framework for reconstructing the free surface, along with the velocity and pressure fields from sparse data, and test it on a mixing tank. Models are trained on limited velocity and pressure data from a time-averaged, axisymmetric CFD reference simulation. The data are free of direct measurements from the free surface or turbulence terms. Models are evaluated across varying impeller speeds and fluid viscosities. Both laminar and turbulent models are tested, including with eddy viscosity closures and anisotropic stresses. A Spalart–Allmaras turbulence closure is used, while including anisotropic stresses can improve the pressure and free surface predictions. From as few as 25 measurement locations, models are able to reconstruct, with low error, the velocity and pressure fields, and the final model achieves average free-surface errors below 1 mm in all tested operating conditions relative to a CFD reference. Additionally, models can accurately detect features such as additional vortices, jet splitting and impingement regions.

title: Physics-informed LSTM for lignocellulosic pyrolysis kinetics at elevated heating rates: Integrating Arrhenius constraints with data-driven modeling
abstract: Reliable prediction of lignocellulosic intermediate pyrolysis kinetics is critical for scaling up thermochemical conversion processes, yet remains challenging at high heating rates. We developed a physics-informed long short-term memory network (PINN-LSTM) integrating particle swarm optimization (PSO) with recurrent neural networks, trained on only 13 thermogravimetric/derivative thermogravimetric (TG/DTG) curves from pure components, blends, and real straws. PSO inversely determines apparent phenomenological kinetic triplets (E, A, n), embedded as Arrhenius-based soft constraints in the LSTM loss function, enforcing physical feasibility without compromising flexibility. On the three held-out straws PINN-LSTM attains RMSE values of 0.80, 0.78 and 0.80 wt%·min−1, corresponding to a 43% reduction in mean RMSE relative to the vanilla LSTM and approximately 76% relative to HRF, the strongest tree ensemble; each comparison is stated against a single named baseline rather than as a combined range. The model accurately captures shoulder-peak transitions and high-temperature tails, with peak-temperature errors below 1 K. The E-lnA relationship observed is that expected under single-heating-rate inversion and is reported as an apparent, jointly determined descriptor rather than as an independently established physical law. A web-based interface enables real-time parameter estimation (E=228 kJ·mol−1, lnA=42.1 s−1, n=2.31) with automated visualization, facilitating industrial adoption. This synergy between data-driven learning and physics-based constraints demonstrates broader applicability to thermochemical systems with mechanistic priors and data scarcity.

title: AI-assisted design of metal-organic frameworks for hydrogen storage: From databases to generative models
abstract: Nowadays, the development of a sustainable hydrogen economy and the widespread deployment of high-capacity hydrogen storage for hydrogen vehicles and energy systems are of great importance. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), with their diverse structures, have emerged as the most promising materials for next-generation gas storage due to their high surface area, tunable pore size, and diversity of chemical bonds. However, the fabrication of MOF materials through manual experimental screening is very time-consuming and costly. Recently, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) algorithms, combined with quantum databases, advanced modeling, and screening strategies for discovering MOF structures, have revolutionized materials science. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in AI-assisted discovery of novel MOF materials specifically for hydrogen storage applications. We present MOF databases, modeling strategies based on material structure descriptors and materials discovery, large language model (LLM) algorithms for automated data mining, and ML-assisted force fields (FFs) at the atomic level for hydrogen storage. Furthermore, we discuss key challenges such as data quality, model transferability, and discrepancies between simulations and experiments. Finally, this review paper outlines future prospects for this rapidly evolving interdisciplinary field, with an emphasis on advancing MOF materials discovery through accurate AI models.

title: Artificial intelligence-driven glycosaminoglycan-mimetic polymer design for cartilage regeneration
abstract: Clinical cartilage repair remains limited by fibrocartilage formation rather than hyaline-like cartilage repair after microfracture. Engineering an instructive extracellular matrix (ECM)-mimetic microenvironment is therefore essential for directing the fate of endogenous bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). Here, we introduced a data-driven strategy integrating literature-derived machine learning with native cartilage matrix analysis to guide scaffold design for cartilage regeneration. Guided by this framework, a chondrocyte-mimetic polymer scaffold (HRC) was constructed using recombinant human type II collagen (rhCol II), type I collagen (Col I), and thiolated hyaluronic acid (HA-SH). Within the scaffold, Col I self-assembled into a strong fibrous framework that provided structural support, while rhCol II participated in the intermolecular organization of the composite matrix. In vitro, HRC enhanced BMSC migration and chondrogenic differentiation. Furthermore, HRC promoted regeneration of a smooth articular surface with an ordered matrix architecture and abundant proteoglycan deposition in cartilage defect models. RNA sequencing revealed enrichment of PI3K–Akt-related signaling, while PI3K inhibition supported its involvement in the in vitro chondrogenic response. Taken together, these findings support the relevance of tissue-specific matrix design for cartilage repair. Overall, the machine learning (ML) strategy used in this study can extend to other tissues constituting with collagen such as the meniscus.

title: Deciphering the water-thermal stability trade-offs via interpretable machine learning for reliable design of dual-stable MOFs
abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) hold immense promise for industrial adsorption and catalysis. However, practical deployment is often hindered by insufficient simultaneous water and thermal stability under harsh hygrothermal conditions. Furthermore, the mechanistic differences and potential trade-offs underlying water and thermal stability remain largely unexplored. Here, we establish an interpretable machine-learning framework integrating molecular descriptors and synthetic parameters to decode the mechanisms governing dual stability. Subsequent feature attribution analyses quantitatively reveal the asymmetric regulation underlying dual-stability. Thermal stability is synergistically determined by multidimensional parameters, including nuclearity and synthesis conditions. In contrast, the water-stability model shows a pronounced association with elemental electronegativity, with additional variation associated with structural descriptors within the sampled chemical space. Notably, increasing certain features (e.g., ligand-to-metal ratio > 1, topological polar surface area (TPSA) > 150 Å) enhances water stability at the expense of thermal stability, exposing pronounced trade-offs. Guided by these insights, we delineate a quantitative design space for dual-stability (e.g., metal electronegativity < 1.8, TPSA < 150 Å, 0.3 < ligand-to-metal ratio < 1.1). Targeted synthesis and characterization of representative MOFs confirm that materials within these parameters reliably achieve superior stability. These findings establish quantitative design rules for overcoming stability trade-offs and enabling the rational engineering of robust MOFs, accelerating industrial application under complex hygrothermal conditions.

title: Ultrasound-enhanced goethite coprecipitation for synergistic enrichment of Ga, Ge and In: A combined molecular dynamics, artificial neural network and EXAFS study
abstract: Amid the global energy transition, digital infrastructure upgrading, and rapid growth of high-end manufacturing, the efficient recovery and high-value utilization of critical metals (Ga, Ge and In) have become important research priorities in resource recycling and strategic mineral security. To address the challenges of the dispersed distribution of Ga, Ge and In in zinc sulfate solution, and the low efficiency of their co-recovery. This study investigated the ultrasonic-enhanced goethite co-precipitation method for simultaneously pre-enriching Ga, Ge and In from a simulated acidic zinc sulfate solution. Based on these findings, an ANN-GA optimization model was developed to achieve precise optimization of multi-parameter coupling. The results indicated that ultrasonic enhancement can significantly improve the goethite formation process and the solid-liquid distribution behavior of Ga, Ge and In, enabling the efficient synergistic enrichment of three rare metals under optimized conditions (ωFe = 99.91%, ωGa = 99.81%, ωGe = 99.71%, ωIn = 99.70%). To elucidate ultrasound effects, conventional characterization techniques were combined with mineral liberation analysis (MLA), atomic force microscopy (AFM), and extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS). The results show ultrasonic cavitation enhances mass transfer, oxidation, and hydrolysis, while modifying microstructure, crystal defects, and interfacial properties of the goethite coprecipitation residue. Ultrasonic treatment produces a more porous and defect-rich goethite coprecipitation residue with increased surface accessibility, thereby promoting the enrichment of Ga, Ge, and In. Molecular dynamics simulations (MD) further indicated element dependent spatial distributions of Ge(OH)4, Ga3+, and In3+ near the goethite/water interface. Overall, ultrasound enhanced goethite co-precipitation provided an effective process for the simultaneous pre-enrichment of Ga, Ge, and In from zinc sulfate solutions and provided a scientific basis for their subsequent selective separation and recovery.

title: Unveiling the atomic scale synthesis dynamics of lithium thiophosphate electrolytes via machine learning interatomic potentials
abstract: The rational design of inorganic materials is often hindered by the complexity of solid-state synthesis, which remains largely empirical and reliant on trial-and-error optimization. Bridging the gap between atomistic mechanisms and macroscopic processing, we present a fully reactive computational synthesis framework capable of predicting phase evolution directly from precursor materials. By leveraging machine learning molecular dynamics (MLMD) driven by the Crystal Hamiltonian Graph Neural Network (CHGNet) potential, we successfully reproduced the experimental synthesis trajectories of the Li2S-P2S5 solid electrolyte system. Our simulations captured the composition-dependent formation of local structural environments characteristic of Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and Li7PS6 phases from 70, 75, and 87.5 mol% Li2S precursors, respectively. Detailed structural analyses revealed the systematic cleavage of bridging sulfur bonds and the dominance of terminal PS43− tetrahedra with increasing Li content, closely mirroring experimental thiophosphate speciation. Although limited simulation timescales restricted full crystallization, the resulting structures exhibited high fidelity to experimentally reported glassy intermediates, as confirmed by structure factor calculations and SOAP-based similarity analysis. This work demonstrates the feasibility of a “virtual reactor” for exploring synthesis pathways, offering a safe and efficient strategy to accelerate the discovery of complex solid-state materials.

title: NanoChef: AI framework for simultaneous optimization of synthesis sequences and reaction conditions at autonomous laboratories
abstract: We present NanoChef , a deep learning-based framework for the simultaneous optimization of synthesis sequences and reaction conditions in autonomous laboratories. Unlike traditional AI models focused solely on continuous variables, NanoChef incorporates positional encoding and MatBERT embedding to represent reagent sequences as vectorized inputs, enabling joint modeling of sequential and continuous variables in nanoparticle (NP) synthesis. In virtual experiments, NanoChef consistently searched for the best-identified optimum across synthesis-order-sensitive landscapes in under 40 cycles. Despite the complexity of 17.5 billion candidate recipes driven by 24 possible sequences in a four-reagent system, this framework achieved an optimal recipe for Ag NP synthesis, characterized by a λ max of 513 nm and a 36% reduction in full width at half maximum within fewer than 350 experiments. This search efficiency was underscored by the reductant-last strategy, which consistently yielded optimal results across all permutations of two- to four-reagent systems. Additionally, NanoChef newly discovered an oxidant–last strategy that produces monodisperse NPs on average. By optimizing both continuous volume and the order of reagent addition, the framework redefines synthesis order as a tunable design variable and demonstrates how AI can accelerate autonomous chemistry while handling high-dimensional combinatorial challenges that exceed the capabilities of fixed-order methods.

title: Role of artificial intelligence and machine learning techniques in pyrolytic liquefaction of biomass and waste polymers: From mechanistic insights to process automation
