abstract: Continuous disposal of various organic wastes and polymers causes environmental and economic drawbacks. Pyrolysis converts scrap tyres, waste plastics, and biomass into bio-oil, syngas, and char, via co-processing. However, optimizing yield and quality across these heterogeneous feedstocks demands models that can navigate highly nonlinear, scale-dependent thermochemistry. This review uniquely couples artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) for all three waste streams in a single mechanistic and automation-oriented framework. The present review documents the reaction kinetics of tires, plastics and biomass and maps these pathways directly to input features and explainable AI techniques. A comparative synthesis of reported R2, RMSE, and MAE data across various feedstocks in literature show that gradient-boosted tree ensembles (XGBoost, LightGBM) outperform deep neural architectures on small pyrolysis datasets. For instance, a deep mixture of experts model collapsed under 10-fold cross validation on a 468-record dataset, underscoring that model complexity without adequate data is counterproductive. The challenges with AI/ML applications in pyrolysis are briefly outlined and mapped with possible recommendations. In addition, an autonomous robotic development platform was framed as a future scope of the present review.

title: Towards generalizable wet foamability predictions: A dimensional analysis approach incorporating dynamic surface tension and symbolic regression
abstract: This study presents a groundbreaking chemical engineering approach to modeling wet foam formation through mechanical mixing and gas-sparging processes. Situated at the intersection of physico-chemistry, dimensional analysis, chemical engineering, and predictive modeling, this work utilizes an extensive experimental dataset covering a broad spectrum of operating conditions.For each foaming process examined, a single dimensionless correlation – capable of accurately predicting foam heights – is derived, irrespective of surfactant type, provided that dynamic surface tension is explicitly accounted for. The findings emphasize the pivotal role of surfactant dynamics in macroscopic foaming behavior, demonstrating that the time-dependent evolution of surface tension must be incorporated into foaming process models. This study serves as a compelling example of how chemical engineering principles can bridge molecular-scale mechanisms (e.g., surfactant migration at bubble interfaces) with macroscopic physical variables (e.g., foam height) observed at the process scale.Beyond its immediate relevance to the foaming community, this work highlights the feasibility of integrating non-constant properties into dimensional analysis frameworks – a practice rarely applied in the chemical engineering field – while adhering to rigorous similarity theory principles. Most importantly, the study underscores a broader message for chemical engineers: modern semi-empirical correlations can achieve unprecedented robustness by synergistically combining dimensional analysis (retaining physical interpretability and scalability, unlike purely data-driven approaches) with AI-driven techniques.

title: Machine learning-integrated wearable sensors for intelligent disease diagnosis and personalized healthcare
abstract: Wearable sensors have emerged as a technology for advancing healthcare through non-invasive, continuous, and real-time monitoring of physiological signals. Despite progress, healthcare systems face challenges in prevention, screening, diagnosis, and management due to reliance on invasive procedures, intermittent measurements, bulky equipment, and interventions. Although wearable sensors can generate data and improve accessibility, their ability to provide clinical insights remains limited. Meanwhile, the complexity of wearable health data places demands on clinical interpretation. Machine learning (ML) offers an approach to uncover patterns from datasets and establish relationships between physiological signals and health outcomes. However, the integration of wearable sensors and ML into practice remains constrained by challenges of data quality, model robustness, interpretability, privacy, and regulatory compliance. In this review, we examine recent advances in wearable sensor-ML systems for healthcare applications. We first introduce the operating principles and classifications of wearable sensors alongside the concepts and methodologies of ML. Then we survey the application of wearable sensor-ML technologies across a wide range of diseases, highlighting representative studies and comparing the performance, advantages, and limitations of ML approaches in wearable healthcare scenarios. Furthermore, we discuss the technical, clinical, and ethical barriers to real-world implementation and summarize strategies to overcome these limitations. By integrating developments with an assessment of challenges, this review underscores the potential of wearable sensor-ML systems for enabling more accurate, continuous, and personalized healthcare. The perspectives provide a roadmap for future research and translation, accelerating the development of intelligent healthcare technologies and advancing the realization of predictive, preventive, personalized, and participatory (4P) medicine.

title: From molecular discovery to system management: A mini-review on machine learning driving full-cycle optimization of aqueous flow batteries
abstract: With the growing global demand for long-duration energy storage technologies, redox flow batteries (RFBs) have become a major research hotspot owing to their decoupled power and capacity and high safety. Nevertheless, challenges including slow screening of active materials, complex multi-physics field coupling and insufficient accuracy of system state monitoring hinder their large-scale commercialization. For aqueous systems in particular, inherent challenges throughout the entire lifecycle of research, development and operation remain, such as coupled pH-potential effects, solubility-potential trade-offs, aqueous solvation effects, as well as hydrolysis and polymerization side reactions. As an emerging data-driven technology, machine learning (ML) features powerful nonlinear fitting and cross-scale modeling capabilities, which are transforming the research paradigm of aqueous flow batteries at an unprecedented rate. This paper systematically reviews the state-of-the-art applications of machine learning across the full lifecycle of flow batteries. First, it summarizes data-driven strategies for property prediction and high-throughput screening of electrolyte molecules in terms of material design. Second, hardware optimization covers membrane design, electrode optimization, and flow-field simulation and topology optimization. Third, the applications of machine learning in state of charge and state of health estimation during system operation are elaborated. Furthermore, the great potential of machine learning in mapping and regulating the full-cycle operation of aqueous flow batteries is demonstrated in the development of surrogate models and digital twins. Finally, this paper concludes the overall research advances and highlights the key challenges facing the future development of intelligent research and innovation systems for aqueous flow batteries.

title: From molecular generation to process-relevant performance: AI-driven identification of novel working fluids
abstract: The search for working fluids that balance thermodynamic performance, safety, and environmental sustainability remains a pressing challenge for refrigeration and heat pump technologies. Here, we present a hybrid computational workflow combining deep generative learning with classical thermodynamic modelling to identify novel working fluid candidates. Using a graph-based diffusion model, we generate and screen molecules against a quantitative physicochemical profile derived from known working fluids. We characterise five selected candidates in depth through molecular dynamics simulations, the polar soft-SAFT equation of state, COSMO-RS calculations, and two neural network predictors for flammability and GWP. We find that the predicted thermophysical and transport properties of the candidates fall within the range of established hydrofluorocarbons. Benchmarking against R-245fa and R-134a identifies a new compound (3,3,3-trifluoro-2-methylpropene) as the most promising candidate for high-temperature heat pump applications, and confirms another (1,1,1,2,2-pentafluoropropane) as a viable refrigerant for vapour compression cycles. Our work establishes a scalable framework for the rational, data-driven discovery of next-generation working fluids.

title: Combining physics-informed machine learning and heterogeneous transfer learning for hydrodenitrogenation of co-processed feedstocks
abstract: Accurately predicting the nitrogen content of co-processed petroleum feedstocks after hydrotreatment is a common challenge in refining, exacerbated by the limited experimental data available for each new feedstock. Transfer learning addresses this scarcity by leveraging knowledge from a related, data-rich source. For the source, the hydrodenitrogenation (HDN) of fossil vacuum gas oil, a rich dataset and an accurate prior ordinary differential equation (ODE) are available; for the target, the HDN of co-processed vacuum gas oil and tire-pyrolysis oil, the ODE structure is unknown and an additional descriptor (the tire fraction) is present, making the problem heterogeneous. To recover this unknown ODE, we propose HTL-HyODE, a heterogeneous transfer learning hybrid ODE in which small neural networks encode its unknown components while the rest is kept explicit and transferred from the source. For comparison, we also develop physics-informed variants (HTL-PINNs) of data-driven heterogeneous transfer networks. On simulated data, HTL-HyODE reduces the test mean absolute error (MAE) by up to 52% relative to a no-transfer hybrid baseline at a training size of n t = 25 when the networks are correctly placed. On experimental data, the benefit with respect to the no-transfer hybrid baseline depends on the target size and on the retained structure: at n t = 15 the best-matched structure reduces the MAE by about 50%–57%, whereas at n t = 50 the data-driven and physics-informed networks overtake it, DHTLFT-PINNs reaching the lowest error. Embedding the kinetic structure explicitly is thus most effective when it is reliable and data are scarce, while network-based transfer becomes preferable as data accumulate; the learned hybrid components remain physically consistent in both regimes.

title: Engineering precision antimicrobials: AI-driven design of self-assembling non-natural peptide nanostructures
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has evolved from a clinical challenge into a system-level engineering problem that demands therapeutic platforms capable of retaining efficacy in protease-rich, heterogeneous, and dynamically evolving infection microenvironments. Conventional antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are limited by inadequate proteolytic stability and insufficient selectivity, while isolated advances in AI-driven sequence design, non-natural peptide chemistry, and supramolecular self-assembly have yet to be integrated into a coherent engineering framework. This review presents an integrative perspective on the co-design of molecular composition, supramolecular organization, and computational prediction for self-assembling non-natural peptide antimicrobial nanostructures. We survey chemistry-aware graph encoders, conditional generative models, and multi-task phenotype predictors, and critically assess the evidence for their applicability to peptoid, halogenated, and stapled scaffolds. On the materials side, we analyze stimulus-responsive shape transformation for biofilm eradication, self-assembling hydrogels for infected wound repair, and supramolecular shielding as a safety-by-design strategy. The review makes four engineering contributions: (i) an AI-ready minimum characterization data set spanning six interoperable domains; (ii) a critical analysis of four major AMP clinical failures (pexiganan, omiganan, iseganan, brilacidin) with translatable lessons; (iii) a manufacturability framework linking continuous-flow SPPS to closed-loop design; and (iv) a maturity-tiered assessment of what AI-guided peptide design can and cannot yet deliver. We argue that the field is mature enough to generate chemically-expanded libraries and integrate manufacturability constraints, but not yet ready to replace in vivo validation with in silico surrogates.

title: Fast parameter identification for elementary-step surface mechanisms using kinetically parameterized neural networks
abstract: Microkinetic models provide physically grounded descriptions of catalytic systems. However, quantitative prediction of catalyst performance requires refinement of elementary-step parameters against reactor-level measurement data. This calibration is computationally demanding because it involves repeated reactor simulations with computationally expensive microkinetic models. Surrogates that approximate the kinetic model reduce evaluation cost, but are currently tied to fixed kinetic parameters and therefore cannot be used for mechanism calibration. To address this limitation, we introduce kinetically parameterized Global Reaction Neural Network (pGRNN) surrogates that map both operating conditions and elementary-step kinetic parameters of a detailed microkinetic mechanism to species source terms. By embedding stoichiometry, thermodynamic consistency, and elementary-step structure, the surrogate replaces expensive kinetics evaluations while retaining a mechanism-consistent representation. Using the preferential CO oxidation on platinum, we show that the pGRNN predicts source terms across a broad range of operating conditions and kinetic parameters with a relative error of 1.2%. Reactor model evaluation is accelerated by a factor of 3100. The pGRNN is used in place of the kinetic model during mechanism calibration, reducing calibration time by factors of approximately 2400 for a synthetic single light-off curve and a synthetic multi-experiment campaign. Finally, we demonstrate the workflow by efficiently calibrating the mechanism against measured reactor-performance data from two experimental setups. A differentiable implementation of kinetic and reactor model further enables efficient gradient-based calibration. The proposed workflow provides an accelerated route for adapting detailed microkinetic models to catalyst-specific performance data.

title: CatRetriever: Contrastive representation learning for slab-to-bulk retrieval in generative catalyst discovery
abstract: Inverse design is an emerging data-driven paradigm for efficiently navigating vast chemical spaces to discover new materials with targeted properties, and in the context of heterogeneous catalysis, surface generative models have recently advanced this goal by directly generating catalyst surface-adsorbate structures. However, these models typically operate at the slab level and do not provide the corresponding parent bulk structure, making it difficult to assess bulk-dependent properties such as formation energy, surface energy, crystallographic symmetry, and synthesizability. Here, we address this missing slab-to-bulk connection as a retrieval problem and introduce CatRetriever, a contrastive representation learning model that aligns slab and bulk crystal representations in a shared latent space. From a slab query, CatRetriever accurately retrieves plausible parent bulk candidates with R@1 > 91% and R@3 > 98%. We further extend the CatRetriever framework into an adsorption energy-guided candidate screening pipeline that combines bulk retrieval, generative search space expansion, and adsorption energy distribution analysis. This workflow evaluates candidates by both structural compatibility with the query slab and their ability to access the target adsorption energy range across diverse surface environments. CatRetriever therefore provides a scalable route for connecting catalyst generative models with physically plausible and adsorption energy compatible bulk catalyst discovery.

title: Machine learning-assisted development of high-performance Cr-doped tungsten oxide triethylamine gas sensors
abstract: Accurate detection of triethylamine (TEA) is essential for environmental and industrial safety. However, conventional metal oxide semiconductor sensors exhibit insufficient sensitivity and selectivity. This study develops an intelligent TEA sensor based on Cr-doped WO3 nanomaterials integrated with machine learning. The 1 wt% Cr-WO3 sensor exhibited optimal performance, with a response of 330.1 to 50 ppm TEA at 240 °C (4.78 times higher than pristine WO3), rapid response/recovery times (11 s/44 s), and a low detection limit of 42 ppb. The sensor also demonstrated excellent selectivity, repeatability, and stability, attributed to Cr-induced surface oxygen vacancies that enhance gas interactions. Based on machine learning, we established a gas recognition model using the KNN algorithm and a concentration prediction model using the neural network algorithm. This work integrates material optimization and intelligent algorithms to establish a “high-sensitivity detection-smart analysis” framework, thereby advancing gas sensors toward systematic intelligence for next-generation monitoring systems.

title: AI-driven SERS biosensing chip for digital biomarker detection in diagnosis and monitoring of early-stage HCC
abstract: For complex diseases, sensing and decoding patterns in biofluids are crucial for accurate diagnosis. However, it has been challenged by suboptimal sensitivity and inadequate information processing for accessing measurable outcomes. To address this gap, we present an intelligent diagnostic sensor platform that synergistically integrates fabrication-compatible silicon-based surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) biosensing chips with a self-learning explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) framework by enabling digital biomarker-based diagnosis of early-stage hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The SERS biosensing chip, named SEARCH (Silicon-Etched Au-Reduced silver electro-Chemical deposition Heuristic), exploit hierarchical noble metal nanoarchitectures with dense electromagnetic hot spots, high enhancement of Raman signals, and superior inter-batch consistency, enabling sensitive detection of vibrational molecular fingerprints in serum. To interpret the high-dimensional Raman spectra, we developed a self-learning convolutional neural network (CNN)-based XAI framework that autonomously identifies and refines class-specific digital biomarkers, allowing it to dynamically adapt to population heterogeneity via iterative learning and unveil multidimensional spectral signatures encoded in serum-derived Raman spectra. In a multi-population cohort (N = 300), our platform demonstrated exceptional diagnostic performance, consistently achieving area under the curve (AUC) values above 0.93 across multiple classifiers in distinguishing early-stage HCC from both healthy controls and high-risk individuals. Comparative analysis revealed that SEARCH-derived digital biomarkers outperformed three conventional HCC serum markers. This work underscores the translational potential of combining scalable SERS biosensing with intelligent spectral analysis for digital cancer biomarker learning. The platform offers a robust, cost-efficient (<1.4 USD per test), and clinically actionable solution for the early diagnosis of HCC, showcasing the future of intelligent biosensing in precision oncology.

title: A hydrogel-based SERS sensor with wearable potential and machine learning integration for sweat stimulant detection
abstract: Doping abuse presents a persistent challenge in competitive sports and public health. To address the limitations of conventional detection methods, we developed a flexible, skin-adhesive hydrogel-based SERS sensor with wearable potential for non-invasive, on-body detection of doping agents in sweat. The ASP hydrogel (Au@Ag NRs/S-CNF/PAA/PAAM) was fabricated by embedding sulfonated cellulose nanofiber (S-CNF)-stabilized Au@Ag NRs into a PAA/PAAM double-network matrix. This design enhances nanoparticle dispersion, mechanical flexibility, and sweat absorption. The sensor achieved detection limits of 1.75 × 10−8 M (HCTZ), 1.0 × 10−9 M (TMZ), and 8.86 × 10−8 M (SAL), with excellent signal uniformity (RSD = 4.58 %) and 60-day storage stability. Mechanical tests confirmed optimized tensile strain (176.6 %) and good adhesive strength. The ASP hydrogel also demonstrated strong antibacterial activity against both E. coli and S. aureus (inhibition rate > 99 %) and high biocompatibility (cell viability >96 %), ensuring long-term skin safety during wear. Furthermore, machine learning algorithms enabled accurate spectral classification of the three stimulants, achieving 100 % test accuracy and AUC = 1.0. This multifunctional hydrogel platform integrates high sensitivity, mechanical durability, antimicrobial protection, and intelligent data processing, offering strong potential for real-time on-body stimulant monitoring in anti-doping, sports medicine, and personalized health management.

title: AI-assisted experimental analysis of geometry and flow effects in microstructured reactors
abstract: Efficient micromixing is critical in chemical microreactors, yet predictive modeling remains challenging due to complex flow dynamics. This study investigates micromixing performance in micro-coiled flow inverter tubes (MCFIs) using artificial neural networks (ANN), adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference systems (ANFIS), and genetic algorithms (GA). Experimental data were collected for six MCFI geometries using the Villermaux–Dushman reaction, with the segregation index (Xs) as the primary measure of mixing efficiency. Model inputs included the number of 90° bends, flow rate ratio of alkaline to acid solutions (r = Qalkaline/Qacid), and acid concentration, while outputs were Xs and pressure drop (ΔP). ANN achieved the highest prediction accuracy (Xs: 4.217 % MRE; ΔP: 1.30 % MRE), outperforming ANFIS (Xs: 6.481 %; ΔP: 1.91 %) and GA (Xs: 12.43 %; ΔP: 4.28 %). GA-driven multi-objective optimization revealed optimal MCFI designs that balance Xs and ΔP, offering practical guidance for reactor design. The results highlight the potential of data-driven models for the accurate prediction and optimization of micromixing in complex microreactor geometries. Unlike previous studies that focused on single-objective or simulation-based optimization, this work integrates experimentally validated data with AI-driven surrogate modeling and multi-objective optimization to quantitatively explore the trade-off between micromixing efficiency and energy consumption in micro-coiled flow inverters.

title: Novel discovery of geraniol and salvianolic acid B in regulating endometriosis recurrence targets LGALS3/VEGFA via integrating AI and biosensors
abstract: Endometriosis (EM) affects approximately 10 % of reproductive-aged women globally, with a postoperative recurrence rate as high as 50 %. However, the underlying targets and mechanisms of recurrence remain incompletely understood, hindering the development of effective targeted therapies. In response to this challenge, this study proposes an innovative strategy integrating information technology (IT) and biotechnology (BT), based on clinical samples from recurrence and non-recurrence EM patients. LncRNA and mRNA expression chip data from patients were initially acquired using microarray technology, and potential recurrence targets were identified using 8 machine learning algorithms. Subsequently, high-sensitivity biosensors were developed to validate the functional activity of these targets and screen for regulatory components. Finally, the biological regulatory effects of the molecules on the targets were confirmed using lesion cell models, providing experimental evidence for precision treatment. Results showed that two genes, vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGFA) and Galectin-3 (LGALS3), were identified as potential recurrence targets from 55,148 differentially expressed genes (DEGs). The developed biosensors exhibited high sensitivity, with a detection limit as low as 1 fM and a quantification range from 1 fM to 1 mM. Additionally, 21 critical quality attributes (CQAs) were identified using the biosensors, with two CQAs, geraniol and salvianolic acid B, showing strong interactions with VEGFA/LGALS3 targets. Ultimately, the therapeutic efficacy of these two CQAs in treating EM recurrence was validated through lesion cells models. This work offers a novel framework by integrating IT and BT technologies, addressing critical challenges in the identification of recurrence targets and therapeutic components in EM, and will be broadly useful for the research and development of clinical precision medicine.

title: Machine learning-assisted sensor array based on enhanced dual enzyme-like activities of Fe SAzymes modulated via Pluronic surfactant for multi-category perfluoroalkyl intelligent recognition and quantification
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent environmental pollutants with significant health risks, necessitating the development of efficient and cost-effective detection methods beyond conventional techniques. This study modulated the pore microenvironment of single-atom nanozymes (SAzymes) using Pluronic surfactants to enhance their oxidase-like (OXD-like) and laccase-like (LAC-like) activities. The optimized material, Fe/NC-@L31, exhibited improved surface area and pore volume, facilitating substrate diffusion and active site accessibility. A machine learning-assisted sensor array was then constructed based on the differential inhibitory effects of PFAS on the dual-enzyme activities. The Random Forest (RF) algorithm accurately discriminated seven categories of PFAS, and regression models achieved quantitative detection with recoveries of 85–103 % in real water samples. This classification-regression strategy provides a robust and intelligent platform for PFAS monitoring in environmental matrices.

title: Liquid-in-liquid printing and machine learning assisting the achievement of omni-directional, self-encapsulated flexible strain sensors
abstract: The practical application of flexible strain sensors is often limited by their unidirectional sensitivity and structural vulnerability caused by additional encapsulation processes. To overcome these issues, this work introduces an omnidirectional and self-encapsulated flexible strain sensor fabricated via liquid-in-liquid printing. The achieved sensor incorporates a branched graphene network that ensures uniform strain response in all designed directions, and it effectively inhibited the directional dependence typical of conventional sensors. Meanwhile, the self-leveling behavior of the liquid substrate allows the sensing element to be seamlessly encapsulated in a single step, enhancing interfacial integrity and long-term durability. Experimental results demonstrate that the sensor exhibits highly linear response, low hysteresis, and stable performance over 5000 stretching-releasing cycles. When integrated with a ResNet50 deep residual network, the sensor achieves human action recognition with an average accuracy of 96.15 %, and enables orientation-independent control of a robotic hand, highlighting its potential in human-machine interaction and intelligent industrial systems. This study establishes a scalable and efficient strategy for developing high-performance, durable flexible sensors through synergistic material and structural design.

title: Smart SERS platform with a machine-learning approach for the detection of thiram in fruit juices using an Ag NPs/NiFeLDH/MXene composite
abstract: Pesticides are widely used in modern agriculture to enhance crop yields and are recognized as environmental pollutants, making it crucial to monitor pesticide residue for the food safety and environmental protection. Herein, a sensitive and non-destructive strategy was developed to detect thiram in different fruit juices using surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS). The high SERS sensitivity relies on the effective interaction of analyte molecules with the substrate via the charge-transfer processes or within the hotspot regions. To explore the synergism of electromagnetic and chemical effects, a composite was constructed by decorating silver nanoparticles (Ag NPs) via an in-situ process onto the hydrothermally grown nickel‑iron layered double hydroxide (NiFeLDH) on the delaminated MXene. The Ag NPs/NiFeLDH/MXene composite exhibits high SERS sensitivity towards probe molecules (thiram, methylene blue (MB) and malachite green (MG)) due to the strong electrostatic attraction of the positively charged NiFe ions from the LDH to the negatively charged groups of MXene and the efficient anchoring of Ag NPs to the hydroxyl group of NiFeLDH. The composite demonstrates a significant SERS enhancement effect (up to 1010) and strong SERS performance towards MB, MG and thiram with the lowest detectable concentration of 1.24 × 10−12 M, 1.59 × 10−12 M and 2.8 × 10−11 M, respectively. Moreover, thiram at different concentrations was successfully detected in real-samples such as tomato, orange and apple juices. Additionally, a support vector machine (SVM) model applied to the SERS spectra of thiram in different real-samples achieved a classification accuracy exceeding 97 %. These results demonstrate the practicality of Ag NPs/NiFeLDH/MXene for the trace level detection of pesticides and organic pollutants.

title: From mechanism to design: Thermodynamic–metabolic coupling and data-driven optimization of Fe S substrates in constructed wetlands
abstract: Constructed wetlands enable sustainable nitrogen removal but are constrained by electron donor scarcity. Although iron–sulfur (FeS) substrates provide sustained redox energy, the mechanisms linking their thermodynamic properties with microbial metabolism remain unresolved, hindering rational design. Here, we propose an energy–metabolism coupling framework, where mechanistic insights yield a guiding rule and data-driven modeling translates it into FS substrate optimization. Results demonstrate that strongly reductive environments accelerate early nitrogen removal but cause redox imbalance and ion accumulation, whereas moderate redox potentials activate the TCA cycle and enrich denitrifies such as Pseudomonas and Shewanella, supporting long-term stability. Functional gene analysis further shows that electron oversupply upregulates iron transporter genes, imposing energetic burdens. These insights point to a central guideline: effective FeS regulation requires balancing electron availability with metabolic adaptability. Building on these insights, we developed a machine-learning model that predicts denitrification performance across FeS ratios, enabling rational optimization. In 200-day validation experiments, the optimized system consistently maintained nitrogen removal efficiencies above 90 % with minimal fluctuation (standard deviation <5 %). Taken together, this study establishes a scalable FeS regulation strategy and provides a blueprint for designing efficient and resilient constructed wetland systems.

title: Ultrasensitive dual-mode sensor with machine learning-decoupled pressure-temperature perception
abstract: Multifunctional electronic skin has attracted remarkable attention for its promising applications in health monitoring and human-machine interaction. However, it is still challenging to develop a multifunctional sensor via a single functional material or structure that achieves high sensitivity and multi-signal decoupling. This paper proposes a dual-mode flexible tactile sensor that generates distinct capacitive responses to both temperature and pressure stimuli. By synergy effect of hierarchical micropyramids structure and compressible PVA/MXene ionic gel electrolyte, the sensor demonstrates remarkable pressure sensitivity of 23.22 % kPa−1 with the range of 0–133.5 kPa, temperature sensitivity of 0.975 % °C−1 with the range of 25–75 °C. According to the capacitive response characteristics of temperature and pressure, the machine learning-enhanced multifunctional sensor can simultaneously identify and distinguish capacitance signals generated by temperature-pressure stimuli, achieving an impressive accuracy rate of 98.52 %. Finally, a 4 × 4 sensor array was printed to detect braille of six different meanings with accurate identification. Owing to the simple ‘sandwich’ structure design, ionic transport mechanisms, and machine learning algorithms, the sensor provides a cost-effective and promising method to multimodal signals decoupling, which paves the development of e-skin and human-computer interaction applications.

title: A urinary glucose detection platform based on 3D-MIP-SERS substrate and deep learning ensemble model
abstract: This study developed a high-performance 3D molecularly imprinted surface-enhanced Raman scattering substrate (3D-MIP-SERS substrate) with glucose-selective recognition capabilities, and combined it with deep learning ensemble model to establish a non-invasive urine glucose detection platform. The theoretical low detection limit of the 3D-MIP-SERS substrate for glucose is as low as 0.02 mM, and it exhibits excellent selectivity towards interfering molecules such as fructose. The substrate can directly incubate with urine samples without complex preprocessing to obtain high-quality spectra. To achieve precise glucose concentration identification, a deep learning model integrating channel attention and spatial attention mechanisms was designed, and combined with ensemble learning strategies to classify the spectra of artificial urine with different glucose concentrations, achieving a classification accuracy of 95.2 %. This study constructed a urine glucose detection system that combines high selectivity and sensitive recognition by molecularly imprinted SERS substrates and efficient data analysis by intelligent algorithms, offering a new technical path for early screening and home monitoring of diabetes.

title: Histidine-engineered Cu-HAc nanozyme with boosted peroxidase-like activity for accurate intelligent identification of β-lactam antibiotics through machine learning
abstract: Traditional detection techniques are difficult to distinguish and detect multiple β-lactam antibiotics simultaneously. The detection performance of sensor arrays is also limited due to the poor catalytic activity of nanozymes or the preparation of multiple receptor units. Here, inspired by the microenvironment of amino acid residues in the natural enzyme catalytic active center, a histidine-functionalized copper-based nanozyme (Cu-HAc@His) was constructed through a defect engineering strategy. Compared with the parent nanozyme (Cu-HAc), the obtained Cu-HAc@His nanozyme has higher peroxidase-like (POD) activity. Given the significant difference in catalytic activity of Cu-HAc@His nanozyme under different pH, a sensor array was constructed using three different pH values for efficient identification of nine β-lactam antibiotics. Meanwhile, relying on the improvement of various machine learning (ML) models, the precision of the concentration-irrelevant classification system built using this array has been enhanced to 93.52%. This result has played a role in promoting blind sample recognition. More importantly, combining regression algorithms with sensor arrays enables precise quantitative analysis of multiple β-lactam antibiotics. This work is not only of great significance for improving the identification of β-lactam antibiotics in actual samples, but supplies a point of reference and direction for developing highly active POD nanozymes down the line.

title: Data-driven discovery of novel additives for superconformal cobalt electrodeposition in 3D interconnects
abstract: In advanced electronic manufacturing, additives play a pivotal role in achieving high-quality metal interconnect by enabling precise pattern filling during electrodeposition. Currently, due to complex mechanisms, vast molecular spaces and lack of predictive models, the development of additives still relies on inefficient trial-and-error methods. In this work, a machine learning (ML)-based data-driven framework is developed to accelerate the discovery of cobalt electrodeposition additives. Focusing on molecular adsorption dynamics at the cobalt electrolyte interface during electrodeposition, this work employs quantum chemical properties to guide the construction of machine learning models for identifying molecules with ideal adsorption potential. Bayesian optimization is employed to optimize model accuracy by tuning hyperparameters, and SHAP analysis provides interpretable chemical insights. Three novel additives are identified, which are 2-aminopyrazine (APZ), 1-methylimidazole-4,5-dicarbonitrile (MIDCN), and 2-amino-4-ethylpyridine (AEP). Electrochemical and electroplating validation confirms that all additives exhibit strong inhibition effects, enabling grain refinement that reduces cobalt film surface roughness below 10 nm Ra, with the optimal performer achieving 4.58 nm Ra. Furthermore, superconformal filling of through‑silicon vias (TSVs) with aspect ratios >5 is achieved. This work establishes a machine learning-based data-driven strategy as an effective tool for accelerating the discovery of high-performance electrodeposition additives. The identified additives provide new insights into industrial metallization solutions for scaled-down nodes.

title: Skin-inspired hierarchical strain-partitioned sensor for ultralow detection thresholds and broad-range strain detection, empowered by dual-mode machine learning
abstract: Inspired by biomimetic strategies, crack-based strain-sensing technology has greatly advanced the hardware foundation of human–machine interfaces. However, conventional crack sensors face a critical trade-off among ultralow detection thresholds and broad-range operational ranges, which remains a key bottleneck limiting their overall performance. Here, drawing inspiration from the multilayered distribution of mechanoreceptors in human skin, we propose a hierarchical, multidimensional strain sensor architecture composed of vertically graphene (VG), MXene, and carbon nanotubes (CNTs). By introducing microchannels pattern in the VG layer together with a multi-step stretch–release coating strategy for the MXene and CNT layers, each material layer is structurally engineered in a targeted manner to form a stepwise conductive network. The synergistic coupling of these multilayer conductive pathways reduces the lower limit of detection 0.05‰ and expands the upper limit of detection to 80%, enabling a sensing range spanning five orders of magnitude. Beyond material engineering, a dual-mode machine learning framework, combining eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) for static posture classification and Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) for dynamic motion recognition, achieves classification accuracies exceeding 99%. This cross-disciplinary integration of hierarchical material design and intelligent data analysis paves the way for next-generation wearable interfaces and health-monitoring systems.

title: Deep learning-assisted piezoelectric nanogenerators based on layered SnS2/MoS2 heterostructures for interactive sensing and affective computing applications
abstract: Layered metal dichalcogenides (LMDCs) have attracted widespread attention in piezoelectric systems, particularly for miniaturized energy devices and wearable sensing applications. However, insufficient output performance and limited sensing accuracy remain critical challenges. In this work, we developed a van der Waals heterostructure (vdWH) composed of molybdenum disulfide/tin disulfide (SnS2/MoS2) by using chemical vapor deposition (CVD). The enhancement of intrinsic piezoelectricity was further confirmed by piezoelectric force microscopy (PFM). Furthermore, the as-fabricated SnS2/MoS2 vdWH was assembled into a piezoelectric nanogenerator (SM-PENG) device and demonstrated as a self-powered healthcare sensor to monitor diverse human motions. A sequential fast data density functional transform (s-fDDFT) model was also employed to improve the prediction accuracy of the designed sensor. Most importantly, the SM-PENGs were integrated into a multi-channel facial expression recognition platform for affective computing applications. We believe that this SM-PENG not only shows great potential for future ultrathin active sensors, but also represents a promising step toward personalized healthcare monitoring and emotion recognition.

title: Innovative utilization of waste printed circuit boards and coal gangue/ash for multifunctional glass-ceramics: structure-property insights via data-driven analysis
abstract: To address environmental challenges from electronic/industrial wastes accumulation, this study fabricated multifunctional glass-ceramics using waste printed circuit boards (WPCBs) and coal gangue/ash (CG/CA), integrating experimental techniques with machine learning (ML) to uncover structure-property-function relationships. First, the CaO-Al2O3-SiO2 glass-ceramic system was optimized by adjusting Al2O3/SiO2 ratio, glass network structure, crystallization behavior, and micromorphology. AS2 sample (Al2O3/SiO2 = 0.28) was identified as the base composition due to its superior performance, achieving high crystallinity (89.53%), bending strength (BS = 342 MPa), dielectric constant (εr = 6.62), low dielectric loss (tan δ = 1.14 × 10−3), and low thermal expansion coefficient (CTE = 5.86 × 10−6/K). Incorporating CA and CG provided cost-effective and sustainable alternatives. CA25 (CA/PCBA = 25/75) achieved comparable properties (BS = 289.5 MPa, εr = 6.77, tan δ = 4.24 × 10−3, CTE = 5.74 × 10−6/K), making it suitable for electrical applications. CG75 (CG/PCBA = 75/25) exhibited excellent BS (373 MPa) and magnetic properties (saturation magnetization = 5.71 emu/g, coercivity = 990 Oe), indicating potential for magnetic recording and magnetic separation. Three ML models, particularly random forest, revealed complex, nonlinear relationships and synergistic effects among structural features that influence performance by incorporating interaction terms and combining with statistical analysis. The process immobilized heavy metals (leaching below limits), reduced energy consumption, and achieved a 2680.09 CNY/t gross profit. This work provided an eco-friendly and cost-effective route for waste valorization into high-value materials.

title: A single urine test-based SERS–AI–BAM for on-site multiple cancer diagnosis and metabolite profiling
abstract: Rapid detection of multiple cancers offers remarkable advantages, particularly when the type of cancer is unknown, and enables the discovery of undiagnosed cancers through screening. Cancer development causes abnormal alterations in metabolites, many of which are excreted in the urine. Recognizing changes in urinary metabolites can reveal specific characteristics of various cancer types and aid in their diagnosis. Herein, we analyzed 218 urine samples from healthy individuals and patients with pancreatic, prostate, lung, and colorectal cancers using plasmonic materials to obtain label-free surface-enhanced Raman scattering signals. Applying artificial intelligence-based analytical methods, we achieved a diagnostic accuracy of >99% across all five groups. To identify urinary metabolic biomarkers, we compiled a library of known urinary metabolites and applied the multivariate curve resolution–alternating least squares method, a bilinear algorithm model, to relatively quantify the secretion levels of selected metabolites. This approach combines SERS signals from plasmonic materials with AI analysis and mathematical modeling to propose biomarkers. The technology is expected to provide a versatile platform not only for multicancer diagnosis but also for diagnosing various diseases, offering a promising tool for early detection and personalized medicine.

title: A customizable three-dimensional-printed triaxial force sensing finger cot with residual fully connected neural network algorithm for wearable hand rehabilitation
abstract: The restoration of hand function is pivotal for regaining autonomy and quality of life following neurological or orthopedic impairments. Multidimensional assessment of finger forces is essential for motor recovery, yet current rehabilitation solutions are often constrained by insufficient multidimensional force sensing capability and poor wearing comfort. Here, we present a real-time monitoring system for assisted hand rehabilitation, integrating a fully customizable triaxial force sensing finger cot with a residual fully connected neural network (Res-FCNN) for force component decoupling. Using high-resolution digital light processing (DLP) three-dimensional (3D) printing, the customizable triaxial force sensing finger cot is fabricated combining complex structures with microscale precision and ergonomic design. The sensitivities of the triaxial force sensor of the system are 0.0213 and 0.0625 N−1 in tangential and normal directions, respectively. The proposed Res-FCNN model enables precise decoupling of triaxial force components, achieving an R2 greater than 0.95 across all axes. Moreover, experimental validations (including finger motion trajectory distinction and grasp stability assessment) demonstrate that the real-time monitoring system integrating the customizable wearable hardware with algorithm-based signal decoding provides a practical framework for quantitative analysis and evaluation of hand rehabilitation training.

title: Integrating data and physics: A review of data-driven methods for computational multiphase flow
abstract: Computational modeling of multiphase flow systems is crucial across various fields, including chemical engineering, energy, environmental science and aerospace industry, enabling cost-effective design and analysis. However, accurate simulation, prediction, control, and optimization remain difficult due to the high-dimensional, chaotic behavior and dynamic interfaces of multiphase flows. Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning, physics constrained learning, generative models, and reinforcement learning offer promising tools to overcome these challenges. This review presents the current landscape of AI in multiphase flow research. It highlights AI-enhanced numerical solvers for interface dynamics, including explicit interface tracking and implicit interface capturing, as well as intelligent sparse grid processing. AI-extended simulation implementations are also explored, with an emphasis on generative models such as generative adversarial networks (GANs), variational autoencoders (VAEs) and large language models (LLM)-driven agents that synthesize physically consistent samples and automate complex modeling and simulation workflows. Moreover, AI-oriented control and optimization methods – such as Bayesian optimization (BO), reinforcement learning (RL), and automatic differentiation (AD) – are analyzed for optimizing mixing, stability, and phase distribution, particularly in industrial settings that require real-time, high-performance solutions. Finally, we provide a critical assessment of the challenges and opportunities of learning-based algorithms, emphasizing dataset normalization and model-design regularization to enhance generalization. Overall, this review bridges multiphase-flow mechanics, data science, AI, and computational chemical engineering, and documents an ongoing digital and intelligent progression from fully physics-based equation solving approaches to a physics-coupled, and data-driven integrated computational framework.

title: Application of machine learning in the design of biomedical nanomaterials
abstract: As artificial intelligence technology advances rapidly, machine learning shows great potential in materials science. It can efficiently process and analyze large-scale data, uncover complex patterns, and offer new approaches for material prediction and design. This review focuses on the application progress of machine-learning models in biomedical nanomaterial design. Firstly, it presents the basic principles, development history, and advantages of machine learning in this field. Then, it provides a deep analysis of the technical breakthroughs in machine-learning models for predicting physicochemical properties, optimizing synthesis routes, and analyzing biological interactions of nanomaterials. Finally, it addresses the challenges of insufficient data quality and limited model interpretability in machine learning, and proposes solutions like developing more explainable machine-learning methods, standardizing data-reporting formats, combining machine learning with traditional molecular simulations, and enhancing result verification. Overall, this review aims to promote a shift from experience-driven to data-driven approaches in the field of biomedical nanomaterial design and to facilitate innovation and clinical translation in this area.

title: Inspired by natural antioxidants: Design of high-performance phenolic antioxidants based on machine learning and its application in NR
abstract: While traditional synthetic antioxidants are efficient, their toxicity presents ecological drawbacks. This study harnessed multi-scale simulation and machine learning to design a high-performance, eco-friendly phenolic antioxidant. Inspired by natural antioxidants, this study analyzed the influence of natural antioxidant molecular structure on the bond dissociation energy (BDE), and established a database containing phenolic antioxidants' structural information and BDE, then bioinspired-designed a high-performance phenolic botannical acid-derived antioxidant (CAA) by machine learning. The Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model was employed to predict the bond dissociation energy of antioxidants with high accuracy (R2 = 0.87, RMSE = 11.71 kJ/mol). The new phenolic antioxidant CAA with low BDE was designed by mapping substituent descriptors to molecular descriptors. We further investigated the toxicological effects and anti-aging mechanisms of CAA through integrated experimental and multi-scale simulation methods. A quantitative analysis of the chemical reactions and. physical behaviors was conducted, comparing CAA with sinapic acid, syringic acid, gallic acid, butylated hydroxyanisole (BHA), and 2,4,6-Tri-tert-butylphenol (2,4,6-TTBP). Toxicity simulations indicated that CAA has lower acute/chronic toxicity than BHA and 2,4,6-TTBP, with no mutagenicity or bioaccumulation. Moreover, multiscale simulations revealed its high antioxidant capacity, characterized by a low BDE (280.3 kJ·mol−1) and a low transition state (TS) energy barrier (20.4 kJ·mol−1). Furthermore, the CAA-incorporated natural rubber (NR) composite exhibited exceptional thermo-oxidative stability, retaining 87.8% of its tensile strength after 72 h of thermal aging. Additionally, migration tests confirmed the superior anti-migration stability of CAA, evidenced by a minimal change (9.2%) in change ultraviolet (UV) absorption intensity within the NR composite. Therefore, the designed antioxidant CAA is environmentally benign and exhibits superior resistance to thermo-oxidative aging and migration. This work provides valuable guidance for screening and designing high-performance, eco-friendly antioxidants.

title: 3D-printed microstructured ionic hydrogel and nano-friction generator for self-powered electronic skin and deep learning character recognition
abstract: Developing flexible sensing materials that integrate high conductivity, mechanical robustness, self-healing capabilities, and environmental stability remains a critical challenge for next-generation wearable electronics. However, conventional hydrogels often suffer from intrinsic trade-offs between these properties and are prone to freezing-induced deactivation. Herein, a multifunctional POAL hydrogel was engineered via a synergistic strategy combining the double-helix network of agar, dynamic Schiff base crosslinking of oxidized sodium alginate (OSA), and ionic coordination of LiCl. This unique multi-network architecture endows the hydrogel with outstanding comprehensive properties, including a tensile strength of 111.9 kPa, an elongation at break of 158%, and a self-healing efficiency of 48.9%. Notably, the hydrogel exhibits exceptional ionic conductivity (2.25 S/m and anti-freezing tolerance down to −42.1 °C, ensuring reliable operation in harsh environments. Leveraging its excellent rheological properties, micro-triangular pyramidal arrays were precisely fabricated via Digital Light Processing (DLP) 3D printing to construct a high-performance triboelectric nanogenerator (POAL-TENG). By maximizing the effective contact area, the device achieved a peak output voltage of 239.9 V and a superior pressure sensitivity of 89.14 mV Pa−1, effectively harvesting mechanical energy. Furthermore, to realize intelligent sensing, a hybrid Deep Learning model (ResNet-18 + Bidirectional LSTM) was integrated to process handwriting signals, achieving a 97% recognition accuracy. This work presents a comprehensive strategy for designing robust, freeze-tolerant, and intelligent self-powered sensing systems, expanding the horizons of human-machine interaction (HMI).

title: Nanoplastics and co-pollutants negatively affect the photosynthesis of photosynthetic organisms: insights from meta-analysis and machine learning
abstract: Nanoplastics are increasingly recognized as emerging stressors that impair photosynthesis in photosynthetic organisms, and their co-occurrence with environmental pollutants can further intensify phytotoxic effects. To address the fragmented understanding of these combined impacts, we integrated a meta-analysis of 1067 experimental observations with explainable machine learning to quantify how nanoplastics and co-pollutants jointly influence photosynthetic processes. The results showed predominantly negative effects across light reactions and rubisco enzyme activity, with organism species, nanoplastics dose, size, and exposure duration identified as major determinants of photosynthetic inhibition. High-sensitivity indicators of photosynthetic stress were identified, and corn emerged as a particularly sensitive organism. By linking physicochemical properties and exposure conditions to quantitative photosynthetic outcomes, this study provides a clearer and more accessible framework for predicting phytotoxicity and supports improved ecological risk assessment and management strategies.

title: Thermo-oxidative aging mechanism and machine learning-assisted lifetime prediction of CF/PPESK composites
abstract: Continuous carbon fiber-reinforced poly(phthalazinone ether sulfone ketone) (CF/PPESK) composites exhibit exceptional high-temperature resistance and mechanical properties, rendering them promising candidates for aerospace applications. However, the degradation mechanisms and service lifetime of these composites under prolonged thermo-oxidative aging remain insufficiently elucidated. This study systematically investigates the structure-property evolution of CF/PPESK composites at 250–290 °C through integrated multiscale characterization and machine learning approaches. After 1008 h of thermo-oxidative aging at 250 °C, the interlaminar shear strength (ILSS) retention decreases by 87.8%, primarily due to interfacial debonding and microcrack propagation. While short-term cross-linking of PPESK at 290 °C enhances ILSS by 20%, prolonged exposure at this temperature leads to a 50.7% reduction in flexural strength, mainly attributed to molecular chain scission and interfacial degradation. The competitive temperature-dependent mechanism is quantitatively described through Starink kinetic analysis. Based on this, a machine learning model is constructed to precisely quantify the complex and nonlinear relationship that governs the material performance and its post-aging chemical state. The optimized Random Forest model demonstrated high prediction accuracy for the retention of both flexural strength and ILSS, with mean absolute errors as low as 0.22 and 0.19, and coefficients of determination reaching 0.96 and 0.97. This model provides an analytical tool for understanding and modeling the degradation behavior of CF/PPESK composites.

title: Supercritical water gasification of lignocellulosic biomass: Kinetic modeling enhanced by Bayesian optimization
abstract: A new kinetic model for the supercritical water gasification of lignocellulosic biomass is presented. This model accurately simulates the production of gases up to C 3 products, and distinguishes condensable products as either aqueous condensate or tars. The reaction orders were treated as hyperparameters, which were tuned via Bayesian optimization. The model was validated against experiments conducted in a continuous laboratory plant operating within a broad range of conditions, including variations in temperature (823–973 K), pressure (240–300 bar), biomass content (1.3–6.6 wt%), K 2 CO 3 addition (0–3750 ppm), and residence time (6–48 s). The proposed model provides insight into the behavior of the reactive system and is useful for applications such as scale-up, process optimization, and process design. • New kinetic model for SCWG of lignocellulosic biomass predicts gas products up to C 3 . • Reaction orders tuned via Bayesian optimization • Model validated in a broad operating window with the cross-validation method • Obtained insight into the behavior of the reactive system

title: Multiple ensemble graph neural networks for the high-throughput screening of ionic liquids for carbon capture: Modeling study and experimental validation
abstract: The escalating need for efficient carbon dioxide (CO2) capture has positioned ionic liquids (ILs) as promising candidates due to their tunable structures and high CO2 affinity. However, systematic strategies that integrate machine learning (ML) predictions with experimental validation remain limited, and the prediction accuracy and reliability of single ML methods for new ILs needs to be improved. In this study, we introduced four ensemble frameworks that strategically integrates five classical graph neural networks (GNNs), capitalizing on their complementary strengths to effectively mitigate the inherent limitations of single-model approaches. When predicting the CO2 absorption capacity and viscosity of novel ILs, the ensemble frameworks generally outperformed traditional ML methods, with the optimal ensemble model achieving R2 values of 0.9258 and 0.9250, respectively. To enable high-throughput screening, we generated a virtual library of 7616 ILs via pairwise combination of 112 cations and 68 anions, and established multi-dimensional criteria (CO2 absorption mole fraction >0.1, viscosity <100 mPa·s at 40 °C and 101.325 kPa, SAScore <3.5) to select ILs balancing performance and synthetic feasibility. Finally, we screened 176 new high-performance candidates and validated four ILs experimentally, with close consistency between predicted and experimental properties (relative deviations: 4.21%, 8.85%, 18.32% and 16.14%, respectively). The framework accelerates the design of ILs with exceptional CO2 absorption capacity and reduced viscosity, thereby establishing a generalizable and interpretable ensemble ML approach for molecular materials discovery.

title: Discovery of high-energy-density materials via machine learning-assisted high-throughput virtual screening and experimental approach
abstract: The pursuit of new high-energy density materials with desirable sensitivity properties has been a prominent research focus in recent years. However, the intrinsic trade-off between energy and sensitivity poses a major obstacle in the design of advanced energetic materials. In this work, machine learning assisted high-throughput virtual screening (ML-HTVS), integrated with experimental validation, was employed to accelerate the discovery of high-energy density and low-sensitivity materials. Through this approach, we rapidly identified 3-amino-7-nitro-[1,2,4]triazolo[1,5-b][1,2,4,5]tetrazine-2-oxide (ICM-107) as a promising candidate molecule. Subsequently, we successfully synthesized this compound starting from 3,6-bis(3,5-dimethyl pyrazol-1-yl)-1,2,4,5-tetrazine (DMPT) through a five-step process. ICM-107 exhibits an impressive experimental density of 1.973 g·cm−3 and outstanding calculated detonation performance (Dv: 9584 m·s−1, P: 40.0 GPa) as well as experimental measured detonation performance (Dv: 9290 m·s−1, P: 39.5 GPa). Among all [5,6]fused-ring energetic materials, ICM-107 stands out with the highest recorded detonation performance, approaching that of the benchmark explosive CL-20. Additionally, it features a favorable decomposition temperature (Td: 212 °C) and low sensitivity characteristics (impact sensitivity, IS: 20 J; friction sensitivity, FS: 324 N). These highly promising properties make it highly attractive as a high-energy and low-sensitivity energetic materials.

title: Implementation of excellent tensile strain for sign language translation using wood-based finger-code supported by machine learning algorithms
abstract: Based on the Hofmeister effect to optimize interfacial interactions, this study combined a chemical-physical dual cross-linking strategy and integrated machine learning algorithms to successfully fabricate a wearable wood-based finger-code. This device exhibits a response time of only 212 ms, a low detection limit of 0.19% strain, and also features environmental friendliness and low cost, which is used to achieve precise capture of subtle finger joint deformations and conversion between sign language movements and letter signals. The sensor uses wood cellulose as a natural three-dimensional support framework, with polyacrylic acid (PAA) and polyacrylamide (PAM) as functional fillers. The interfacial synergy between the framework and fillers provides a structural basis for the device's excellent performance. Meanwhile, Hofmeister effect modulated hydrogel micro-crosslinking structure; sulfate ions (SO₄2−) optimized hydrogel stiffness and flexibility via regulating interfacial water arrangement, hydrogen bonds and hydrophobicity. It not only achieves a longitudinal tensile stress of 12.49 MPa and a transverse tensile stress of 0.83 MPa, but also exhibits high mechanical strength, outstanding adhesion, favorable cyclic stability, and superior electrochemical performance. In practical application scenarios, after wearing this wearable device, model training and gesture recognition analysis were conducted using the Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) Classifier machine learning algorithm. Finally, an ultra-high recognition accuracy of 98.46% was achieved, enabling real-time and accurate analysis of gesture movements and rapid output of corresponding letter signals, thus truly realizing green, low-cost, and high-sensitivity sign language-text conversion. This research not only provides a new functional device with excellent performance for the field of intelligent human-computer communication, but also opens up a new direction for barrier-free communication through an economical and efficient technical route, showing broad application prospects.

title: AI-driven process-tolerant BioFET sensing model for precise biliary atresia diagnosis of infants with a single drop of blood
abstract: Biliary atresia (BA) is a rare but life-threatening neonatal liver disease and remains one of the leading causes of pediatric liver transplantation worldwide. If untreated, the 2-year survival rate is below 10%, and delayed diagnosis markedly reduces the success rate of Kasai portoenterostomy. Current diagnostic methods rely primarily on dried blood spots (DBS) and ELISA, which require relatively large blood volumes, are time-consuming, and are poorly suited for routine newborn screening, creating an urgent need for rapid and neonate-friendly diagnostic tools. Here, we present an AI-assisted biosensing platform for rapid and quantitative detection of matrix metalloproteinase-7 (MMP7), a clinically validated biomarker for BA. The platform integrates an electric double-layer extended-gate field-effect transistor (EDL-EGFET) with an AI-based calibration strategy that compensates for chip-to-chip variation and enables consistent quantification across sensors. By incorporating process parameters into model training, the AI system effectively reduces chip-to-chip variability, significantly improving the robustness of the sensing platform. Clinical validation using 20 patient samples demonstrated a strong correlation with ELISA-based quantification. The Pearson correlation coefficient improved from 0.80 using the conventional method to 0.96 with the AI-enhanced model. The system achieved a limit of detection of 0.32 ng/mL, covered the clinically relevant MMP7 range, and reduced the total diagnostic time from 8 h to 10 min. Only 10 μL (one drop) of blood was required per test. This innovative AI-driven EDL-EGFET platform demonstrates strong potential for advancing precise clinical diagnostics, enhancing neonatal care, and addressing the diagnostic challenges associated with this neglected disease.

title: Continuous flow synthesis of fluconazole monitored by inline ultraviolet spectroscopy: 3D microfluidic platform and Bayesian optimization
abstract: Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) face significant challenges in end-to-end continuous flow synthesis, including low throughput, inefficient condition optimization, and discontinuous multi-step processes. This study develops a methodological framework for the continuous flow synthesis of fluconazole, centered on three key innovations: a milliliter-scale 3D microfluidic chip (MFC) with a high-density Barker transform structure, which achieves >99% mixing efficiency within 6 s (Reynolds number 3–350) and overcomes the volume limitation of traditional microfluidics; a synergistic optimization strategy combining Bayesian Optimization (BO) and in-line UV monitoring, which identifies optimal reaction conditions with minimal experiments; and a fully uninterrupted flow process integrating in-line extraction and circulating flow, eliminating off-line workup and streamlining time-consuming steps. Applied to fluconazole synthesis, this framework achieves an 86% yield in 2 h and 40 min, outperforming traditional batch processes and existing continuous flow routes. This work provides a scalable methodological paradigm for the full-process continuous synthesis of other APIs, highlighting the value of integrated device-design, real-time analytics, and process regulation in pharmaceutical manufacturing.

title: Fusing nanoprisms and embedded AI: a portable sensor for intelligent peroxide value monitoring in edible oils
abstract: The rapid and on-site monitoring of peroxide value (PV) is crucial for assessing the quality and safety of edible oils. To address this need, two enzyme-free optical sensing strategies were developed based on iodide-mediated chromogenic systems, utilizing 3,3′,5,5′-tetramethylbenzidine (I-TMB) and triangular gold nanoprisms (IAu NPRs), respectively. The IAu NPRs system exhibited a wider linear detection range and a faster response, attributed to localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) shifts due to peroxide-induced iodide etching. A linear correlation was established across a PV range of 0.0045 to 27.85 mmol·kg−1 using UV–vis spectrophotometry, with a calculated detection limit of 0.0015 mmol·kg−1. Validation with real oil samples demonstrated satisfactory recovery rates (98.94–101.40%) and relative standard deviations (RSD) between 2.30% and 3.53%. Furthermore, a portable detection platform was constructed by integrating this sensing strategy with the Kendryte K210 smart chip and a deep learning algorithm. This integrated system provided results consistent with laboratory-based UV–vis measurements, indicating its potential for practical field analysis of edible oils. The combination of nanoprism-based sensing with portable artificial intelligence analytics represents a significant step toward rapid food quality monitoring technologies.

title: Machine learning-assisted discrimination and detection of volatile organic compounds based on chemiresistive gas sensors made with Bi2WO6/In2O3 heterojunctions
abstract: This study reports a novel room-temperature chemical resistance gas sensor, which is based on the flower-like Bi2WO6/In2O3 heterojunction and is co-integrated with a machine learning algorithm, achieving high-performance and selective detection of volatile organic compounds. The composites synthesized by the combined hydrothermal-calcination method have a unique microstructure, in which In2O3 nanoparticles are uniformly anchored to Bi2WO6 nanospheres to form effective n-n-type heterojunctions. The optimized sensor (labeled B/I-2 with a Bi:In molar ratio of 1:2) demonstrates excellent sensing performance at 25 °C: a response value of up to 16.8 to 100 ppm n-butanol, which is approximately 7.3 times higher than pure Bi2WO6 (2.3), along with a low detection limit (55 ppb), fast response/recovery time (55 s/77 s), excellent repeatability, and up to 31 days of stability. In addition, the sensor maintains a significant response (10.4) in high humidity (74% RH) environments. To overcome the inherent selectivity challenges of metal oxide sensors, four machine learning models are introduced: random forests, convolutional neural networks, long short-term memory networks, and genetic algorithm-optimized backpropagation networks. Five interfering VOCs (n-butanol, n-propanol, ethanol, acetone, and xylene, all at concentrations of 100 ppm) were classified and identified. Among them, the random forest model achieved the highest recognition accuracy of 95.74%, demonstrating the effectiveness of machine learning in improving sensor selectivity. Diffuse reflection infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy revealed the reaction path on the surface of the material, confirming the oxidation of n-butanol to CO2 and H2O. Finally, by integrating the B/I-2 sensor with the STM32 microcontroller, a portable prototype device was built, which successfully realized real-time monitoring of n-butanol and visual LED alarms, verifying its practical application potential.

title: Machine learning unlocks multi-metal synergy in Prussian blue cathodes toward ultralow-cost sodium-ion grid storage
abstract: Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are emerging as a cost-effective alternative to lithium-ion batteries for large-scale energy storage. However, their commercialization has been hindered by the lack of low-cost and high-performance cathode materials. Here, we report a machine learning–guided strategy for designing multi-metal Prussian blue analogues (PBAs), establishing a paradigm of synergistic elemental modulation. The optimized PBA-MCNF delivers a reversible capacity of 102.59 mAh g−1 at 1C and maintains 97.07% of its capacity after 2500 cycles (based on 105.68 mAh g−1 at the first cycle). The synergistic effect among Mn, Cu, Ni, and Fe simultaneously broadens the Na+ migration channels and enhances both conductivity and structural stability. Cost analysis reveals that, compared with LiFePO4, the cathode material cost is reduced by 33.8%, with an average energy storage cost as low as 0.083 $/kWh. By integrating machine learning, DFT calculations, experimental validation, and techno-economic analysis, this work provides a comprehensive framework for advancing SIB research and opens a new avenue for practical large-scale deployment.

title: Hetero In2O3@Co3O4 derived from MOF-on-MOF conjugate combined synergistically with exponential-trigonometric optimization-support vector regression enables high-precision quantitative detection of H2S
abstract: Due to the widespread application of hydrogen sulfide (H2S) in industries such as chemical, medical, and food, highly selective detection of H2S at low temperatures is of great significance. Chemiresistive gas sensors based on metal-oxide-semiconductor (MOS) have been widely used for detecting various gases; however, due to the low efficiency of electron transfer in individual MOSs, their gas-sensing performance is far from satisfactory. Herein, a porous bimetallic oxide In2O3@Co3O4 heterojunction has been obtained by elaborately constructing metal-organic framework (MOF)-on-MOF conjugate (MIL-68@ZIF-67). The developed In2O3@Co3O4 sensor achieves great sensing performances for H2S (100 ppm), exhibiting outstanding selectivity, high sensitivity (110.2), and rapid recovery speed (47 s) at a low working temperature (100 °C), which are significantly better than that of pristine In2O3 and Co3O4. The large mesoporous architecture, rich active sites generated by composite Co3O4, and formation of type II charge transfer pathway are primarily accountable for the improved H2S-sensing capabilities. Moreover, density functional theory (DFT) calculations show that In2O3@Co3O4 has a higher adsorption energy for H2S compared to other comparative gases. The optimal sensor demonstrates high-accuracy (R2 = 0.9907) H2S concentration prediction capability driven by Machine Learning. The ability to predict H2S concentration by combining high-performance sensor with regression prediction model provides a feasible approach for the next generation of devices in environmental monitoring and other related fields.

title: A deep learning-assisted SMART label for food freshness monitoring and prediction under variable lighting conditions
abstract: In this study, a deep learning-assisted Smartphone-based, MOF-powered, Amine-Responsive, Traceability (SMART) label was developed for the real-time monitoring and precise prediction of food freshness through the food supply chain. This non-destructive freshness assessment is achieved by photographing the SMART label with a smartphone for deep-learning-based image analysis. An anthocyanin @ zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (A @ ZIF-8) nanocomposite was synthesized using a one-pot method, in which anthocyanins were encapsulated within the MOF framework and subsequently embedded in a hydrogel matrix. The strategy of MOF encapsulation effectively enhances the structural stability of the loaded anthocyanins, which worked as a freshness indicator, while the integration of MOFs and hydrogels significantly enhances the response sensitivity of the SMART label. Considering the strong influence of ambient lighting on smartphone-based freshness assessment, representative real-world lighting conditions (~50 lx, ~500 lx, ~5000 lx, and ~ 50,000 lx) were simulated to construct a dataset. A cascaded light-adaptive convolutional neural network (CNN) model achieved prediction accuracies exceeding 91% when trained on 5760 marked images, outperforming representative other end-to-end CNN models, showing its desirable sensing stability in variable lighting conditions. Coupled with the self-developed “FoodSense” application, the proposed system provides a practical and reliable platform for rapid food freshness prediction and early risk warning across the food supply chain.

title: AI-driven fault diagnosis in smart bearings using mosaic-patterned electret for multi-modal motion sensing
abstract: Smart bearings offer a promising approach for real-time motion and condition monitoring in rotating machinery by embedding sensing functionality directly into the bearing structure. However, most existing smart bearing designs remain constrained to single-modal motion sensing, typically capturing only rotational or vibrational motion. In this paper, a novel smart thrust ball bearing (STBB) is proposed, incorporating a mosaic-patterned polarized electret for enhanced multi-modal motion sensing. Charges are injected into the electret film in a patterned manner using silicon shadow masks fabricated via deep reactive ion etching (DRIE). The coupled signal from simultaneous rotational and vibrational motions is fully decoupled through the dual Fourier transform (DFT) algorithm. The results show that the STBB exhibits high linearity, with R2 = 0.9999 and R2 = 0.9998 for rotation and vibration, respectively, and a rotational sensitivity of 7.48 rpm·Hz−1. The STBB is further integrated into a six-joint robotic arm for dynamic monitoring. Combined with a long short-term memory (LSTM) neural network, the STBB achieves 90.33% fault classification accuracy. These findings highlight its potential as a scalable and multi-modal sensing solution for intelligent maintenance systems.

title: Honeycomb electrode-based triboelectric nanogenerator for deep learning-derived bimodal human-machine interaction systems
abstract: This study presents a bimodal human-machine interaction panel based on a honeycomb electrode structure. The device is designed in accordance with the principle of triboelectric nanogenerators and is capable of recognizing contact and non-contact handwriting inputs. By embedding CaCu₃Ti₄O₁₂ particles into the Ecoflex triboelectric layer, the output performance in non-contact mode is significantly improved, achieving a voltage output of 8.3 V at a distance of 30 mm. When integrated with a convolutional neural network model, the device demonstrates high-precision recognition of 26 English letters in non-contact mode, as well as contact-based Chinese characters and numeric combinations, with an average recognition accuracy exceeding 95%. Furthermore, a human-machine interaction system was developed using the BHMIP, where tapping out Morse code are employed to control directional commands and non-contact input is used for numerical input, enabling precise control of Sudoku games. This system effectively demonstrates the application potential of BHMIP in gesture recognition, self-powered signal acquisition, and intelligent input control. Although surface charge stability under high humidity and signal decoupling in complex scenarios remain challenging, this work presents a solution for the development of self-powered, multi-dimensional human-machine interfaces.

title: Machine learning–guided screening of highly efficient multi-cationic photosensitizers for capture–contact–photodynamic antibacterial fabrics
abstract: The development of highly efficient photosensitizers is crucial for advancing photodynamic therapy (PDT), yet current approaches largely rely on traditional trial–and–error synthesis coupled with iterative performance screening, which slows down its extensive application. Herein, we present a machine learning–based platform that predicts the photophysical properties of functionally tailored photosensitizers through regression and classification models, enabling rapid screening and identification of TMPB as an optimal candidate. Experimental validation confirmed that TMPB exhibits robust reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation via both Type I and Type II pathways, achieving a high relative singlet oxygen quantum yield of 95.4% and strong superoxide anion radical production. Moreover, TMPB displays bio-responsive fluorescence and a synergistic antibacterial mechanism combining contact–mediated membrane disruption with light–triggered photodynamic inactivation.
