The multi-cationic nature of TMPB enables facile loading onto various fabric materials (T@Fabric), effectively blocking pathogen transmission via synergistic “capture–contact–photodynamic” functions, highlighting their promise for photodynamic antimicrobial fabrics. Overall, the machine learning techniques presented in this study offer an innovative and efficient approach for the data-driven screening and development of next-generation medical protective materials.

title: Adaptive direct ink writing of dual-curable, silica-filled rubber latex composites via a hybrid physics-machine learning framework
abstract: Additive manufacturing of high-performance filled rubber composites with industrially relevant mechanical and chemical performance remains a significant challenge, particularly at silica loadings required for stiffness, durability, and chemical resistance. This study presents a dual-curable waterborne latex-silica ink system that enables direct ink writing (DIW) of carboxylated styrene-butadiene rubber composites with up to 50 wt% silica, without compromising printability or final performance. The ink incorporates a photocurable N-vinylpyrrolidone/triethylene glycol divinyl ether interpenetrating network, which provides immediate green strength upon UV exposure, followed by a secondary ZnO-activated sulfur vulcanization step that constructs a robust polysulfidic network. Rheological characterization revealed tunable yield stress and shear-thinning behavior, which are suitable for extrusion across a wide composition range. To ensure consistent print fidelity across 30–50 wt% silica, a machine-learning-based adaptive viscous filament printing (ML-AVFP) framework was implemented;which uses experimentally determined rheological descriptors and filament-printing calibration data to automatically rewrite G-code with composition-specific Z-offset and print-speed profiles, thereby improving filament flattening and interlayer overlap, suppressing printing-induced porosity, and reducing final post-vulcanization shrinkage by ∼17–30% versus fixed-parameter DIW. The resulting dual-cured composites exhibited tensile strengths of up to 21 MPa, elongations approaching 800%, high toughness, low compression set from −40 to 100 °C, and excellent oil resistance. Functional components, such as gaskets, bellows, and brake diaphragms, were successfully printed withdense, pore-free microstructures and reliable performance under realistic mechanical and fluid-exposure conditions. This study establishes a scalable hybrid materials-process strategy for the digital manufacturing of industrially relevant elastomer parts via DIW.

title: Efficient electronic configuration and adsorption energy balance enabled by trimetallic nanozymes: Toward AI-powered visual identification of Pseudomonas aeruginosa
abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa (P. aeruginosa), a widespread multidrug-resistant pathogen, threatens public health through rapid transmission, high virulence, and resilient biofilm formation, resulting in significant mortality. Consequently, it is imperative to develop rapid, sensitive detection methods and efficient elimination strategies for P. aeruginosa. We synthesized durian-like Cu5Pd4Au NPs via a facile one-pot co-reduction strategy. Efficient electronic structure of Cu5Pd4Au NPs leads to balanced adsorption energy, endowing them with exceptional peroxidase-like activity (32.21 U/mg), which is 5.5-fold higher than that of Pd NPs. Leveraging the robust catalytic activity and high antibody-loading capacity, we constructed a multifunctional platform integrating immunoassays and antibacterial function. Combined with machine learning algorithms, the platform achieves rapid and sensitive discrimination of bacterial concentrations. Furthermore, Cu5Pd4Au NPs effectively eliminate multidrug-resistant bacteria and biofilms through synergistic reactive oxygen species generation and photothermal effects. This work not only provides a high-activity nanozyme but also establishes a new paradigm for designing multifunctional nanozymes.

title: Development and testing of a nanobubble-based hydrodynamic cavitation system
abstract: Emerging pollutants pose a significant challenge to conventional water and wastewater treatment technologies, highlighting the need for targeted and energy-efficient advanced oxidation processes. Although hydrodynamic cavitation (HC) has shown promising results, the potential of nanobubble-assisted HC remains largely unexplored. In this study, a specialized Venturi tube designed for nanobubble generation was developed and implemented in a pilot-scale (14 L) HC system for the degradation of humic acid (HA) and five active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) (climbazole, sulfadiazine, sulfamethazine, sulfapyridine, and venlafaxine). A response surface methodology (RSM) framework was applied to optimize the Venturi geometry, resulting in a high nanobubble fraction (ca. 90% < 1 μm), with a mean diameter of approximately 151 nm and a zeta potential of −15.4 mV. To further explore the design space, neural network modelling based on 10 prototypes was employed. The analysis revealed that reducing the throat diameter (D t ) to 0.5 mm could decrease the mean bubble diameter to approximately 90 nm, but with a four-fold reduction in hydraulic throughput (20 vs. 80 L/h), highlighting a critical trade-off between bubble size minimization and treatment capacity. In degradation tests, sodium persulfate (PS) consistently outperformed hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) as an auxiliary oxidant. PS-assisted HC achieved ca. 56–88% primary degradation of the tested APIs and ca. 60% mineralization for HA. This performance was governed via rapid oxidant activation within the first 5–15 min, followed by sustained hydroxyl radical generation driven by hydrodynamic cavitation. Notably, the system operated without external energy inputs such as UV irradiation or ultrasonic transducers. Consequently, nanobubble-assisted HC represents a scalable, reagent- and energy- efficient water and wastewater treatment process, capable of delivering performance comparable to more complex hybrid processes.

title: All-textile piezoelectric sensors for machine learning-enabled wearable muscle strength assessment in older adults
abstract: To meet the demand for early identification and dynamic assessment of age-related hand function decline, an all-textile integrated piezoelectric sensor based on PVDF-TrFE/MWCNTs composite nanofibers is developed. Using commercial silver fabric electrodes and in-situ electrospun nanofiber membranes, the sensor enables passive, accurate grip strength monitoring. MWCNTs improve the dielectric properties and charge collection efficiency, and increase the piezoelectric β-phase content from 85.5% to 90.4%. The sensor shows high sensitivity (126.03 mV/N), a wide working range (0.1–6 N), and good stability over 16,000 cycles. Integrated with deep learning, the hand motion monitoring system achieves high-precision motion recognition (R2 = 96.51%). Grip strength, control stability, and finger coordination are quantitatively evaluated on 10 young and 11 elderly subjects. This work provides a wearable strategy for early warning and rehabilitation assessment of hand function decline in the elderly, facilitating the application of flexible electronics in aging-related health management.

title: Digitalization of microbial electrosynthesis: Understanding operational variables for ethanol production optimization
abstract: Microbial electrosynthesis (MES) is a bioelectrochemical technology devoted to carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) conversion into value-added organic products. Traditionally, it has been addressed through trial-and-error approaches, with limited experimental data. This study introduces a data-driven framework to advance the MES digitalisation through systematic analysis of operational variables influencing CO 2 conversion. CO 2 conversion to acetic acid and ethanol was investigated in MES cells integrated within an automated bench-scale platform. It enabled real-time control of key operational variables, i.e. dissolved CO 2 , pH, and pressure, while monitoring electrical conductivity, cell voltage and temperature. The ethanol production rate was improved by 35% (14.80 g m −2 d −1 ), obtained controlling dissolved CO 2 at 100–300 mg L −1 , pH at 4.5–4.8 and pressure at 1.8 bar. Process data were analysed through pattern discovery (based on both operation and production variables) and unsupervised clustering (based solely on operational variables). The latter allowed to identify distinct operational phases, which matched the real production stages, solely based on operation variables. Principal component analysis revealed that acetic acid production was primarily dependent on dissolved CO 2 , with secondary contributions from pH and electrical conductivity. Electrical conductivity emerged as an identifying signal for ethanol production. The proposed data-based methodology elucidates the key variable interactions and supports phase-specific monitoring and control strategies for MES optimization in the absence of time-consuming, punctual product measurements. • Real-time operation control improved ethanol production rate by 35% in MES cells. • CO 2 limitation and pH acidification through fine control triggered solventogenesis. • SCFCM from operational data enabled process partition in product-selective phases. • EC signal dynamics are linked to ethanol selectivity in MES.

title: Machine-learning-enabled cross-selective VOC sensing in ionic-liquid-based printed gas sensors
abstract: Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) pose significant risks to indoor air quality and industrial safety, underscoring the need for fast, selective, and low-power monitoring technologies. Here, we develop a flexible, room-temperature sensing platform based on printable poly(vinylidene fluoride) films incorporating chemically diverse ionic liquids. The tailored polymer–ionic liquid interactions enable selective detection of structurally similar VOCs -acetone, isopropanol, and ethanol - using nanoparticle-free inks compatible with scalable additive manufacturing. Custom-designed capacitive transducers enhance sensitivity and produce rapid, stable responses suitable for continuous operation. A four-sensor array integrated with a low-cost Arduino acquisition system achieves response times below 60 s and recovery times below 10 s without external heating. Machine-learning models applied to the cross-selective outputs reach 99.89% classification accuracy and enable quantitative prediction of acetone and isopropanol at concentrations below their IDLH thresholds, and ethanol at levels relevant to long-term exposure guidelines. This platform offers an energy-efficient and scalable solution for indoor air-quality assessment and industrial VOC surveillance.

title: Machine learning-enabled sensor array using noble metal–functionalized WS 2 nanoflakes for drastic selective gas sensing
abstract: Noble-metal nanoparticle (NP) decoration has emerged as an effective strategy to enhance the performance of gas sensors, yet the underlying principles governing selectivity tuning remain poorly understood. In this study, we decorated two-dimensional (2D) tungsten disulfide (WS2) flakes with noble-metal NPs using a solution-based process without reducing agents, leading to a dramatic shift in selectivity. The decorated WS2 flakes enabled clear discrimination among nitrogen dioxide (NO2), ammonia (NH3), and hydrogen (H2), with a level of selectivity rarely observed in conventional three-dimensional metal-oxide nanostructures. This distinctive behavior originates from the synergy between the layered, edge-enriched architecture of WS2 and the catalytic/electronic effects of the noble-metal NPs. By integrating machine learning algorithms, we further demonstrate robust analyte classification and predictive capability across multiple gases. We propose a selective sensing mechanism based on charge-transfer interactions between target gas molecules and the functionalized sensing surface, which underpins the observed discriminative response. Our findings provide fundamental insights into the design of next-generation sensor arrays based on 2D materials, offering a strategic pathway for superior gas selectivity.

title: Nanotech-enabled and AI-driven paper-based analytical devices (PADs) for cancer screening: From material engineering to intelligent diagnostics
abstract: Paper-based lateral flow assays (LFIAs) have become a central platform for decentralized cancer diagnostics, offering rapid, low-cost testing that enables decentralized analysis. Over the past decade, substantial engineering advances have expanded the performance envelope of paper-supported tumor biomarker detection, driven primarily by the integration of functional nanomaterials with increasingly sophisticated device architectures. This review synthesizes these developments from a chemical engineering perspective, focusing on how surface-engineered nanomaterials (e.g., gold and magnetic nanoparticles, quantum dots) modulate mass transport, reaction kinetics, and signal transduction within porous cellulose matrices to enhance sensitivity and dynamic range. In parallel, smartphone-based optical readout systems, when integrated with machine learning algorithms, have proven effective in mitigating intrinsic signal variability and enabling objective, quantitative interpretation. Beyond analytical performance, we critically examine persistent engineering barriers to clinical translation, such as substrate heterogeneity, flow irreproducibility, reagent instability, and manufacturing scalability challenges. Accordingly, we outline a translational roadmap prioritizing robustness, standardization, and system-level design to accelerate the conversion of lab-on-paper prototypes into clinically deployable diagnostic tools.

title: Machine-learning-enabled starch/MXene moisture sensing bioelectronics for human monitoring and interaction
abstract: The drive toward sustainable sensors demands materials and manufacturing routes that deliver high sensing performance without generating persistent waste. We report a water-based, blade-coating process to fabricate starch/Ti 3 C 2 Tₓ MXene nanocomposite films that operate as multifunctional, moisture-responsive bioelectronics. The films form a layered conductive architecture with a Young's modulus of 6.4 GPa and tensile strength of 82.3 MPa at only 1.36 vol% MXene, exceeding the mechanical performance of previously reported biodegradable conductive films. The composite films display a low percolation threshold of 0.48 vol% and offer tuneable conductivity over 9.6 × 10 −4 to 0.48 S/m. In combination with exceptional humidity sensitivity (>700% ΔR/R 0 at 95% RH), these features enable high-performance multimodal moisture sensing, including respiration analysis, speech detection, skin hydration monitoring, and non-contact human–machine interaction (HMI). When integrated with machine-learning classification, a single transient sensor can accurately distinguish breathing patterns and recognise spoken words with 97% accuracy. In addition, the films exhibit moisture-driven actuation, excellent biocompatibility (cell viability >97%), and fully biodegrade in soil within 30 days. By combining scalable processing, intelligent sensing and transient functionality, this work positions biodegradable bioelectronics as a credible alternative to conventional wearable sensor technologies. • We demonstrate, for the first time, that humidity-induced resistance signals from natural-biopolymer based, transient films can be processed using machine learning to accurately classify breathing modes and spoken words, enabling AI-assisted physiological monitoring and HMI. • The biobased nanocomposite films exhibit exceptional humidity sensitivity (>700% ΔR/R₀ at 95% RH), enabling precise detection of moisture variations for respiration monitoring, speech recognition, skin-hydration assessment, and contactless control of a smart-car. • In addition, the films combine a low percolation threshold (0.48 vol%), tuneable conductivity, and high mechanical strength (82.3 MPa), ensuring stable electrical performance and mechanical integrity during repeated operation. • The devices fully biodegrade in soil within a month, addressing the rapidly growing challenge of electronic waste from disposable sensors and short-lifetime wearables.

title: Electrochemically enhanced anaerobic ammonia oxidation: Performance prediction and mechanism elucidation based on big data and machine learning
abstract: Anaerobic ammonia oxidation (anammox) is a promising energy-efficient biological nitrogen removal technology, but its widespread application is constrained by slow bacterial growth, prolonged startup periods, and strict dependency on nitrite. This study systematically investigated the enhancement effects of applied voltage on biofilm-based anammox systems using big data analysis and machine learning (ML) approaches. Over 800 sets of literature data were collected and analyzed, revealing that nitrogen removal rate (NRR) increased 3.45-fold at optimal voltage (0.4–0.5 V) compared to non-voltage control. Four ML algorithms (Random Forest, Gradient Boosting Regression, eXtreme Gradient Boosting, and Categorical Boosting) were employed to develop predictive models for the NRR. The Categorical Boosting model exhibited superior performance, achieving R2 values of 0.974 and 0.852 for the training and testing sets, respectively. SHAP analysis identified applied voltage as the critical influencing factor, while partial dependence plots revealed its nonlinear regulatory effects and the synergistic interactions among multiple features. A 106-day continuous reactor experiment validated the model's effectiveness: at the predicted optimal voltage of 0.4 V, the system achieved an NRR of 720 mg N/(L·d) with a nitrogen removal efficiency of 87%. Notably, the system maintained stable performance even with a 24% reduction in influent nitrite concentration, alleviating the inherent nitrite dependency of anammox processes. Microbial community analysis revealed that anaerobic ammonium-oxidizing bacteria maintained 80% contribution ratio, significantly higher than other functional bacteria, confirming the strong activation effect of applied voltage. This study confirms the core role of ML in precise performance prediction and key parameter identification, providing data-driven support for the identification of optimal conditions, intelligent control, and scaled application of electrochemically enhanced anammox processes.

title: Exploration of salivary biomarkers for accurate diagnosis of anxiety, depression, and somatic symptom disorder by the integration of microfluidic chip and machine learning
abstract: Depression represents a major global public health concern, affecting hundreds of millions of individuals worldwide. The World Health Organization forecasts that, by 2030, depression will emerge as the primary driver of the global healthcare challenge. Consequently, the identification of biomarkers specific to anxiety (ANX), depression (DEP), and somatic symptom disorder (SSD) is crucial for early and accurate diagnosis and timely treatment. Here, we explicited a diagnosis model to screen the patients by a salivary biomarkers panel in the of a cohort consisting of healthy individuals and patients with ANX, DEP, and SSD, through a microfluidic chip. The detection results show that the expression levels of inflammatory cytokines were elevated in patients compared with healthy individuals. A four-biomarker panel was employed to train the machine learning (ML) model (M4D) based on the random forest (RF) algorithm for early and accurate differential diagnosis, which includes tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleukin-8 (IL-8), interleukin-1β (IL-1β) and Interferon-gamma (IFN-γ). It can identify the specific type of mental disorder for an individual with AUC > 0.98, without invasive procedures. The diagnostic accuracy in the test set reached 92.22%. The proposed non-invasive diagnostic method presents promising applications in making precise diagnosis of mental disorders.

title: Photocatalytic hydrogen production: Materials design, system engineering, and data-driven advances
abstract: Photocatalytic hydrogen production offers a sustainable solar-to‑hydrogen conversion route by splitting water under light irradiation. However, most systems remain confined to laboratory conditions because of limited efficiency, stability, and scalability. This review provides an overview of how materials design, system engineering, and data-driven tools can be integrated to advance photocatalytic hydrogen production toward practical deployment. Fundamental strategies for improving solar-to‑hydrogen efficiency are first summarized, focusing on band-structure modulation, charge-carrier dynamics, surface catalytic-site optimization, and stability enhancement. Representative photocatalyst families—including metal oxides, metal sulfides, MOFs, MXenes, and their heterostructures—are discussed in terms of how S-scheme and Z-scheme architectures, cocatalyst loading, facet control, and defect engineering collectively govern light absorption, charge separation, and reaction kinetics. Beyond powder suspensions, approaches such as photothermal catalysis, photoelectrocatalysis, magnetic-field-assisted photocatalysis, and photobiocatalytic systems that couple biological components with inorganic photocatalysts are highlighted. Emphasis is placed on the role of artificial intelligence in accelerating materials discovery, elucidating structure–property–performance relationships, and guiding reactor and process optimization. By linking mechanistic insights with system-level design and using quantitative performance indicators such as AQE and STH, this review outlines a framework for developing efficient, durable, and scalable photocatalytic hydrogen production technologies suitable for real-world deployment.

title: Loofah-inspired recyclable MXene/polypyrrole fiber-skeleton hydrogels for machine-learning-assisted multimodal flexible sensor
abstract: Flexible hydrogel sensors that are strong, multimodal, and recyclable are highly desirable for wearable electronics but remain difficult to realize because conventional conductive gels are mechanically isotropic, single responsive, and structurally fragile. Here, we report a loofah-inspired recyclable MXene/polypyrrole (PPy) fiber-skeleton hydrogel (PBMA) constructed from PPy, bacterial cellulose (BC) fibers, a poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA)/tannic acid (TA) matrix, and well-dispersed Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene, in which directional freeze-thaw processing generated an aligned loofah-like porous architecture with anisotropic mechanical and conductive pathways. The resulting hydrogel simultaneously achieves high tensile strength (~1.8 MPa), large toughness (~6 MJ·m−3), and stretchability up to ~250%, while exhibiting low hysteresis and durable piezoresistive response over 5000 loading–unloading cycles. PBMA functions as a multimodal strain–humidity sensor with a gauge factor (GF) up to 4.66, fast electromechanical response/recovery (~160 ms), and humidity sensitivity over 10–80% RH with ~10 s response time. Benefiting from strong adhesion, antibacterial activity, and thermal reprocessability that retained over 90% of its original sensing performance, PBMA enables long-term conformal monitoring of physiological motions, respiration and ambient humidity, Morse-code communication, object-diameter and spatial pressure mapping, and machine-learning-assisted gesture recognition with 99.75% accuracy. This loofah-inspired fiber-skeleton design provides a sustainable route to high-performance, recyclable hydrogel electronic skins.

title: Kinetic modeling and machine-learning optimization of a novel three-stage fluidized-bed gasifier for hydrogen-rich and low-tar syngas production
abstract: Biomass gasification remains a key pathway for clean fuel production; however, conventional fluidized-bed reactors continue to suffer from limited carbon conversion and persistent tar formation, constraining system efficiency and industrial adoption. This study introduces a novel three-stage fluidized-bed gasifier—integrating controlled devolatilization, high-temperature steam/air reforming, and char gasification—to simultaneously enhance syngas quality and suppress tar generation. A kinetics-based Aspen Plus model was developed and rigorously validated against experimental data. To capture multivariate interactions across operating conditions, Design of Experiments (DOE) and Response Surface Methodology (RSM) were coupled with Support Vector Regression (SVR), significantly outperforming classical regression in predictive accuracy. Multi-objective optimization using NSGA-II identified Pareto-optimal trade-offs among cold gas efficiency (CGE), carbon conversion efficiency (CCE), and tar yield. Results demonstrate that increasing the reformer temperature from 1050 to 1200 °C elevates CGE from 82% to 92% and boosts CCE from 88% to 97%, while reducing tar yield from 4 to 0.3%. The optimized operating window yields hydrogen-rich syngas (up to 27% H₂) with an LHV of 7.75 MJ/Nm3, alongside near-complete carbon conversion and minimal tar yield (<0.1%). Overall, the proposed three-stage configuration—supported by advanced kinetic modeling and machine-learning-assisted optimization—establishes a robust platform for high-efficiency, low-tar biomass-to‑hydrogen conversion, offering strong potential for deployment in next-generation renewable energy and low-carbon fuel systems.

title: A bioinspired electronic skin with orthogonal hydrogel and cascaded deep learning for decoupling tangential force and deformation mapping
abstract: Human skin interprets physical contact by jointly sensing surface deformation and multidimensional forces, a dual-vector capability that underpins dexterous interaction. However, existing robotic tactile sensors fundamentally lack this dual-vector perception, failing to capture simultaneously both tangential forces and deformation fields. Prompted by this gap, we present a bioinspired electronic skin (e-skin) for the high-precision perception of tangential forces and deformation fields. Inspired by the mechano-transduction pathway of Ruffini corpuscles, the e-skin features an orthogonal hydrogel grid architecture to mimic this transduction mechanism. We further employ a cascaded deep regression framework to reverse-engineer this transduction, forming a “sensing” and “perception” integrated paradigm. Crucially, this biomimetic e-skin first reconstructs deformation vectors (ΔX, ΔY) with high fidelity (MAE < 0. 5423 mm, R2 > 0.9955) over a ± 20 mm range, then infers tangential forces (Fx, Fy) from the estimated deformations with remarkable accuracy (MAE < 0.247 N, R2 > 0.9931) within ± 7.5 N. Validated through deformation field reconstruction and human-robot interaction, this system is capable of perceiving nuanced physical interactions, enabling a robot to interpret interaction intentions.

title: Data-driven discovery of high-performance surface passivators for efficient and stable perovskite solar cells
abstract: Effective passivation of interface defect is vital for improving perovskite solar cell (PSC) performance. Traditional trial-and-error methods to identify passivators represent slow, costly, and dependent on expert input, limiting thorough exploration of potential candidates. This study introduces an automated platform, “MatInsight”, to extract key PSC parameters from literature, creating a dataset for training seven machine learning (ML) models. The categorical boosting (CatBoost) model excelled as the top predictor, identifying influential molecular descriptors—dihedral angle (Phi), topological complexity (BertzCT), molar refractivity (MolMR), and minimum absolute EState index (MinAbsEStateIndex)—for optimizing power conversion efficiency (PCE). We predicted passivation efficacy within a molecular library, followed by experimental validation. Notably, PSCs using 3-fluoro-4-aminobenzonitrile (FABN) demonstrated superior defect passivation, achieving a PCE of 25.7% and maintaining 84% efficiency over 1400 h in ambient conditions. This scalable approach offers a robust framework for rapidly identifying effective passivators, significantly advancing the development of stable, high-efficiency PSCs.

title: Machine learning-driven COD real-time monitoring electrochemical analysis system based on nitrogen-etched boron-doped diamond electrode
abstract: Industrial development and urban expansion exert considerable ecological pressure due to organic wastewater discharge, necessitating fast, real-time water-quality monitoring to oversee treatment processes and warn against unsafe discharge. In this study, a miniaturized electrochemical (EC) detector and artificial intelligence (AI)-based real-time water quality analysis software were developed to monitor organic components, concentrations, and chemical oxygen demand (COD) in wastewater. A nitrogen-etched boron-doped diamond (NBDD) sensing electrode, with a surface composed of relatively intact (100) diamond planes and graphene-covered nanocrystals, was employed. This electrode demonstrated high responsiveness, electrocatalytic activity, and long-term stability toward all six dyes (carmine, methylene blue, methylene green, basic fuchsin, rhodamine B, and indigo). The AI software employed principal component analysis (PCA) for dimensionality reduction; support vector machine (SVM) for dye classification; and a fusion algorithm (iterative reweighted least squares (IRLS)/multilayer perceptron (MLP)/gradient boosting machine (GBM)) for predicting COD and concentration. It achieved dye identification accuracies ranging from 82.7% to 100%. The NBDD-EC detector combined with the AI analysis system achieved high correlations between the predicted and actual values of dye concentration and COD. When deployed industrially, it predicted dye wastewater COD with 96 ± 2% accuracy, providing a reliable hardware-software solution for real-time monitoring, crucial for discharge oversight.

title: Dynamic optimization of coke formation in dry reforming of methane using a neural quasi-steady-state model
abstract: This work develops a microkinetic-surrogate-based dynamic optimization framework for identifying coke-aware operating strategies in dry reforming of methane. A neural quasi-steady-state model (NQSSM) is introduced in which the fast-reacting species are predicted using an artificial neural network, while coke coverage is retained as an ordinary differential equation(ODE) state. This structure enables transient system prediction at a fraction of the computational cost of the full microkinetic model, thereby allowing dynamic optimization that accounts for catalyst deactivation. Bayesian optimization is integrated with the NQSSM to efficiently determine dynamic operating schedules that maximize performance. Dynamic optimization under multiple coke constraints on reactor coke coverage reveals a clear trade-off between syngas production and coke accumulation. This trade-off is quantified by a weighted syngas performance index (WSPI), which is introduced in this research to reflect the productivity of H2 and CO and the consumption of CH4 and CO2 over time. With tighter constraints, the optimal operating regime shifts toward more oxidation-favoring conditions. This shift manifests systematically in the optimal profiles, including decreasing temperature, increasing pressure, and reduced early-stage flow rate. The NQSSM accurately captures these time-dependent strategic adjustments while preserving mechanistic interpretability. Overall, the proposed framework provides a mechanistically grounded and computationally efficient approach for designing degradation-aware operating strategies and can be readily extended to other reaction systems in which dynamic behavior and catalyst deactivation are closely coupled.

title: Crosstalk-free dual-mode electronic skin enabled by selective electrospinning and machine learning-based decoupling
abstract: Electronic skins play a crucial role in health monitoring, human motion detection, and soft robotics. Nevertheless, achieving an integrated dual-mode electronic skin using compatible and simplified processes while reducing crosstalk between different sensing signals remains a significant challenge. This study developed dual-mode electronic skin using selective electrospinning deposition of functional layers for pressure and temperature sensing. The electronic skin consists of two parts: a top layer based on electrospun polyvinylidene fluoride-trifluoroethylene (PVDF-TrFE) nanofibers sandwiched between interlocked mortise-tenon structured electrodes for pressure sensing; and a bottom layer based on PVDF-TrFE and silver nanowires (AgNWs) for temperature sensing. The mortise-tenon structured electrode design and selective-deposition electrospun nanofiber significantly enhances the piezoelectric response. Each layer is process-compatible and specific structures are set up according to the different signals collected, thus achieving excellent sensing performance. The electronic skin utilizes two different sensing mechanisms with dual-parameter decoupling method, which successfully eliminate cross-sensitivity interference between temperature and pressure. The system inherently corrects for the temperature coefficient of the pressure signal, yielding higher accuracy than single-parameter sensors. Furthermore, an intelligent decoupling optimization algorithm via machine-learning is introduced to enable high-precision decoupling pressure and temperature stimuli to identify different materials like human perception of touch.

title: Learning from limited data and feedback for cell culture process monitoring: A comparative study
abstract: In cell culture bioprocessing, real-time batch process monitoring (BPM) refers to the continuous tracking and analysis of key process variables – such as viable cell density, nutrient levels, metabolite concentrations, and product titer – throughout the duration of a batch run. This enables early detection of deviations and supports timely control actions to ensure optimal cell growth and product quality. BPM plays a critical role in ensuring the quality and regulatory compliance of biopharmaceutical manufacturing processes. However, the development of accurate soft sensors for BPM is hindered by key challenges, including limited historical data, infrequent feedback, heterogeneous process conditions, and high-dimensional sensory inputs. This study presents a comprehensive benchmarking analysis of machine learning (ML) methods designed to address these challenges, with a focus on learning from historical data with limited volume and relevance in the context of bioprocess monitoring. We evaluate multiple ML approaches – including feature dimensionality reduction, online learning, and just-in-time learning – across three datasets, one in silico dataset and two real-world experimental datasets. Our findings highlight the importance of training strategies in handling limited data and feedback, with batch learning proving effective in homogeneous settings, while just-in-time learning and online learning demonstrate superior adaptability in cold-start scenarios. Additionally, we identify key meta-features, such as feed media composition and process control strategies, that significantly impact model transferability. The results also suggest that integrating Raman-based predictions with lagged offline measurements enhances monitoring accuracy, offering a promising direction for future bioprocess soft sensor development.

title: Autonomous characterisation of fouling-free feasible operating regions in continuous flow precipitation of ketoprofen nanoparticles
abstract: Continuous antisolvent precipitation enables efficient pharmaceutical manufacturing but is susceptible to fouling, which disrupts operation and compromises product quality. To address this challenge, we developed and validated a closed-loop, autonomous screening platform for identifying non-fouling conditions in continuous antisolvent precipitation, demonstrated for ketoprofen nanoparticle formation in a confined impinging jet reactor using ethanol as solvent, water as antisolvent, and Kollidon VA 64 (PVP/VA) as additive. The platform integrates real-time, pressure drop-based fouling detection with adaptive experimental design. Initially, it performs design of experiments to generate feasibility labels (fouling or non-fouling). A class balancing strategy then targets under-represented regions, and active learning with Gaussian Process (GP) classification selects subsequent experiments to reduce uncertainty in feasibility prediction. With an experimental budget of 50 precipitation experiments, the system autonomously mapped the boundary separating fouling and non-fouling regions across three key process variables: total volume flow rate (1–11 mL min −1 ), antisolvent-to-solvent volume flow rate ratio (4–10), and drug-to-additive mass ratio (0.2125–4.25). The resulting GP classifier achieved high prediction accuracy with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) greater than 0.8 in cross-validation experiments and an AUC of 1.0 in a set of eight follow-up validation experiments. The methodology revealed complex interactions between process conditions and fouling behaviour, identifying robust non-fouling operating windows. This autonomous framework provides a systematic and efficient approach for fouling detection and operating region characterisation in continuous pharmaceutical precipitation, reducing development effort and improving process reliability.

title: Competitive adsorption performance of volatile organic compounds on ZSM-5: Key influence factors and mechanisms
abstract: The zeolite rotor-regenerative thermal oxidizer (RTO) system has been widely applied to control volatile organic compounds (VOCs) emissions from automotive coating processes. Zeolite selection was crucial for treatment efficiency. Given fluctuations in VOC emissions, this selection was influenced by the ZSM-5 characteristics, VOCs types and competition among these VOCs. Herein, the key influencing factors and mechanisms for competitive adsorption of typical VOCs (butyl acetate, acetone and aromatic hydrocarbons) on ZSM-5 with varying Si/Al ratio was investigated by correlation analysis, LightGBM model with SHapley Additive exPlanation and molecular simulation. The competition between components, determined by adsorption strength and sites of VOC molecules, was identified as the key factor. Among these VOCs, butyl acetate, with the strongest adsorption force, always dominated the adsorption process, while acetone and aromatic hydrocarbons showed weaker adsorption and were significantly influenced by inter-component competition. The competitive intensity also depended on adsorption sites of VOCs on ZSM-5, which was related to the Si/Al ratio. At Si/Al < 150, butyl acetate shared fewer adsorption sites with these weaker-adsorbed VOCs resulting in relatively weak competition, which made this ZSM-5 suitable for aromatic hydrocarbon-rich exhaust. At Si/Al ≥ 150, extensive overlap between the adsorption sites for butyl acetate and weaker-adsorbed VOCs contributed to high selectivity of butyl acetate, making this ZSM-5 effective for ester-dominant exhaust. These will provide theoretical guidance for selecting and regulating zeolites to efficiently treat different VOC components.

title: Neural network-based multi-objective optimization of a biomass polygeneration system with chemical looping carbon dioxide displacement of nitrogen
abstract: Efficient and cost-effective utilization of biomass is crucial for mitigating energy and environmental pressures. This study proposes a new biomass polygeneration system integrating chemical looping carbon dioxide displacement of nitrogen (CLCDN) for simultaneous electricity and fuel gas production. In the proposed system, high-temperature O2 and CO2 mixtures produced by the CLCDN process are used as the gasifying agent, and externally concentrated solar energy supplies the heat required for gasification. A neural network-based multi-objective optimization model is developed to improve exergy and exergoeconomic performance, and enhance syngas quality. The model development involves two stages. First, Bayesian optimization is employed to determine the optimal hyperparameters of a multilayer perceptron (MLP). Then, multi-objective optimization is conducted using the trained MLP model. Under optimal hyperparameters, the MLP achieves a coefficient of determination of 0.99. The optimization results indicate that the proposed system achieves optimal performance at a CLCDN reaction temperature of 841.34 °C, a CO2 to biomass mass flow ratio of 0.44, and a gasification temperature of 1016.14 °C. Compared with the reference system, the exergy efficiency (74.09%) and effective carbon efficiency (99.49%) increase by 2.19% and 33.17%, respectively. Meanwhile, the CO2 mass flow rate in syngas decreases by 2.514 ton/h, while the unit exergy cost of total products (0.019 $/kWh) increases by 5.56%. Overall, the proposed system enables efficient biomass gasification and improves syngas quality. The developed optimization framework provides a theoretical basis for system design and performance improvement.

title: Accurate and expandable graph deep learning for accelerating predictive identification of high-potential organic photovoltaics
abstract: Organic photovoltaics (OPVs) are a leading renewable energy technology, yet the discovery of high-performance non-fullerene acceptors (NFAs) is often hindered by the vastness of chemical space and the synthetic costs of complex fused-ring systems. In this study, we develop a robust, physics-informed graph deep learning framework based on a directed message passing neural network (D-MPNN) to accelerate the predictive identification of high-potential OPVs. By representing molecules as fragment-level graphs enriched with computable descriptors—including DFT-derived frontier orbital energies and molecular mechanics-calculated structural parameters—our model achieves excellent predictive accuracy, yielding a Pearson correlation coefficient (r) of 0.93 and a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.89% under 10-fold cross-validation. The model's capability was rigorously validated through a temporal “blind” test of 42 newly reported NFA ternary OPV devices (published after model training), where it maintained a high predictive accuracy (MAE = 1.17%) even for systems containing novel molecular fragments. Leveraging this framework, we performed high-throughput virtual screening (HTVS) of approximately 334 million ternary combinations, identifying 4904 novel systems with predicted power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) surpassing the training dataset ceiling of 19.36%. Furthermore, fragment-level Z-score analyses identified key structural motifs, such as specific non-fused rigid cores and the benefit of “No-p-spacer” architecture, providing actionable design rules for experimental development. This accurate and expandable framework offers a powerful platform for the predictive identification of high-potential ternary OPVs.

title: AI-guided discovery of an efficient chitinase enables green production of chitobioses with distinct cadmium stress-alleviating efficacy in rice
abstract: Abiotic stresses, particularly heavy metal contamination, induce excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) in plants, causing oxidative damage and severe crop yield losses. Structurally defined chitobioses are promising natural antioxidants hold great promise as biostimulants to enhance plant stress tolerance in sustainable agriculture. However, their green, cost-effective synthesis remains a bottleneck. Here, we employed an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven structure-based enzyme mining strategy to identify a thermostable, highly specific endochitinase (CT10) from Paenibacillus elgii, which efficiently hydrolyzes low-cost colloidal crustacean chitin into N, N′-Diacetylchitobiose (GlcNAcβ1-4GlcNAc, AA) with minimal byproducts. Coupling CT10 with regioselective chitin deacetylases (VcCDA/NodB) in one-pot cascade reaction yielded three additional structurally defined chitobioses: GlcNAcβ1-4GlcN (AD), GlcNβ1-4GlcNAc (DA), and GlcNβ1-4GlcN (DD), all with >95% purity. Among these, DA exhibits superior hydroxyl radical (OH•) scavenging activity comparable to l-ascorbic acid. Exogenous application of the four chitobioses alleviated cadmium (Cd) stress in rice (Oryza sativa L.), restoring growth, reducing ROS/MDA accumulation, and upregulating antioxidant enzyme genes (sod, pod, cat). Notably, DA showed the most potent efficacy in promoting root biomass recovery and activating antioxidant defense pathways. This study establishes a scalable, green platform for the synthesis of structurally defined chitobioses and delineates their structure-specific roles in alleviating heavy metal toxicity, providing a nature-based strategy to improve crop resilience in abiotic stress-affected agricultural systems.

title: High mechanical-sensing hydrogels coupled with machine learning for acoustic signal recognition
abstract: Flexible wearable electronic devices and engineering require that functional materials have the characteristics of strong mechanical adaptability, high sensing sensitivity and system integration capability. Hydrogels have broad application prospects in this field due to their inherent biocompatibility and flexibility of tissue simulation. However, traditional hydrogels are limited in their large-scale and engineering applications due to their core limitations, including elusive mechanical sensing balance, limited functionality and inadequate system integration. In order to solve these key shortcomings, a design strategy combining covalent-non-covalent synergistic crosslinking and ion regulation for the preparation of P(AM-co-AA-co-CAVIm)/HEC composite hydrogels is developed. The obtained materials combine the covalent bond stability with the energy dissipation and microenvironment modulation capabilities of dynamic non-covalent interactions, thus establishing an optimized structural framework to enhance the mechanical and sensing performance. The resultant PMAIH-3 hydrogel achieves an elongation at break of 3204.58% and a tensile strength of 512.9 kPa, alongside segmented linear sensing responses (GF1 = 3.18, GF2 = 10.1), rapid response dynamics of 0.36 s, and stable operation over 200 cycles, effectively overcoming the inherent compromise of traditional hydrogels. Further integration of the hydrogel’s sensing capabilities with machine learning enables the construction of a voice-authentication system that delivers accurate sound signal capture and high-precision performance across multiple users. Collectively, this integrated material-system approach furnishes a powerful platform for advancing high-performance intelligent wearable bioelectronic devices.

title: Machine learning-assisted dual-mode sensing array: NIR-enhanced Cu-Co3O4 nanozymes for high-throughput antioxidant discrimination
abstract: Antioxidants play a critical role in sustaining physiological balance, making the rapid and accurate identification of multiple antioxidants essential for disease diagnosis and analysis. Conventional single-mode sensing arrays often suffer from inefficiency and inconsistency. Addressing this challenge, we engineered Cu-doped Co3O4 nanozymes (Cu-Co3O4) with tunable doping ratios using a self-templating approach. By integrating the optimized Cu-Co3O4 nanozyme with near-infrared (NIR) irradiation, we developed a dual-mode sensing platform that combines colorimetric and photothermal signals for high-throughput, precise antioxidant detection. Under NIR exposure, Cu-Co3O4 demonstrates significantly enhanced catalytic oxidation of TMB, driven by synergistic non-radiative relaxation and redox reactions of photogenerated carriers, amplifying both chromogenic and photothermal responses. Leveraging the distinct reducing capacities of various antioxidants on oxidized TMB (oxTMB), our sensing array—combined with machine learning—effectively processes unique response patterns. Linear discriminant analysis enabled the discrimination and quantification of key antioxidants, including ascorbic acid, dopamine, uric acid, glutathione, and melatonin, while hierarchical clustering and random forest algorithms validated methodological accuracy. Notably, the random forest model successfully predicted component concentrations in binary antioxidant mixtures. This study not only advances the strategic modulation of enzyme-like activity and photothermal properties in transition metal oxides but also establishes a robust framework for high-throughput target analysis in complex matrixes.

title: Bioleaching of critical minerals from marine sediments by indigenous microbial communities: Experimental and predictive analysis
abstract: Marine sediments represent a valuable source for critical minerals that prompts growing research interest in their potential for sustainable resource recovery. This study investigated the impact of bioleaching microorganisms, evaluating three different microbial inocula: sediment indigenous Fe-oxidizing bacteria, sediment indigenous Fe- and S-oxidizing bacteria, and Acidhiobacillus ferrooxidans. Key operational parameters including initial pH (2.0-7.0), energy source availability (Fe and S), and total solids content (5-10%) were also systematically varied to optimize bioleaching efficiency. The highest metal bioleaching for Al, Mg, and K was achieved using Fe- and S-oxidizing bacteria enriched from the marine sediment. The maximum concentrations in the leachate were detected as 806 mg/L (17.6%), 506 mg/L (65.7%), and 169 mg/L (22%) for Al, Mg and K, respectively. Alicyclobacillaceae was one of the key microorganisms which dominated microbial community over time. On the other hand, Sulfuristis played a key role in the early shifts in the microbial community. Additionally, Least Square Boosting (LSBoost), Random Forest Regression (RF), and Linear Regression (LR) were employed to evaluate the influence of experimental variables. All models demonstrated predictive performance for critical mineral release from the sediment, with LSBoost showing superior predictive accuracy.

title: Machine learning-assisted property prediction and virtual screening of polyimides for flexible electronic applications
abstract: Polyimides (PIs) are indispensable high-performance polymers for advanced flexible electronics, owing to their remarkable thermal stability, mechanical strength, and optical properties. To accelerate the design of colorless, transparent, and thermally stable PIs, this work introduces a machine learning (ML)-driven inverse design framework. By integrating molecular fingerprinting with ML models, we first developed accurate quantitative structure-property relationship (QSAR) models. Gradient Boosting (GB) model with RDKit fingerprints was identified as the optimal predictor (R2 > 0.94) for optical absorption (λmax), charge transfer (CTe), and thermal decomposition temperature (Td5). SHAP interpretability analysis further elucidated the roles of key substructures such as flexible ether linkers, fluorinated groups and conjugated structure. Guided by polycondensation chemistry, PIs disassembled into dianhydride (A) and diamine (B) building units and combinatorially expanded through flexible ether linkages (O) to create a virtual library consisting of 1530 AB-type and 175,664 ABOC-ype hypothetical monomers. High-throughput screening under stringent criteria (λmax < 400 nm, CTe < 0.2 e, Td5 > 530 °C) using a multi-task learning sparse encoder (MTL-SE) model successfully identified top candidates, including the outstanding h-BPDA-162 and 287 high-performance h-ABOC-type PI monomers. This work provides a scalable computational framework and specific structural guidelines as leads for the rational design and synthesis of advanced PI materials.

title: Machine learning-driven lipase engineering for highly enantioselective synthesis of chiral florfenicol intermediate via enzymatic resolution-chemical racemization coupling system
abstract: (2S,3R)-p-methylsulfonylphenyl serine ethyl ester [(2S,3R)-p-MPSE], a key chiral building block of the aryl β-hydroxy-α-amino ester family, serves as one of the critical intermediates for the synthesis of the veterinary antibiotic florfenicol. Kinetic resolution of rac-threo-p-MPSE by lipases represents a highly promising route. However, low catalytic efficiency of natural enzymes restricted its application. In this study, a lipase BSL from Bacillus subtilis was mined and rational design was performed to obtain a series of mutants. A robust Partial Least Squares (PLS) regression model, integrated with multi-dimensional encoding from the Amino Acid Index Database (AAindex) and Fast Fourier Transform (FFT)-based data processing technology, was constructed and trained. Using this machine learning (ML)-driven enzyme engineering approach, a mutant E115F/L67D/I421Q/P317I was successfully created, showing a 15.4-fold increase in catalytic efficiency (kcat/Km). Under the load of 1 M high substrate concentration, this mutant could achieve complete resolution of rac-threo-p-MPSE within 4 h, yielding optically pure (2S,3R)-p-MPSE (e.e.s > 99%) with a yield of 97.4% (based on the theoretical amount of single enantiomer). Additionally, the inactive isomer (2R,3S)-p-methylsulfonylphenyl serine [(2R,3S)-p-MPS] was recycled via chemical racemization based on a reversible retro-aldol cleavage mechanism and re-esterification, which facilitated the recycling of the substrate. This study not only breaks through the bottleneck of low catalytic efficiency of natural lipases through a machine learning-mediated precise enzyme engineering strategy, but also establishes a high-benefit chiral preparation process for (2S,3R)-p-MPSE via an enzymatic resolution-chemical racemization coupling system.

title: Machine-learning-assisted cancer detection and classification based on selective CTC capture and sequential in situ biomarkers quantification by polyvalent dual-aptamer DNA hydrogel
abstract: Early and accurate cancer classification based on circulating tumor cells (CTCs) is limited by inefficient enrichment, release-induced perturbation, and the lack of integrated strategies for cell-resolved multimodal biomarker analysis, particularly for aggressive subtypes such as triple-negative breast cancer (TN-BC). Herein, we report a unified engineering platform based on polyvalent dual-aptamer (PDApt)-DNA hydrogel that enables selective CTC encapsulation and sequential in situ quantification of membrane-bound and intracellular biomarkers without cell release or lysis. The PDApt-DNA hydrogel is constructed from two rolling-circle-amplified strands bearing polyvalent aptamers, enabling efficient and broad-spectrum CTC capture. Surface-enhanced Raman scattering/fluorescence (SERS/FL) nanoprobes are programmably organized within the three-dimensional (3D) hydrogel network via DNA hybridization, allowing in situ detection of epithelial cell adhesion molecule (EpCAM) on the cell membrane by SERS and intracellular microRNA-21 (miRNA-21) by FL. The 3D encapsulation increases z-axis electromagnetic hot-spot density, thereby enhancing SERS performance while preserving cellular viability. A two-step linear discriminant analysis (LDA) framework is further established by integrating three CTC-associated features, namely CTC count, membrane-bound EpCAM expression, and intracellular miRNA-21 expression, to enable cancer discrimination in the first step and subtype stratification in the second step. In a cohort of 31 participants, the platform enables effective separation between cancer and healthy samples and clear identification of TN-BC (100% sensitivity and 100% specificity). Overall, this work establishes a non-release, multimodal CTC engineering strategy that couples gentle enrichment of CTCs with in situ biomarkers quantification, providing a generalizable framework for CTC-based precision diagnostics and clinical stratification.

title: Synthetic data-driven prediction and interpretation of biomethane production in direct interspecies electron transfer-stimulated anaerobic digestion process
abstract: Direct interspecies electron transfer (DIET) simulation has emerged as an effective strategy to enhance methane production in anaerobic digestion (AD). However, reliable prediction and interpretation of DIET-AD performance remain challenging due to nonlinearity and limited experimental datasets. In this study, we propose an integrated, synthetic data-assisted machine learning (ML) framework to predict methane enhancement in magnetite-mediated DIET-AD systems, combining data augmentation, robust modeling, and experimental validation. The synthetic dataset was generated by generative adversarial network (GAN), which was rigorously validated from statistical, principal component, clustering analysis, and Kolmogorov–Smirov test to ensure consistency with original experimental data. Multiple ML models, including ensemble-based, neural network-based, and attention- based algorithms, were systematically evaluated. Among them, an attention-based algorithm showed superior performance and robustness, achieving an average coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.92, root mean squared error (RMSE) of 6.30, and mean absolute error (MAE) of 4.04 on test data. Explainable artificial intelligence analysis using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) indicated that substrate concentration and magnetite dosage were dominant drivers of methane enhancement. Experimental biomethane potential (BMP) tests further confirmed model reliability, with observed enhancements of 5.1% and 15.8% falling within the predicted 95% confidence intervals of 3.5–6.6% and 15.6–21.3%, respectively. Therefore, this framework contributes to practical insight into a transferable strategy for robust prediction, interpretation, and experimental guidance of nonlinear bioprocesses under data-scarce conditions.

title: S/N induced coordination isomerism hydrogels on 3D-printed device for machine learning-assisted multiplex detection of heavy metal ions
abstract: A portable hydrogel-based colorimetric sensing material integrated with machine learning analysis has been developed for the simultaneous on-site sensing of five toxic heavy metal ions (Cd2+, Pb2+, Hg2+, Cr6+, As3+). This capability stems from atomically designed hydrogels that enable visual recognition of metal ions through coordination differences. Notably, coordination-isomerism-driven differential recognition enables the simultaneous detection of these five ions. Three hydrogel sensing units (HP1, HP2, HP3) are synthesized via Ba2+ coordination of sodium alginate (SA) backbone molecule (Pr2) with response molecules (Pr4, Pr6, Pr8) featuring thiocyanate (–S–C≡N) and isothiocyanate (–N=C=S) groups. These units are spatially arranged in a 3D-printed device. The dominant coordination sites are S atoms in HP1 and HP3, whereas the dominant coordination site in HP2 is the N atom. Smartphone-captured RGB signals are converted into Euclidean distance (d-value) and processed using the machine-learning technique of linear discriminant analysis (LDA), achieving multiplex quantification with detection limits of 3.76 nM (Cd2+), 6.33 nM (Pb2+), 4.19 nM (Hg2+), 7.84 nM (Cr6+), and 6.42 nM (As3+) across a linear range of 0.01 to 5 μM for all five heavy metal ions. The platform demonstrates exceptional specificity against interferents and robust discrimination for binary to quinary heavy metal mixtures. This integration of rationally designed hydrogel probes, a 3D-printed device, and machine learning technology establishes a sensitive, accurate, and low-cost strategy for POCT (point-of-care testing) of multiple coexisting toxic heavy metal ions in environmental and food safety applications.

title: Nanocellulose-reinforced deep eutectic solvent-based smart hydrogel sensor for adaptive window regulation and machine learning-assisted low-temperature motion monitoring
abstract: Wearable hydrogel sensors often suffer from poor environmental stability and mechanical mismatch under temperature fluctuations, leading to signal drift and unreliable performance in real-world applications. To overcome these limitations, we developed a skin-inspired multifunctional hydrogel based on a green deep eutectic solvent (DES) system reinforced with cellulose nanofibrils (CNFs). The hydrogel was fabricated via UV-initiated polymerization of polyacrylamide (PAM) and gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA), with phytic acid and CNFs forming a dynamically cross-linked network through covalent, hydrogen-bonding, and ionic interactions. The incorporation of DES provides stable ionic conductivity and enhanced environmental tolerance, while CNF reinforcement significantly improves mechanical robustness. As a result, the PDGCP hydrogel exhibits high tensile strength (0.65 MPa), large stretchability (1862%), and stable sensing performance over thousands of cycles. The hydrogel also exhibits antibacterial activity and excellent biocompatibility. As a wearable strain sensor, it achieves a wide sensing range (up to 1200%) and enables reliable monitoring of human motion as well as high-fidelity ECG and EMG signals. In addition, the hydrogel can function as a smart window component with bidirectional temperature responsiveness. By integrating machine learning algorithms, the system enables real-time recognition of complex ice-skating motion postures with an accuracy of 98.25%. This work highlights a sustainable DES-based hydrogel platform with enhanced mechanical stability and environmental adaptability, offering promising applications in wearable electronics, intelligent sports monitoring, and adaptive building systems.

title: Scalable expanded-graphite coating for high-performance single-crystal Ni-rich cathodes with data-driven optimization
abstract: Single-crystal Ni-rich cathodes possess a monolithic structure that effectively suppresses the formation of microcracks, even under repeated volumetric changes during charge–discharge cycling. However, these single-crystal cathodes often exhibit slow Li-ion diffusion kinetics and poor rate capability, primarily due to the long diffusion pathways within the micron-sized particles. In this study, we introduce a simple and scalable one-pot method for applying an expanded-graphite (EG) surface coating to single-crystal Ni-rich cathodes. EG forms a uniform and conductive carbon layer through ball milling after surface activation with 3-aminopropyltriethoxysilane. This conductive coating significantly enhances the electrical conductivity of the cathode and effectively suppresses electrolyte-induced side reactions, thereby improving cycling stability while maintaining compatibility with existing industrial regeneration processes. A data-driven optimization approach based on Gaussian-process-based Bayesian optimization was employed to determine the optimal EG loading for maximizing electrochemical performance. The method is further demonstrated at kilogram scale, highlighting its feasibility for large-scale manufacturing. Overall, this work presents a practical approach for producing high-performance single-crystal Ni-rich cathodes and provides a promising route toward commercially viable cathode regeneration beyond laboratory-scale studies.

title: Data-driven mechanism derivation in hydrogenation reaction systems: A hybrid approach integrating machine learning and mathematical models
abstract: This study proposes a hybrid approach that integrates a black-box model with an equation-based mechanism verification model to identify the causative reactants of side reactions occurring in hydrogenation reaction systems and to derive their mechanisms. Due to the complex reaction network inherent in hydrogenation systems, exhaustive exploration and prediction of all side reactions are practically difficult, and such predictive uncertainty can lead to deterioration in product quality and economic losses. Accordingly, this study constructed a reliable dataset by performing preprocessing steps to remove missing values and outliers based on actual operating data, and designed an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) model. As a result of enhancing the generalization performance of the model through data transformation that reflects domain knowledge in the form of reaction rate expressions, the coefficient of determination (R2) improved to 0.97, and the root mean squared error (RMSE) decreased markedly to 0.04. In addition, the influence of each reactant was quantified and visualized using eXplainable AI (XAI) techniques, based on which the side reaction mechanisms were derived. To verify the derived mechanisms, reaction rate expressions were formulated using the Langmuir–Hinshelwood (L–H) and Power Law models, and a Monte Carlo-based mathematical model was developed. The validation results showed very high performance for all products, with R2 values greater than 0.98 and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) lower than 2.31%. This study has academic and industrial significance in that it systematically elucidates actual side reaction mechanisms while presenting a highly reliable predictive model applicable to reaction control design.

title: Smart bearings enabled by the tribovoltaic effect and machine learning
abstract: The tribovoltaic effect, which directly converts mechanical energy into electricity at dynamic semiconductor interfaces, presents a novel pathway for intrinsic mechanical sensing. Here, we materialize the “surface-as-sensor” paradigm by harnessing this effect to create a self-sensing bearing. This is achieved through a spontaneously formed molybdenum disulfide (MoS₂) layer on the bearing races, which establishes dynamic Schottky contacts with the steel balls, effectively turning the bearing surface itself into the sensing element. Mechanical friction at these interfaces directly generates a continuous stream of real-time electrical signals via the tribovoltaic effect. We analyze the underlying mechanism of this effect within the dynamic bearing system and demonstrate that the magnitude and characteristics of the resulting tribovoltaic outputs are intrinsically modulated by operational conditions, serving as highly sensitive and direct fingerprints of rotational speed and load. By employing explainable machine learning and deep learning to decode these signals, we achieve accurate monitoring of operational states, such as rotation speed, with the identification accuracy exceeding 96%, and further demonstrate its capability in early fault diagnosis. This work successfully establishes the tribovoltaic effect as a practical and powerful sensing mechanism, validating the “surface-as-sensor” concept as a pathway to a new generation of embedded, self-sensing intelligent machinery.

title: Machine-learning assisted decoupling of strain and temperature via an antagonistic sensing ionic elastomer
abstract: The simultaneous perception of multiple physical stimuli is essential for intelligent soft robotics and personalized healthcare. However, the concurrent detection of strain and temperature is fundamentally hindered by signal crosstalk, which compromises accuracy and reliability. Existing solutions, often relying on heterogeneous integration or intricate circuitry, inevitably sacrifice mechanical stability and scalability. Here, we introduce a sensing paradigm that leverages intrinsic material properties to achieve physical signal orthogonality. We design a solvent-free ion-conductive elastomer that exhibits antagonistic electrical responses to strain and temperature: its resistance increases but capacitance decreases upon stretching, whereas both resistance and capacitance increase with heating. This inherent signal decoupling stems from distinct ion migration and interfacial polarization mechanisms under mechanical and thermal stimuli. To translate this orthogonal relationship into precise quantitative readings, we employ a random forest regression model that directly maps the coupled resistance-capacitance signals to strain and temperature values, bypassing the need for complex analytical inversion. Our sensor achieves high-fidelity decoding, with determination coefficients of 0.90 for strain and 0.94 for temperature. It also maintains robust performance over 300 stretching cycles. We further demonstrate its practical utility in a firefighter safety warning system that simultaneously monitors body motion and detects extreme heat exposure. This work establishes a material-centric and algorithm-powered roadmap for multi perception, paving the way for high-fidelity sensing in complex environments.

title: Identification, segmentation and tracking: Hydrodynamic research in liquid-liquid-solid systems via machine learning
abstract: Accurate analysis of droplet and particle hydrodynamics is crucial for understanding flow, mass transfer, and heat transfer in liquid-liquid-solid (LLS) systems. However, simultaneously characterizing multiple dispersed phases remains challenging. This study proposes a machine learning framework integrating You Only Look Once (YOLO) and ByteTrack to simultaneously identify, segment, and track droplets and particles. YOLO11n is identified as the optimal model, achieving an F1 score of 0.883, mAP50–95 of 0.702, and processing speed of 20 ms per image. The model demonstrates strong generalization across various multiphase systems. In LLS systems, the effects of solid phase mass fraction, oil phase volume fraction, rotational speed, and particle mean diameter on droplet size distribution, Sauter mean diameter, and motion characteristics are investigated. An empirical correlation d32,dD=0.01671+40.4991ωsdpD0.01141+22.4046φoWe−0.2131 is developed to predict droplet Sauter mean diameter, with most deviations within 10%. This method enhances the understanding of LLS system hydrodynamics and facilitates reactor optimization, and scale-up.

title: A unified kinetic Monte Carlo and Bayesian optimization framework for the circular design of poly(methyl methacrylate): From synthesis to recycling
abstract: Polymer recycling is a significant challenge in the development of sustainable materials, motivating the design of strategies that balance recyclability with performance. Here, we present a unified method that links an integrated kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) model with a Bayesian optimization routine to determine synthesis conditions for poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) that balance recyclability with target molecular weight requirements. Validated against experimental benchmarks, the model explicitly correlates synthesis conditions with microstructural defects and subsequent depolymerization kinetics. Mechanistic analysis reveals that aggressive synthesis conditions increase polymerization process and defect density, which hinders depolymerization process and may yield polymer too short chains for practical application. To address this, we developed an autonomous three-dimensional optimization routine that efficiently navigates the design space, identifying a synthesis protocol that minimizes the total processing time while maintaining target molar mass strictly. This work establishes an effective, data-driven methodology for the rational design of closed-loop recycling polymers.

title: Strong dipole-dipole interaction-enhanced dual-network piezoelectric hydrogels for long-term pulse monitoring and machine learning-based object recognition
abstract: Flexible piezoelectric hydrogel skins are promising for wearable health monitoring, human-machine interaction and soft robotics. However, their application faces a critical challenge in reconciling tissue-level compliance with bias-free, high-SNR, and environment-resilient outputs, while simultaneously circumventing the need for bulky power supplies. Here we introduce a dual-network PAAM/PVDF-TrFE hydrogel via solvent-exchange processing that promotes β phase formation and dipole-dipole alignment, enabling mechanically robust piezoelectric skins. The resulting sensors exhibit linearity within the range of 1–600 kPa, with sensitivities of 2.76 mV·kPa−1 below 280 kPa and 1.11 mV·kPa−1 in the secondary regime above 280 kPa, while demonstrating fast response and recovery times (43 ms and 63 ms, respectively) and robust cyclic stability over 6500 cycles. Functionally, the sensors can decode finger-joint and facial micro-movements, precisely resolve arterial pulse waveforms (P1/P2/P3), and drive a five-pad array for object recognition using a lightweight RBF-SVM. By bridging molecular dipole alignment with machine-learning, this materials-to-algorithms platform advances the frontier of bias-free, self-powered sensing and low-power human-machine interfaces, showing significant potential for multi-element arrays and soft-robotic manipulation.

title: Machine learning-assisted iontronic detection of diurnal cortisol rhythm for neuroendocrine assessment of major depressive disorder
abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is primarily diagnosed based on clinical symptoms, reflecting the absence of reliable molecular markers. Although cortisol has been implicated in MDD, its clinical relevance remains unclear, partly due to reliance on single time-point measurements that overlook circadian dynamics. Here, we develop an iontronic platform that enables sensitive profiling of salivary cortisol and permits systematic evaluation of its diurnal variation. The sensing strategy integrates aptamer-based molecular recognition with a transcription-driven amplification pathway, converting weak cortisol-binding events into measurable modulation of ion transport under nanoconfinement, achieving a detection limit of 3.4 pM. Using this approach, we analyzed cortisol rhythms in healthy individuals and patients with MDD. In addition to elevated basal levels, MDD patients exhibited markedly increased diurnal amplitude, indicating disrupted neuroendocrine rhythmicity. Notably, dynamic features of cortisol fluctuation provided substantially greater discriminatory power than static concentration values. When combined with basic clinical parameters and evaluated using a support vector machine model, these rhythm-based signatures enabled reliable differentiation between MDD and control groups. These findings identify amplified diurnal cortisol fluctuation as a quantifiable neuroendocrine phenotype of MDD. Rather than emphasizing absolute hormone levels, this work highlights temporal dysregulation as a potential molecular marker and provides a noninvasive framework for objective neuroendocrine assessment in psychiatric research.

title: Dynamic aggregation control via machine learning-integrated PBM for minimizing impurity entrapment
abstract: The achievable purity in crystallization is limited by a multiscale structural transition, where loose aggregates densify into bridged agglomerates that readily entrap impurities. A specialized machine learning model applied to in situ microscopy images yields a time-resolved fractal dimension that quantifies the evolving morphology of crystal aggregates and serves as a descriptor of their structural state. We embed this descriptor into a turbulence-informed breakage formulation for crystal aggregates and couple it with the system's aggregation and breakage dynamics, defining a multiscale framework that identifies the structural threshold at which loose aggregates transition into bridged, impurity-entrapping agglomerates. Building on this mechanism, we develop the Morphology–Evolution-informed Purity Strategy (MEPS), which identifies an extraction window before the formation of bridged agglomerates, thereby yielding crystals formed from loose aggregates that readily release entrapped mother liquor, in contrast to the several-fold higher retention of mother liquor observed at later extraction times. This approach provides a mechanistic basis for determining optimal extraction timing, offering a practical route for suppressing impurity entrapment in crystallization processes.

title: Ag nanowire-embedded core (PS)-shell (PVDF) nanofibers for high-performance triboelectric nanogenerators and artificial intelligence-driven material recognition
abstract: Over the past decade, extensive research has focused on surface engineering and multi-layer approaches to enhance the contact electrification and electrostatic induction of triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs). However, most of these techniques involve time-consuming, multi-step fabrication processes, highlighting the need for innovative approaches. In this study, we introduce a core-shell nanofiber (NF) architecture composed of a polystyrene (PS) core embedded with silver nanowires (Ag NWs) and a polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) shell. This core (PS/Ag)-shell (PVDF) structure significantly enhanced both charge trapping and β-phase induction. Systematic optimization demonstrated that embedding 0.04 vol% Ag NWs into the PS core increased the average peak-to-peak voltage to 319.9 V, representing a 94.3% enhancement compared with pristine core-shell NFs. Comprehensive analysis confirmed that the core-loaded structure outperformed its shell-loaded counterpart because the spatial confinement of Ag NWs within the PS core, together with shielding by the PVDF shell, enhanced charge storage and suppressed leakage current. The core–shell structure also exhibited faster charge accumulation, which is particularly advantageous in applications where external mechanical work is supplied momentarily. Finally, a model trained on triboelectric voltage data achieved 98.3% classification accuracy for five distinct materials, highlighting the potential of this self-powered TENG sensor for intelligent material recognition.

title: Sense, think, and robot control: Multimodal material recognition sensing integrated with large language model reasoning
abstract: Touch is fundamental to human material perception, involving diverse receptors and complex cognitive processing. However, existing studies are often limited to single-modal sensing and stop at recognizing material type. In this work, multimodal sensing is integrated with a large language model (LLM) to improve material recognition accuracy and enable deeper thinking. The proposed compact flexible multimodal sensor can simultaneously acquire pressure, thermal, and dielectric signals, achieving an overall recognition accuracy of up to 99.13% across 23 representative materials. Based on the recognition results and task requirements, the LLM generates robot control decisions. Augmented reality (AR) provides system visualization and user control, enabling intuitive human–robot interaction. This system demonstrates intelligent robotic sorting driven by material recognition in real-world scenarios and may inspire the application of multimodal sensors in embodied intelligence.

title: Niobium doping enables durable Ni-rich layered cathodes through interfacial and morphological stabilization with data-driven performance validation
abstract: The addition of a small amount of niobium oxide during the synthesis of Nb-modified 9-series Ni-rich layered oxides yields multiple beneficial effects.
