These include suppression of aluminum segregation from the precursor, refinement of primary particle size within dense spherical secondary particles, mitigation of oxygen release during electrochemical cycling, and reduced structural changes associated with the H2–H3 phase transition at voltages up to 4.3 V vs. Li|Li + . The optimized Nb-doped material with 0.5 mol% Nb addition demonstrates excellent rate capability and improved cycling stability, achieving 85.3% capacity retention after 200 cycles at 1C, even for electrodes with a high active-material mass loading of approximately 8.5 mg cm −2 . The role of Nb in structural and electrochemical stabilization is elucidated using operando X-ray diffraction, ex situ soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy, and complementary microscopy studies. In addition, a gated recurrent unit-based approach enables effective prediction of long-term cycling stability. Overall, this strategy demonstrates a viable pathway toward stabilizing high-energy Ni-rich cathodes while accelerating performance assessment for practical lithium-ion battery applications.

title: Integrating experiments, numerical simulations and Bayesian optimisation to maximise drug permeability of hollow pyramidal microneedle arrays
abstract: This study presents an experimental–numerical framework integrated with Bayesian optimisation (BO) for the design of hollow pyramidal microneedle (MN) arrays to enhance transdermal drug permeability across the skin. Finite element (FE) simulations have been carried out to model coupled fluid flow and drug delivery in multilayered skin, including convection–diffusion of the drug in HMN and fluid slip condition at fluid (MN tip)–skin (porous) interfaces. The geometric design parameters, including lumen diameter, array pitch, and needle count, have been optimised using a Gaussian process–based BO (GP-BO) framework implemented in Python via the scikit-learn library. Experimental validation has been performed using hollow microneedle (HMN) arrays loaded with ibuprofen (IBU) sodium, applied to ex vivo neonatal porcine skin in Franz diffusion cell setups. Drug permeation has been subsequently quantified using high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) analysis. The results revealed that approximately 150 μg (≈3%) of the administered drug permeated into the receptor compartment after 24-h, whereas 295.79 ± 148.95 μg remained within the dermal layers, indicating prolonged drug retention and effective localised delivery. The integrated BO methodology significantly improved permeability predictions while minimising computational costs, resulting in optimal HMN geometries that maximised both volumetric flow rate and transdermal permeability. The improvement in performance represents around 5% enhancement over the previously optimised configuration, demonstrating both the effectiveness and robustness of the BO framework.

title: A digital twin framework for predictive modeling of liver-on-a-chip system dynamics using limited experimental data
abstract: This study presents a data-efficient digital twin framework for a liver-on-a-chip (LoC) integrated optical biosensor platform that integrates a computational microfluidics solver with a physiologically based pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PBPK-PD) model to predict doxorubicin-induced hepatotoxicity. A learning-based model discrepancy term, trained on glutathione S-transferase alpha (GST-α) release as a biomarker, corrects structural mismatches and aligns simulations with measurements. The microfluidics module computes steady, incompressible, laminar velocity fields and transient advection-diffusion-reaction of drugs and oxygen, providing spatiotemporal concentration profiles that inform the PBPK-PD compartments. A hybrid uncertainty quantification approach, combining Bayesian inference to calibrate transport and kinetic parameters from sparse data with an XGBoost discrepancy model that captures residual bias, estimates posterior predictive intervals that account for both epistemic and aleatoric uncertainties. The calibrated twin reproduces time-resolved GST-α trajectories at various dose levels, with observed responses falling within the posterior intervals. For the high-dose doxorubicin condition (20 μM), the predicted GST-α concentration shows a relative deviation of about 9% for the 2D model and 5–6% for the 3D model compared to the filtered experimental measurements. The learned discrepancy extends to previously unseen drug concentrations, enabling conservative extrapolation within quantified uncertainty bounds. Overall, the framework addresses common issues of data scarcity and model-experiment mismatch in organ-on-a-chip studies, informing preclinical decision-making for drug safety and toxicity assessments.

title: Smart thrust bearing with integrated discharge-based energy harvesting and deep-learning fault detection
abstract: Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) are promising energy harvesting devices that convert wasted energy into electrical energy from ambient environments, especially in the form of friction. However, they have a few drawbacks, such as low output and severe wear. To address these drawbacks, we adopt a phenomenon known as electric discharge. Rotation is a representative input form for mechanical components, and we are inspired by a thrust bearing structure for generating our TENG as bearings are widely used in many industries and are constantly rotating. In this paper, a thrust ball bearing TENG (TBB-TENG) is proposed. The TBB-TENG exhibits characteristic patterns on the stator by modifying its surface to induce an electric discharge and ultimately enhance the output. Additionally, a mechanical stability analysis is performed theoretically in response to the modification. Furthermore, parametric studies are conducted to optimize the proposed TBB-TENG. Finally, we present the practical use of TBB-TENG as a self-powered defect diagnosis sensor using a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN), demonstrating its high accuracy.

title: Data-driven discovery of targeted CuM nanoparticles on 2D CuBa for CO2 fixation: Synergistic effects of ionic liquids in C–C/N coupling
abstract: Revealing the mechanism of CO2 electroreduction (CO2R) to multicarbon (C2+) products remains challenging, especially at the complex electrode−liquid interface and under potential-dependent energy conditions. This study presents comprehensive density functional theory calculations and data-driven screening of CO2R to ethylene and acetamide over Cu-based bimetallic nanoparticles (NPs) loaded on a CuBa surface. Given that 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium tetrafluoroborate ([Bmim][BF4]) can promote local enrichment and activation of CO2 under potential-dependent energy conditions and achieve efficient CO2R, 25 electric double layer models were constructed using CuBa@CuM NP catalysts and [Bmim][BF4] ionic liquid (IL) in an acidic explicit solvent microenvironment. The Gibbs free energy profile for each proton-coupled electron transfer process of CO2 was calculated via potential-dependent energy integration, with the IL solvent model considered under a constant potential. First CO2 is reduced to CO, after which C–C coupling can occur in *CO–*CHO and *CO–*COH or during *CO direct dimerization toward ethylene synthesis, while C–N coupling in *CCO–*NH3 is most feasibly favored toward acetamide synthesis. CuZr, CuPd, CuPt, and CuBi NPs loaded on CuBa demonstrated outstanding activity, with limiting potential (UL) values of −1.27, −1.21, −1.28, and −1.37 V, respectively, which were smaller than those of other catalysts used in ethylene and acetamide synthesis. Then, based on structural, thermodynamic, and electronic calculations, various quantitative indicators of the structure–activity relationship were established, such as correlations between Bader charge transfer and the binding energy of the intermediate, d-band center difference, and UL of the maximum free energy change step. These results were quantitatively related to CO2R reaction activity through key species interactions and electronic property descriptors. Furthermore, ab initio molecular dynamics simulations were performed in the NVT ensemble at 300 K for 10 ps to estimate CO2 activation over different CuBa@CuM NP catalysts, including the radial distribution function, coordination number of O–H, bond length (C=O), and bond angle (OCO) variations in the CO2 molecule. Finally, various machine learning models were adopted to predict the optimal UL of CO2R to ethylene in a Python3 environment. The coefficient of determination and mean absolute error were employed to evaluate model performance, with values of 0.92 and 0.16 for the extreme gradient boosting model, respectively, indicating its optimal ability to predict catalytic activity. By combining high-performance computing and big data screening for complex catalytic reaction mechanisms, the study provides a better understanding of the catalytic process and offers guidance for future catalyst design for C2+ product synthesis via CO2R.

title: Capacity prediction of cobalt nickel phosphide supercapacitors based on machine learning
abstract: Nickel cobalt phosphide (NiCoP) has emerged as a promising electrode material for supercapacitors due to its strong redox activity, high conductivity, low cost, and excellent chemical/thermal stability. This study proposes a high-precision hybrid machine learning model, CNN (Convolutional Neural Networks)-BiGRU(Bidirectional gated recurrent unit)-Attention model, for predicting the capacitance of NiCoP-based electrode materials. The dataset consists of 803 experimental instances with 9 input parameters: Ni and Co molar ratios, morphology, specific surface area, current collector, electrolyte concentration, potential window, current density and the output parameter of the supercapacitors' capacity. The relationship between material composition, microstructure, electrochemical properties, and capacitance was successfully fitted. After normalization, R2, RMSE, and MAE values of the CNN-BiGRU-Attention algorithm reach 0.98, 0.021, and 0.18, respectively, demonstrating exceptional model accuracy and fitting capability. The generalization ability of the model was verified through experiments with a mean relative error of 9.20%, indicating remarkable stability and reliability. Furthermore, a novel NiCoP electrode material with a nonstoichiometric ratio of Ni1.3Co0.55P was screened out by searching the space generation method, which exhibits an outstanding specific capacitance of 2263.3 F/g at a current density of 1 A/g. This work provides an innovative and effective method for predicting NiCoP performance, while significantly optimizing of multicomponent phosphide-based supercapacitors with enhanced specific capacitance.

title: An AI-guided framework for discovery and evolution of sulfotransferases enables efficient sulfotyrosine bioproduction
abstract: The discovery of efficient enzymes for specific biotransformation remains a rate-limiting step in synthetic biology, traditionally relying on laborious experimental screening. Here, we demonstrate how artificial intelligence (AI) dramatically accelerates this process by establishing a streamlined pipeline for sulfotransferase (SULT) discovery and engineering. We leveraged the deep learning model UniKP to predict enzyme kinetic parameters from protein sequences alone, enabling rapid in silico prioritization of candidate SULTs for sulfotyrosine (sTyr) synthesis. This AI-guided approach identified active enzymes with a 50% success rate from a random pool and outperformed traditional BLAST selection from a library of 1000 homologs. An AI-prioritized SULT was successfully engineered through directed evolution, yielding a variant with 7.25-fold enhanced activity while maintaining broad substrate promiscuity. When integrated into engineered Escherichia coli (E. coli), this evolved enzyme enabled high-level sTyr production (1578 μM). Our work establishes AI as a powerful tool to shortcut the enzyme discovery and optimization timeline, serving as a case study that illustrates how AI can be integrated into the rapid development of biocatalysts.

title: Multiscale pulsating intensification and wavelet entropy-driven AI optimization of fluidized biomass hydrogen production
abstract: To address the issue of suboptimal hydrogen production efficiency resulting from particle agglomeration and channeling during biomass fluidized bed gasification, this paper presents a method for process intensification and prediction that integrates multiscale flow analysis with deep learning. Initially, pressure pulsation signals are decomposed using power spectral density (PSD) and wavelet transforms to identify the system's eigenfrequencies. The mechanisms by which pulsed gas flows are intensified across the micro, meso, and macroscales are examined. This involves overcoming diffusion limitations at the microscale, disrupting bubbles and particle agglomerates at the mesoscale, and enhancing bed mixing and promoting reaction equilibrium at the macroscale. Secondly, the multiscale coupling relationship between flow complexity and hydrogen yield is elucidated. The trends of wavelet flow-reaction entropy and gas yield exhibit synchronization with increasing pulsation frequency. This study establishes wavelet flow-reaction entropy as a key feature characterizing the correlation between flow complexity and reaction performance. Finally, a two-level Deep Neural Network model driven by wavelet flow-reaction entropy is developed. This model follows the flow trends of the fluidized bed system and enables the accurate prediction of hydrogen yield under various operating conditions, achieving an overall R2 of 0.969. Furthermore, the optimal pressure and pulsation frequency ranges (Zones A and B) are identified, enhances hydrogen production performance. The predicted maximum H2 yield is 12.67 mol/kg-biomass under conditions of 4.4 bar and 3.5 Hz. This study not only unveils the multiscale flow-reaction coupling mechanism underlying pulsed fluidized hydrogen production but also offers a novel theoretical foundation for the intelligent control of biomass pyrolysis gasification processes.

title: Dual-functional sensing materials for smartphone quantification of sulfur dioxide derivatives and AI-based monitoring of biogenic amines for meat freshness
abstract: The rapid and accurate monitoring of sulfur dioxide (SO2) derivatives and biogenic amines presents a considerable challenge in food safety, primarily owing to the limitations in sensitivity, portability, and real-time analytical capabilities of existing methods. We introduce a dual-functional fluorescent probe RQB-RM, which is capable of detecting SO2 and biogenic amines with high brightness and ultrasensitivity. The quantum yields of RQB-RM were 22.34% and 17.98%, with limits of detection of 5.18 and 35.20 nM. Based on RQB-RM, a series of smart sensing materials (R-Lab, R-Gel, and R-Ele) were developed, eventually creating two integrated platforms, bridging the material and digital realms: (i) the smartphone-assisted platform enabled the quantitative detection of SO2 derivatives without requiring specialized equipment, and (ii) the dual-channel artificial intelligence (AI)-based freshness monitoring platform with R-Gel exhibited exceptional accuracy in the real-time assessment of shrimp spoilage through autonomous learning of signal dynamics. In addition to its application in food monitoring, this probe was comprehensively validated for its precise mitochondrial targeting and cellular imaging capabilities. We combined sensing materials and AI, providing crucial technological support and a paradigm reference for interdisciplinary innovation in fields such as food quality monitoring and biomedical analysis.

title: Polyacrylamide/agarose/trehalose/carbon nanotubes composite hydrogel with stretchability and compressibility for high-performance wearable strain/pressure sensors and machine-learning-assisted gesture recognition
abstract: Hydrogel sensors hold great potential for flexible wearable devices. However, their practical application in complex environments is limited by several shortcomings, such as the inability to detect tensile and compressive stimuli with high accuracy, insufficient frost resistance, and a lack of self-adhesiveness. Herein, we incorporated trehalose into a dual-network hydrogel system composed of polyacrylamide, agarose, and carbon nanotubes through a simple one-pot method to produce a novel composite hydrogel. The addition of trehalose significantly enhances both the mechanical properties and frost resistance of the composite hydrogel to deliver ultrahigh flexibility, superior stretchability and compressibility, strong adhesion, excellent biocompatibility, and reliable frost resistance. Sensors assembled from the composite hydrogel provide high sensitivity with antifreeze performance to temperatures as low as −30 °C. The optimized strain sensor delivers a gauge factor of 9.84 within the 60–90% strain range, a low detection limit (0.1%), and a broad sensing range (0.1–90%). The optimized pressure sensor exhibits high sensitivity (3.46 kPa−1 in the 1–3 kPa region), a wide detection range (39.4 Pa to 100 kPa), fast response (70 ms), and reproducible performance over 1000 cycles. In practical applications, the sensors successfully detect diverse physiological signals, ranging from arterial pulse pressure to heavy foot-treading pressure. Further integration with the Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) machine-learning algorithm results in exceptional prediction accuracy of gesture recognition, achieving 99.44%. All these features testify to promising prospects in motion assistance, health monitoring, and wearable electronics with high sensitivity and reliability.

title: Chemical reactor optimization leveraging distilled LLM enhanced by prompt design and fine-tuning strategy
abstract: Multi-objective optimization plays a critical role in chemical reactor design, where conflicting objectives and complex constraints pose challenges. Traditional optimization methods heavily rely on manual modeling and tuning. To this end, we develop a generative reasoning framework by fine-tuning distilled large language models (LLMs) and designing domain knowledge-embedded prompts for both continuous-variable and mixed-variable optimization of chemical reactors, covering a methanol-steam-reforming fixed bed reactor, a methanol-to-olefins fluidized bed reactor, a multipolar‑magnesium electrolyzer, and two organic flow reactors. Results demonstrate that full-scale LLMs can effectively generate Pareto-optimal solutions but face deployment barriers due to hardware constraints. To improve practical usability, we further design structured chain-of-thought prompts and adopt a quantized low-rank adaptation method to fine-tune locally deployed distilled LLMs. We find that the fine-tuned distilled LLMs significantly enhance multi-objective reasoning performance, improving Pareto frontier identification accuracy from 25% to 79% for the 7B model and from 44% to 91% for the 14B model relative to the corresponding baseline distilled LLMs without fine-tuning. The novelty of this study lies in integrating structured chain-of-thought prompting with parameter-efficient fine-tuning of locally deployable streamlined LLMs, thereby providing a practical LLM-assisted framework for multi-objective optimization of chemical reactors.

title: A degradable, highly tough, and resilient nanocomposite hydrogel for self-powered wearable sensors and a deep learning-assisted recognition system
abstract: The conductive hydrogels always suffered from large hysteresis, low toughness and poor capability of accurately predicting physical deformation, which seriously restricted their application in smart wearable devices. Herein, a novel conductive hydrogel was fabricated using water-soluble chitosan-modified halloysite nanotubes (CS@HNTs) as an organic-inorganic hybrid crosslinker, which imparts high resilience, superior toughness, and excellent fatigue resistance to the resulting material. Through abundant multiple hydrogen bonds, electrostatic interactions between polymer chains and CS@HNTs, and coordination between aluminum ions and carboxyl groups, this system effectively organizes the polymer network without significantly increasing crosslinking density, thereby conferring remarkable mechanical properties (91.4% resilience and a toughness of 1.25 MJ/m3). The hierarchical energy dissipation mechanisms, dynamic mechanical response behavior, and network structure evolution of the materials were systematically characterized by rheology and low-field (LF) nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy. Concurrently, the fully physically crosslinked network facilitates efficient ionic conduction and enables rapid degradation under alkaline conditions. The hydrogel-based sensor also demonstrates a notable thermal response, with a temperature coefficient of resistance of −1.95%°C−1, allowing for precise monitoring of ambient temperature. Furthermore, we constructed a self-powered sensing system for identifying various human motions and, separately, developed an information security system that integrates deep learning algorithm to achieve highly efficient and accurate (98%) information encryption and decryption based on Morse code. This work provides a promising strategy for constructing high-performance, sustainable, and intelligent flexible wearable platforms.

title: Gas-liquid two-phase flow pattern identification based on HHT and SVM-assisted optical carrier microwave interferometry
abstract: In chemical engineering applications, gas-liquid two-phase flow patterns have a direct impact on reaction kinetics, mixing efficiency, and overall system stability. Accurate flow pattern identification enables engineers to predict pressure drops, optimize residence time distributions, and enhance interfacial contact between phases, thereby effectively improving the yield of chemical processes. In this study, a novel distributed optical fiber sensing technology, i.e., optical carrier microwave interferometry (OCMI), is applied for horizontal gas-liquid two-phase flow pattern identification, in combination with time-frequency domain analysis and support vector machine (SVM). Several statistical metrics are employed to characterize the frequency domain features. Through threshold-based methods, bubble/elongated bubble flow and partial wave flow can be recognized, while identifying slug flow and stratified flow remains challenging. To address this challenge, the Hilbert-Huang transform (HHT) is applied to the reconstructed time-series signal to extract discriminative time-frequency spectral features, enabling effective differentiation among all flow patterns. An SVM-based intelligent recognition model is then constructed, leveraging the extracted time-frequency domain features as input, achieving a high classification accuracy of 96.9%. By pioneering the integration of distributed OCMI sensing with HHT-based feature extraction and machine learning, this work establishes a new paradigm for multiphase flow diagnostics that overcomes the inherent limitations of conventional point-wise or local sensing methods through continuous distributed monitoring along the pipeline.

title: Triboelectric nanogenerator-based intelligent sensing communication and deep learning motion recognition system based on ionic hydrogel
abstract: As an important vehicle for the next generation of interactive technologies, the human-machine interaction system deeply integrates flexible electronics, the Internet of Things and artificial intelligence technologies. It shows great potential in many areas such as medical surveillance and smart wearable devices. This study developed a conductive ion hydrogel-based triboelectric nanogenerator (PGL-TENG) and its associated intelligent sensing and communication system, using a deep learning model to assist in identifying human motion status. The hydrogel, prepared from PVA, Gel, and LiCl, exhibited excellent mechanical strength, conductivity, and water retention, and served as the electrode, while VHB tape was used as the friction layer. The assembled PGL-TENG achieved an open-circuit voltage of 200 V, a short-circuit current of 13 μA, and a power density of 1040 mW m−2. A deep learning platform was established to extract voltage features and achieve accurate classification of human motion states, significantly improved gait recognition accuracy, highlighting the potential of deep learning for self-powered sensing and multimodal motion recognition. In addition, an intelligent sensing and communication system was developed, which uses Morse code to identify and transmit various signals, and its dual alarm mechanism uses visual and audio alarms to achieve efficient and reliable transmission of the “SOS” distress signal. This offers a promising technical approach for the development of intelligent wearable devices and intelligent communication systems.

title: Magnetic droplet carrier robot integrated with AI-fueled on-site detection
abstract: Heavy metal pollution poses urgent threats to environmental and human health, yet existing on-site detection technologies face critical sensitivity limitations and operational constraints in field applications. To overcome these challenges, we pioneer an integrated droplet manipulation-detection system synergising a magnetic droplet carrier robot (MDC-robot) with AI-fueled dynamic analysis. This system establishes an on-site workflow where the MDC-robot leverages a zoned wettability surface and multi-degree-of-freedom magnetic actuation for translation and rotation, enabling lossless 3D droplet manipulation. The Mask RGB-drop (MR) algorithm provides AI-fueled quantification of colorimetric signals during droplet processing. Validated in municipal sludge matrices, the integrated platform achieves a 226% increase in Cu²⁺ detection sensitivity through evaporation-assisted preconcentration, meeting drinking-water quality guidelines. Comparison with standard detection techniques confirms reliability, with recoveries of 96-104% and measurement errors below 7%. The system also delivers significantly improved efficiency, automation, and reduced cost relative to conventional manual detection, which remains the dominant approach in practical environmental diagnostics. It is demonstrated that the AI-fueled, materials-integrated methodology defines a new paradigm for intelligent environmental monitoring.

title: Configurable flexible energy storage system for machine learning-powered multimodal health surveillance
abstract: Wearable intelligent health monitoring platforms exhibit substantial application potential in domains such as telemedicine and posture sensing. However, constrained by the interfacial instability and deformation mismatch issues in energy storage systems, ensuring stable and continuous power supply for the monitoring platform under various mechanical deformations remains a major challenge. Here, we report the design and validation of a flexible integrated energy and analysis platform (FIEAP) that provides continuous and stable energy supply and machine learning-based intelligent analysis for wearable systems. This platform employs a synergistic dual-network crosslinking strategy utilizing hydrogen bonding and coordination interactions to enhance interfacial stability by creating a polyacrylamide/sodium alginate (PAM/SA) composite hydrogel electrolyte with strengthened interfacial adhesion, enhanced mechanical compliance, and uniform Zn2+ deposition. With PAM/SA, Zn||Zn battery delivers areal capacity of 5 mAh cm−2 with 99% retention after 1600 h, demonstrating the ultralong cycling stability of the PAM/SA. It is then combined with a series-parallel arranged zinc anode, manganese dioxide cathode, and flexible printed interconnects to make a modular zinc-ion battery array. Combined with a thin-film pressure sensor and Bluetooth low energy, it enables acquisition, transmission, and intelligent analysis of body surface pressure variations for practical applications. We show that the FIEAP can achieve high-accuracy recognition of six walking postures, with an accuracy rate of up to 96.7%. The platform paves the way for the design and application of stable integrated energy systems in wearable intelligent devices, enabling widespread utility for daily motion tracking and disease treatment evaluation.
keywords: Flexible integrated energy and analysis platform

title: Ultra-sensitive self-powered thermogalvanic hydrogel wristband enabled by resistance-gated strategy
abstract: Next-generation human-machine interfaces require energy-sustainable and highly responsive sensing systems. However, most wearable sensors rely on external power supplies and complex signal processing, limiting long-term stability and portability. Here, we propose a self-powered thermogalvanic hydrogel wristband that simultaneously harvests energy from the body-ambient temperature gradient and transduces mechanical deformation into readable electrical signals. The wristband integrates six dual-layer hydrogel patches, each exhibiting high extensibility (534.5%), adaptable modulus (638 kPa), lightweight portability, tunable ionic conductivity, and anti-drying stability for prolonged use. Enhanced sensing is achieved through thermoelectric–mechanical coupling governed by interfacial resistance gating, wherein deformation reduces the resistance barrier and enhances the intrinsic thermoelectric current. This coupling ensures high sensitivity with a response time of merely 40 ms. By integrating deep learning algorithms, the wristband achieves real-time sign language recognition and object authentication with an accuracy exceeding 95%. This work introduces a hybrid strategy for intelligent motion recognition, providing a new insight for sustainable wearable human-machine interaction.

title: Unraveling the adsorption mechanism of PFAS on biochar: A cross-scale integration of DFT calculations and interpretable machine learning
abstract: Per-and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) have become a severe threat to aqueous environmental safety due to their ultra-high persistence, bioaccumulation, and strong mobility. Herein, a cross-scale strategy combining density functional theory (DFT) and interpretable machine learning (ML) was employed to reveal the adsorption mechanism of PFAS on biochar (BC) and identify the key governing factors. DFT calculations demonstrate a pronounced chain-length dependence for PFAS adsorption. Longer chains enable more extensive molecular spreading on BC surfaces. This physical spreading drives a continuous buildup of van der Waals forces. Consequently, the interfacial binding strength increases significantly. Subsequently, DFT-derived quantum descriptors were integrated with a dataset of 1961 experimental adsorption samples for modeling. The CatBoost model achieves optimal predictive performance after Bayesian optimization with a coefficient of determination of 0.9196 and an RMSE of 9.4227. The five-fold cross-validation yields a mean coefficient of determination of 0.8292 (±0.0255),which confirms reliable model generalization ability. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis quantitatively identified initial concentration, adsorption time, average pore size of BC, and the HOMO-LUMO gap of PFAS as the dominant factors. Operational parameters contributed up to 46.89%, significantly higher than BC physicochemical properties (36.31%) and molecular descriptors (16.8%). This study provides a comprehensive microscopic mechanism underlying chain-length-dependent PFAS adsorption, offering fundamental theoretical guidance for the rational design and targeted optimization of BC to enhance the removal of diverse PFAS in aqueous environments.

title: AI-guided evolution of membrane-associated cytidylyltransferase and systems metabolic engineering enable high-titer CDP-choline biosynthesis
abstract: The efficient biosynthesis of cytidine-5′-diphosphocholine (CDP-choline), a vital pharmaceutical intermediate, relies on a sequential two-step pathway catalyzed by choline kinase (CKI) and CTP:phosphocholine cytidylyltransferase (CCT). However, this bioprocess is largely bottlenecked by the sluggish kinetics of CCT, an amphipathic membrane-bound enzyme whose rational engineering is severely hindered by the lack of solved crystal structures. To alleviate this kinetic limitation, this study established a physics-informed and evolution-guided integrated strategy. First, a sequence-structure-dynamics three-dimensional funnel screening workflow was constructed. By combining AlphaFold2-based structural topology filtering with DLKcat kinetic pre-screening, we successfully captured a high-potential candidate CCT from Maudiozyma saulgeensis (MsCCT), with superior chassis compatibility, which showed an 8.69-fold increase in total catalytic activity compared to the control CCT from Saccharomyces cerevisiae (ScCCT). Subsequently, we employed a multi-view integrated Protein Language Model (PLM) zero-shot prediction method. Through the cross-validation of ProGen (evolutionary perspective), SaProt (global structural perspective), and ProSST (local micro-environmental perspective), combined with a domain-focusing strategy, the mutant MsCCTM3 was identified, exhibiting a 2.4-fold catalytic enhancement over the wild-type MsCCT. Upon integrating the evolved MsCCTM3 into a metabolically optimized Bacillus subtilis chassis, multi-omics analysis deciphered a critical kinetic mismatch, revealing that the hyper-active enzyme shifted the metabolic bottleneck to upstream substrate transport and precursor supply capacity. Ultimately, the engineered strain achieved a high titer of 5.65 g/L with a space-time yield of 0.202 g/(L·h) in a 5 L bioreactor, representing a 34.7% improvement over the control strain. This work not only provides an efficient strain for the industrial production of CDP-choline but also offers an integrated data-driven workflow that demonstrates promising potential for engineering complex membrane proteins lacking structural templates.

title: Standardized batch-manufacturable triboelectric sensor arrays for deep learning-enabled race-walking state recognition
abstract: Objective and reproducible biomechanical monitoring is important for race-walking training and technical assessment, yet flexible triboelectric sensors still suffer from poor unit-to-unit consistency caused by manual fabrication and limited validation under sports-relevant wearing conditions. Herein, we propose a standardized fused deposition modeling–flexible printed circuit (FDM–FPC) hybrid manufacturing strategy for batch-manufacturable triboelectric sensor arrays toward smart-insole sensing. In this design, FDM-printed thermoplastic elastomer structures define the elastic spacer and triboelectric layer, while FPC electrodes provide reproducible electrode geometry and integrated interconnection. The resulting sensors showed a low coefficient of variation of 1.45% among 25 devices from five independent batches, markedly lower than that of manually fabricated controls (9.67%). With optimized surface morphology and stable device architecture, the sensor responded to plantar-level loads from 2 to 250 N and captured weak physiological signals, including pulse and respiration. Application-relevant reliability was further verified through 20,000 loading cycles at 200 N, 5000 bending cycles, and temperature, humidity, and artificial-sweat tests. By integrating three sensing units into a smart insole, a seven-channel plantar triboelectric signal representation and a multi-scale convolutional neural network–bidirectional gated recurrent unit (CNN-BiGRU) model were established for race-walking state recognition. Based on six volunteers and 9331 sliding-window samples, Leave-One-Subject-Out Cross-Validation (LOSO-CV) achieved 94.6% accuracy and a 94.3% macro-F1 score for five-class recognition. This work provides a reproducible and application-oriented triboelectric smart-insole platform for auxiliary race-walking technical assessment and wearable sports analytics.

title: Discovery of novel AMPs from Nanorana parkeri: A deep learning approach to combating multidrug-resistant P. aeruginosa infection
abstract: The increasing threat of multidrug-resistant bacterial infections demands new antimicrobial agents and efficient discovery strategies. Amphibians represent a rich yet underexplored source of antimicrobial peptides, but systematic mining of amphibian genomes remains limited. In this study, a deep learning-based framework was applied to the genome of Nanorana parkeri to identify seven candidate antimicrobial peptides. Among them, c_AMP2 exhibited the strongest and broad-spectrum antibacterial activity, including potent inhibition of multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa (MRPA, MIC = 6.25 μM). Rational optimization of c_AMP2 generated two analogs, RR18 and VR18, with enhanced cationicity and amphipathicity. Structural characterization confirmed that both peptides adopt stable amphipathic α-helical conformations, with optimized hydrophobic and cationic segregation. Notably, VR18 exhibited an improved amphipathic distribution, whereas both analogs formed short rod-like nanostructures as revealed by AFM and SEM analyses. Functionally, both of the peptides showed improved activity against MRPA (MIC = 3.13 μM) and rapid bactericidal kinetics. Mechanistic analyses supported a membrane-targeting mode of action, as indicated by molecular simulations and biophysical assays demonstrating membrane binding, depolarization, and permeabilization. In a murine pneumonia and sepsis model induced by MRPA, RR18 exhibited favorable safety and significantly reduced the bacterial burden, alleviated pathology, and suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokine production. These findings demonstrate the potential of amphibian genomic mining for antimicrobial peptide discovery and identify RR18 as a candidate against drug-resistant P. aeruginosa.

title: Cu–nanosheet wrapped plant fiber sponge with tip-enhanced electric field for self–powered triboelectric gesture recognition via convolutional neural network
abstract: The integration of sustainable energy harvesting and intelligent sensing is essential for next-generation self-powered systems. Here, a Cu-nanosheet (Cu-NS) and thermoplastic polyurethane synergistically wrapped plant fiber sponge (PFS@TPU-Cu) is fabricated via a simple ball-milling and impregnation strategy. The incorporation of Cu-NS induces a tip-enhanced electric field that intensifies interfacial polarization and promotes efficient charge transfer during contact–separation. The resulting PTC-TENG achieves an open-circuit voltage of 125 V, short-circuit current of 4.2 μA, and power density of 0.16 W m−2, sufficient to charge a 4.7 μF capacitor to 3 V within 110 s and power 738 LEDs. The device exhibits 80% compressibility, rapid response (46/54 ms), and durability over 5000 cycles, enabling reliable mechanical adaptability. Moreover, integrated with a convolutional neural network, the self-powered sensor attains 95.25% gesture recognition accuracy, demonstrating strong potential in sign language recognition and wearable human-machine interfaces. This work establishes a scalable, field-enhanced triboelectric platform for energy-autonomous intelligent electronics.

title: Machine learning-enabled decoupling of strain and temperature for multifunctional sensing in soft robotic manipulation
abstract: Reliable manipulation in soft robotics requires sensing systems that can simultaneously resolve deformation, force direction, and temperature while remaining robust to cross-interference. Here we report an all-resistive dual-modal flexible sensor that, in combination with machine learning-based inference, enables decoupled perception of strain magnitude, strain direction, and temperature for robotic grasping. The sensor employs a tri-channel rosette architecture in which two channels provide temperature-invariant strain sensing, while a third channel encodes coupled strain-temperature information. This physical encoding allows directional deformation to be extracted from purely resistive signals using a compact and scalable design. To address nonlinear coupling under dynamic loading, we develop a task-specific machine learning framework that achieves recognition accuracies exceeding 91% across all sensing dimensions. Integrated onto a soft robotic gripper, the system enables real-time identification of grasping direction, slip-related deformation, and object temperature during manipulation. By combining minimal hardware complexity with data-driven interpretation, this work advances multifunctional sensing skins for safe, adaptive, and intelligent robotic manipulation in unstructured environments.

title: Smart adsorption systems: Combining electrospun PEI-PAN-GO membranes with deep learning models for real-time prediction and optimization of pollutant removal efficiency
abstract: A versatile PEI-PAN-GO nanofiber membrane was successfully fabricated via electrospinning for the efficient removal of anionic and cationic dyes, namely, Congo Red (CR) and Methylene Blue (MB), and the antibiotic ciprofloxacin (CIP), from aqueous solutions. The membrane exhibited significantly improved mechanical strength, hydrophilicity, and adsorption capacity owing to the synergistic interactions among polyethyleneimine (PEI), polyacrylonitrile (PAN), and graphene oxide (GO). Batch adsorption experiments revealed a strong pH dependence, with maximum removal efficiencies for CR and CIP achieved at pH 2, and for MB at pH 8. The highest removal efficiency was observed for CIP (96.5%), followed by CR (93.2%) and MB (77.4%). Kinetic studies conformed to the pseudo-second-order model, with activation energies of 13.22, 16.01, and 7.69 kJ/mol for CR, MB, and CIP, respectively, indicating a predominantly non-covalent adsorption mechanism (physisorption) with low kinetic barriers, consistent with electrostatic, hydrogen bonding, and π–π stacking interactions. Among the tested isotherm models, the Dubinin–Radushkevich (D–R) model provided the best fit to the experimental data. The thermodynamic parameters confirmed that the adsorption process was spontaneous (ΔSο < 0) and endothermic (ΔHο > 0). Furthermore, the membrane demonstrated excellent reusability, retaining a high removal efficiency with only a 12% decline after five consecutive adsorption–desorption cycles. Four machine learning models were developed to predict removal efficiency across all pollutants, incorporating operational parameters and a coded pollutant type feature (0, 1, or 2). BPNN and Random Forest demonstrated excellent generalization (test R2 = 0.95–0.96, RMSE ≈ 7%), effectively modeling complex pH-dependent interactions, while SVM and XGBoost exhibited overfitting (test R2 = 0.83–0.87) due to CIP amphoteric behavior. The superior performance of BPNN and Random Forest confirms the PEI-PAN-GO membrane as a high-performance adsorbent for the removal of dyes and antibiotics.

title: Mussel-inspired multifunctional supramolecular hydrogel sensor enabled by machine learning for Morse code information communication
abstract: Multifunctional hydrogel sensors have garnered significant interest for their potential in emerging applications such as health monitoring, wearable electronics and human-machine interfaces. However, practical deployment remains challenging due to the difficulty in integrating key functionalities including mechanical robustness, self-healing, environmental stability, strong adhesion, and high conductivity within a single material system. Herein, we present a mussel-inspired polyvinyl alcohol/sodium alginate/polydopamine/borax (PSPB) hydrogel fabricated via a straightforward one-pot method, based on a supramolecular coupling effect of ionic coordination, reversible borate ester bonds, and hydrogen bonding. Benefiting from these intermolecular interactions, PSPB hydrogel demonstrates high fracture strength, excellent elongation, good conductivity, universal adhesion, rapid self-repairing capability with high efficiency, and frost resistance. Owing to its strong skin adhesion and low interfacial impedance, PSPB hydrogel-based strain sensor enables real-time motion recognition and high-quality recording of electrophysiological signals even under demanding conditions. Remarkably, integrated with machine learning-assisted signal processing, the PSPB hydrogel sensor shows great potential for Morse code communication, remote medical monitoring and real-time transmission of emergency information. This work highlights its promise for intelligent healthcare and assistive communication systems by enabling advanced human-machine interaction, voice activity detection, and proactive health management

title: A machine learning-assisted multi-criteria decision making framework for chemical reactor channel geometry selection
abstract: Additive manufacturing enables the realization of diverse and complex reactor channel geometries, substantially increasing the number of feasible design variants. While this design freedom offers opportunities for improved performance, it also complicates the systematic selection of geometries suitable for a given application. This paper presents a data-driven framework to support this selection process in the early reactor concept design phase. The framework employs surrogate models to predict key physical characteristics such as heat transfer, radial temperature difference, pressure drop, and flow profile, and integrates these into a multi-criteria decision making method to guide process engineers in selecting appropriate channel geometries. By focusing on fundamental physical characteristics rather than reaction-specific results, the framework ensures that the surrogate models remain transferable across different reaction systems. Incorporating probabilistic dimensioning further narrows the solution space and reduces the need for iterative experimental campaigns or computationally demanding simulations in reactor design. The applicability of the proposed framework is demonstrated through two case studies in methanol synthesis, highlighting its potential to streamline early-stage reactor development.

title: Explainable machine learning-driven design of porous adsorbents for CO2 capture under humid conditions
abstract: The efficient capture of CO2 from humid gas streams remains a major challenge for carbon-mitigation technologies because water vapor induces strong competitive adsorption in porous adsorbents. Elucidating the underlying mechanisms of CO2 selective adsorption under humid conditions is essential for the rational design of adsorbents in realistic environments. This study integrates machine learning-based multicomponent (CO2, H2O and N2) adsorption modeling, experimental methods and molecular simulations to investigate the key factors governing CO2 separation in humid mixed-gas environments. The results show that the narrow micropore volume and specific surface area are the dominant structural factors governing the CO2 adsorption capacity of porous materials, whereas nitrogen doping primarily enhances CO2 capture capacity and selectivity under low-pressure and high-temperature conditions. The adsorption mechanism of H2O exhibits pronounced differences across humidity ranges. At relative humidity (RH) < 60%, adsorption is dominated by hydrogen bonding or electrostatic interactions at oxygen polar sites. Under high-humidity conditions (RH > 60%), water molecules progressively form clusters and undergo pore filling, with mesopores providing sufficient space for cluster growth and thus becoming the dominant factor governing adsorption. In addition, surface hydrophobic modifications such as silanization and fluorination can markedly suppress H2O adsorption and enhance the selectivity of CO2. Based on these findings, we synthesized a hydrophobic microporous carbon-based adsorbent with a water contact angle of 144.07°. The material exhibits dynamic separation coefficients of 0.229 for CO2/H2O and 6.694 for CO2/N2 in a CO2/H2O/N2 (0.15/0.05/0.80) mixed-gas system. This study establishes a predictive framework for CO2 capture in porous materials under humid conditions and elucidates the synergistic effects of physicochemical properties on adsorption performance, providing guidance for the rational design of moisture-resistant CO2 adsorbents.

title: DL-driven dual-modal proprioceptive-exteroceptive fusion for multi-joint soft grippers
abstract: Dexterous multi-joint pneumatic soft grippers are indispensable for daily object manipulation due to their inherent compliance. However, existing research suffers from a critical trade-off: multi-joint soft grippers only enable single-modal sensing, while dual-modal perception is limited to single-joint structures, which impedes precise control in complex scenarios. To address this issue, we propose the DM-BioGrip—a bio-inspired, deep learning (DL)-driven dual-modal proprioceptive-exteroceptive fusion system for multi-joint soft grippers, based on an optimized 6 wt% carbon black/silicone composite. This composite exhibit super stretchability (>300% strain) and reliable sensitivity with a gauge factor of 5.9 ± 0.37 (mean ± standard deviation, n = 5) at 200% strain, and the distributed sensing array of DM-BioGrip (6 proprioceptive sensors and 28 exteroceptive sensors) enables synchronous and high-precision capture of multi-joint bending states and contact interaction features. Experimental results from 10-fold cross-validation on 7 categories of spherical objects (900 grasping trials per object) show that the DL fusion strategy of DM-BioGrip achieves a 99.7% object recognition accuracy, outperforming the exteroceptive-only (99.0%) and proprioceptive-only (96.6%) single-modal strategies by resolving feature overlaps in single-modal perception. This work pioneers an integrated dual-modal perception strategy for multi-joint soft grippers, offering a practical and reliable solution for intelligent daily object manipulation and the engineering deployment of such devices.

title: One-step fabrication of bioinspired dual-domain hierarchical wrinkled superhydrophobic strain sensors for intelligent perception
abstract: Flexible strain sensors face a fundamental trade-off between sensitivity and sensing range. Furthermore, the interfacial modulus mismatch induced by traditional multi-step fabrication often leads to delamination under complex operating conditions. Inspired by the hierarchical skin morphology of crocodile flanks, we report a one-step regional spraying method to fabricate a superhydrophobic sensor. Driven by a strain-stiffness mismatch, this sensor features a dual-domain hierarchical parallel wrinkled structure, consisting of a polydimethylsiloxane/carbon nanotubes (PDMS/CNTs) composite integrated onto a flexible latex substrate. By differentially modulating the microscopic conductive spacing, this structure achieves an exceptional hierarchical electromechanical response. Specifically, the dense wrinkles in the thin regions act as "strain amplifiers," inducing the rupture of percolation pathways under minute deformations. Conversely, the broad and sparse wrinkles in the thick regions function as "geometric strain buffers," maintaining the connectivity of the conductive network under large strains through geometric unfolding. Moreover, the in-situ induced wrinkles construct a stable Cassie-Baxter superhydrophobic barrier. This integrated "structure-interface-function" design effectively resolves the sensitivity-sensing range trade-off, delivering a high gauge factor (GF) of 7825.3 alongside a broad sensing range of 212%. The sensor additionally exhibits a low detection limit (0.5%), low hysteresis (4.82% at an extreme strain of 200%), and a rapid response time (180 ms). Crucially, the sensor maintains stable electrical and interfacial performance even after 20,000 s of dynamic fatigue testing, immersion in highly corrosive environments, and continuous fluid scouring. Integrated with machine learning clustering algorithms, the proposed sensor exhibits promising potential for intelligent interaction and advanced engineering applications across complex scenarios, including multidimensional physiological monitoring, underwater robotic perception, and tactile object recognition for smart grippers.

title: Alginate-aerogel-framework integrated with bismuth oxyhalide-based Z-scheme heterostructure for the photocatalytic degradation of ofloxacin: Mechanistic insights and machine learning modeling
abstract: The practical implementation of slurry-based photocatalytic reactors is limited by catalyst separation and operational stability. In this regard, sodium-alginate (SA) aerogel beads loaded with Bi12O15Cl6/Fe2O3@C (BFC-II) photocatalyst (BFC-II/SA-aerogel beads) were prepared and tested for the visible-light-driven degradation of ofloxacin (OLX), both in batch and continuous mode. BFC-II/SA-aerogel beads were fabricated by introducing BFC-II photocatalyst into the alginate matrix during hydrogel preparation, and thereafter freeze-dried to obtain a porous aerogel framework. Under optimal conditions, 94.4% of OLX degradation on BFC-II/SA-aerogel beads (batch mode) was recorded after 150 min of reaction time, ascribed to their porous structure, which improved BFC-II photocatalyst dispersion and reduced agglomeration. Moreover, the polymeric framework promotes light scattering and efficient charge transfer. In continuous operation, OLX degradation was slightly lower than in batch mode. Nevertheless, the photocatalytic system exhibited stable performance over multiple cycles, with a degradation efficiency loss of less than 10%. The radical scavenging study, supported by electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) analysis, revealed that O2•− primarily facilitated the photocatalytic degradation of OLX. Nearly half of the degradation products (DPs) of OLX, were found to be outside the toxic range. In addition, the possible transformations of DPs under abiotic environmental conditions were determined using BioTransformer 3.0, and the subsequent changes in ecotoxicity were evaluated in silico. Lastly, machine learning models were employed to model the experimental data, among which XGBoost demonstrated the best predictive performance with the highest R2 value (~ 0.99).

title: Sustainable production of WTR-derived adsorbents: Integrating life cycle assessment, hotspot analysis, and process optimization
abstract: Municipal drinking water treatment residuals are commonly landfilled despite containing aluminosilicate and metal hydroxide phases that can be converted into functional adsorbents. However, waste-derived materials are not inherently environmentally beneficial, particularly when chemical activation and thermal processing are required. This study developed ZnCl₂-activated adsorbents from water treatment residuals (WTR) and integrated material characterization, cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment, and machine-learning-based multi-objective optimization to identify synthesis conditions that balance adsorbent characteristics with environmental burden. Five synthesis scenarios were evaluated by varying pyrolysis temperature and ZnCl₂/WTR ratio. The optimal condition, 500 °C and ZnCl₂/WTR = 1.5, increased BET surface area from 107.97 to 271.38 m 2 g −1 and produced a micro-mesoporous structure while retaining surface hydroxyl functionality. ReCiPe 2016 midpoint and endpoint results showed that adsorbent production imposed higher impacts than direct landfilling per kilogram of WTR managed, mainly due to ZnCl₂ production, thermal energy demand, and drying operations. However, when expressed per kilogram of adsorbent, the optimized material showed a global warming potential of 5.35 kg CO₂ eq kg −1 , below reported coal-derived activated carbon benchmarks. Gaussian Process Regression coupled with Differential Evolution identified the 500 °C, 1.5 ratio condition as the sole Pareto rank-1 solution within the investigated design space. This study highlights that waste valorization is not inherently sustainable and becomes environmentally defensible only when process design is constrained by life cycle performance rather than driven solely by material optimization.

title: Maze-like crack networks guided by wrinkles in MXene/PDMS for machine learning-assisted flexible strain sensing
abstract: Simultaneously integrating high sensitivity, a wide linear range, and robust cyclic stability into a single flexible strain sensor remains a critical yet unresolved challenge for wearable electronics. Herein, we report a facile and scalable strategy to fabricate a MXene/PDMS sensor that employs isotropic wrinkle microstructures to guide the formation of a maze-like crack network (MCN). A critical “peak pinning” effect induced by these wrinkles effectively suppresses catastrophic crack propagation while promoting the progressive generation of the MCN, which inherits the meandering characteristics of the wrinkles. By precisely tuning the MXene deposition density (0.5–4 g m−2), both the wrinkle and crack geometry as well as the resultant piezoresistive properties can be tailored. Consequently, the optimized sensor achieves an exceptional balance of performance metrics: a high gauge factor of 518.7, a broad linear working range of 62.2%, fast response and recovery times (13 ms and 42 ms, respectively), and robust durability exceeding 1000 cycles. The device demonstrates versatile monitoring capabilities across a full spectrum of human activities, spanning subtle physiological signals (e.g., arterial pulse waves and laryngeal vibrations) to large-amplitude joint movements. Furthermore, when integrated with an XGBoost ensemble machine learning algorithm, the sensor enables a smart sensing system that achieves 95.0% classification accuracy for complex hand gestures. Collectively, this work presents a synergistic approach combining scalable fabrication, engineered microstructures, and artificial intelligence (AI)-enhanced data processing to advance the development of next-generation human-machine interfaces.

title: Artificial intelligence-driven discovery and rational design of antimicrobial materials: Bridging data and biology
abstract: The escalating threat of multidrug resistant microorganisms and biofilm infection calls for potent alternatives to conventional antibiotics. Artificial intelligence is transforming antimicrobial material discovery and optimization by enabling high throughput screening, guiding rational design, accelerating candidate prioritization, and elucidating mechanisms of action. This review outlines a full pipeline for AI-driven antimicrobial screening/design across diverse material classes, including antimicrobial peptides, metal–phenolic networks, hydrogels, and nanozymes and beyond. It begins by introducing fundamental principles of antimicrobial mechanisms and AI methodologies, then systematically dissects the AI-driven research workflow encompassing data handling, feature engineering, model training, experimental validation, and iterative refinement. Subsequent sections illustrate the application of this pipeline to each material class through representative case studies, followed by a cross-class comparison that identifies convergent design principles. It then discusses how AI strategies tackle long-standing challenges including biofilm complexity, selective targeting, resistance circumvention, and the trade-off between antimicrobial efficacy and host compatibility. The review further emphasizes how AI enables application-specific customization, translating varying antimicrobial clinical demands (e.g., those from orthopaedics, wound care, pulmonary infections, and ocular diseases) into quantifiable design parameters and criteria. Moreover, it analyzes the future opportunities and challenges for research innovation and clinical translation. By bridging data and biology, this review provides insights to guide rational development of next-generation antimicrobial therapeutics for advanced healthcare.

title: Coupled adsorption–desorption machine learning modeling for predicting inorganic ion retention on iron minerals
abstract: Iron minerals play a critical role in regulating the geochemical cycling of pollutants, yet quantitative prediction of inorganic ion retention at the mineral–water interface remains challenging due to the predominant focus on adsorption while overlooking the desorption process. Herein, an integrated machine learning (ML) framework was established to model both adsorption and desorption behaviors across diverse iron mineral–inorganic ion systems, enabling a quantitative evaluation of the long-term retention capacity and binding stability. A comprehensive adsorption–desorption database was compiled, and separate models were constructed to predict adsorption and desorption efficiencies, achieving strong predictive performance (R2 = 0.948 and 0.917; MAE = 4.772 and 5.317, respectively). SHAP analysis revealed distinct factors controlling these two processes. Adsorption was primarily influenced by environmental conditions and ion properties, while desorption was mainly governed by mineral properties, particularly specific surface area (SSA). Although SSA enhanced both adsorption and desorption, its net influence on binding stability was ambiguous, indicating that the long-term retention capacity cannot be reliably inferred from adsorption alone. Employing model predictions, binding stability was quantified through retention amount and hysteresis index (HI), revealing strong release tendencies for heavy metal cations such as Cd(II), Co(II), and Cu(II), and limited immobilization capacity of magnetite for most inorganic ions. This work established a unified adsorption–desorption modeling framework that advanced the quantitative prediction of inorganic ion retention and mobility at the mineral–water interface, offering a novel approach for stability-aware environmental risk assessment.

title: Rapid particulate microplastics removal from stormwater: Distinct adsorption behavior and data-driven intelligent prediction
abstract: Rapid and efficient removal of MPs from stormwater runoff is essential for mitigating MPs pollution risks in aquatic environments. However, the applicability of conventional adsorption models to MPs capture by superhydrophobic materials and precise machine-learning prediction tools remain underexplored. In this study, experimental studies combined with artificial neural network (ANN) modeling were conducted to investigate the adsorption behavior and mechanism of typical MPs in stormwater runoff. The results showed that MOF-modified superhydrophobic quartz could achieve rapid and efficient capture of PP, PE, and PET within 15 min, with maximum removal efficiency reaching 98.89%, 98.54%, and 97.33%, respectively. The adsorption dynamics were appropriately described by the pseudo-second-order kinetic model. For isotherms, the Sips model outperformed Langmuir and Freundlich models, whereas conventional models showed significant deviations in adsorption capacity at higher equilibrium concentrations, highlighting the limitations in capturing secondary adsorption from hydrophobic aggregation of MPs. To overcome the shortcomings of back-propagation (BP) neural networks, a sparrow search algorithm–optimized ANN (SSA-BP-ANN) was applied for MPs adsorption system and three prediction models were constructed. The R2 values of these models were 0.9922, 0.9989, and 0.9965, outperforming LR, RF, and GBR, which accurately predicted the removal efficiencies of PP, PE, and PET. SHAP analysis indicated that initial MPs concentration and adsorbent dosage had the most significant impacts on the removal efficiency, followed by pH and contact time, whereas temperature contributed the least. This study expanded our understanding of MPs removal from stormwater by MOF-modified superhydrophobic materials and provided valuable insights into adsorption modeling and machine-learning prediction.

title: Machine learning-guided sustainable human type I collagen fragment production in engineered microbial cells for tissue engineering
abstract: Collagen is widely used as a biomaterial in tissue engineering and regenerative medicine. However, growing concerns over animal-derived sources have motivated the development of synthetic human collagen to minimize associated risks. Here, we present a synthetic biology strategy for microbial production of human type I collagen (hCOL1) fragment, integrating machine learning with biofoundry-driven workflows. Using an ESM-2 protein language model combined with biofoundry-based strain development, context-dependent synthetic signal peptides (SP) were designed and evaluated. This approach achieved the production and secretion of hCOL1 fragments in Corynebacterium glutamicum as an industrial host at 24.3 ± 3 mg/L after the third round of strain engineering, representing a 4.9-fold increase compared with the native SP in the first round. Next, scalable hCOL1 fragment production was demonstrated in 5-L fermenters, achieving titers of 857 ± 75 mg/L in fed-batch cultivations using glucose. To validate its potential as a tissue engineering biomaterial, the collagen-based biocomposite scaffolds were fabricated and used to culture human adipose-derived stem cells. The engineered matrices significantly enhanced proliferation and stemness marker expression, surpassing conventional animal-derived collagens. Active learning for context- and host-dependent SP design can facilitate the secretion of not only collagen but also other proteins of interest.

title: Multifunctional conductive hydrogel fibers with high stretchability, anti-freezing, and anti-swelling for wearable strain sensors and deep learning-assisted sign language recognition
abstract: Fiber-based sensors have attracted extensive attention in wearable electronics owing to their high conductivity, exceptional flexibility and the structural versatility of one-dimensional architectures. Despite significant advancements in hydrogel fiber fabrication techniques, the continuous production of multifunctional conductive hydrogel fibers (CHFs) simultaneously endowed with good mechanical properties, high conductivity, anti-freezing capability, anti-swelling performance, and a broad sensing range remains challenging. In this study, a dynamic crosslinking spinning (DCS) strategy consisting of a two-step photo-crosslinking process and a post-drawing technique was employed to construct a multi-crosslinked composite network structure and further achieve the oriented arrangement of polymer networks, thereby successfully fabricating continuous multifunctional CHFs. The two-step photo-crosslinking process achieved continuous spinning from solution to gel fibers. The post-drawing process induces the alignment of randomly distributed network structure in CHFs along the stretching direction, thereby enhancing their mechanical properties (with a breaking strength of up to 12.62 MPa). Moreover, the incorporation of ionic liquids (ILs) and Zr4+ not only improves the conductivity of CHFs but also endows them with excellent anti-freezing capability (about −45 °C). Furthermore, supramolecular interactions such as hydrogen bonding, electrostatic interactions, and metal coordination bonds within CHFs contribute to their remarkable anti-swelling performance in various solvents. The fiber sensor exhibits a wide detection range (0–1300%) and high sensitivity (gauge factor, GF = 5.29), enabling it to detect human motions and physiological signals such as pulse waves. Additionally, we demonstrate the application of the fiber sensors in human-machine interaction (HMI), as well as for sign language recognition and translation through a deep learning-assisted recognition system.

title: Self-powered vibration online monitoring of power transformers enabled by triboelectric nanogenerator
abstract: As critical electrical equipment in power grids, power transformers pose substantial operational risks and financial losses once major faults occur. Traditional detection methods, relying primarily on manual inspection, are unable to provide real-time monitoring of transformer operational states. In this work, we develop a self-powered vibration online monitoring system of power transformers designed for continuous condition surveillance. Central to this system is the proposed composite spring-type triboelectric nanogenerator vibration sensor (CST-TEVS), which can effectively capture vibration signals with low accelerations (0–0.6 g) and broadband (100–500 Hz) characteristics of transformer operation. Building on this, an intelligent diagnostic framework integrating Hierarchical Decremental Multi-scale convolution (HD-Multiscale) and a Squeeze-and-Excitation enhanced Residual network is developed, achieving transformer condition identification accuracy exceeding 99%. Furthermore, a dedicated visualization interface enables real-time presentation of vibration signals and diagnostic outcomes. This work demonstrates a reliable and scalable route for intelligent, autonomous substation monitoring—effectively bridging vibration sensing, intelligent diagnostics, and visualization into a unified system.

title: Hybrid dataset of real-and-simulated pulse waveforms for deep learning-driven blood pressure estimation using MXene-based iontronic sensors
abstract: Deep learning-based non-invasive blood pressure (BP) estimation is emerging for cardiovascular disease management, yet it remains constrained by the scarcity of biomedical data and the difficulty of building physiologically faithful training datasets from limited cohorts. In this study, a hybrid framework integrating physiologically grounded PDA-based data augmentation, CNN-LSTM architecture, and MXene-based pseudocapacitive iontronic pressure sensor is presented for BP estimation from radial artery pulse waveforms. The sensor, incorporating MXene electrodes and an ionic liquid/polymer dielectric layer, exhibited high sensitivity (101 kPa−1), fast response time (43 ms), and mechanical durability exceeding 10,000 load cycles. With a high areal capacitance of 161.9 mF/cm2, the sensor enabled stable acquisition of radial artery waveforms. To overcome the data limitations of biomedical research, the proposed simulator was utilized to expand the limited reference cohort within its physiological distribution, enabling the hybrid architecture to jointly learn time-series pulse characteristics and BP features. The model achieved R2 values of 0.907 and 0.904 for systolic and diastolic BP, with mean absolute errors of −2.16 and 2.99 mmHg, respectively. The proposed framework thus offers a physiologically grounded approach to BP estimation that addresses biomedical data limitations, with the potential to be applied to other limited cohorts in clinical and biomedical research.

title: Machine learning-enabled prediction of enzymatic saccharification of agricultural residues for biorefinery
abstract: Due to the high heterogeneity of substrates and the inherent complexity of enzymatic hydrolysis, the structure–activity relationships governing lignocellulosic saccharification exhibit strong nonlinearity and remain a major prediction bottleneck. In this study, a machine learning framework was developed using a multi-dimensional dataset of 150 lignocellulosic samples to quantify the nonlinear relationships between substrate characteristics and sugar yield. The CatBoost algorithm achieved superior predictive accuracy (R2 > 0.91), outperforming conventional regression models. SHAP analysis identified feedstock origin and cellulose crystallinity as the dominant factors governing hydrolysis kinetics, while Generalized Additive Models revealed optimal operating ranges for each parameter. Critically, the resulting prediction platform enables real-time estimation of enzymatic efficiency for diverse feedstocks. This data-driven approach accelerates the transition from lab-scale biomass conversion to scalable industrial applications in biorefinery.

title: Multi-scale error-triggered latent assimilation for reduced-order digital twins of gas–solid flow reactors
abstract: Gas-solid flow reactors are complex dynamical systems in chemical engineering, characterised by highly coupled, multi-scale physical fields that evolve over space and time. Accurate and efficient prediction of these reactors is essential for monitoring and optimisation, yet remains challenging due to limited and noisy measurements for validation, as well as the prohibitive cost of large-scale high-fidelity simulations. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes a correction-enhanced reduced-order modelling (ROM) approach with multi-scale latent assimilation for gas-solid flow reactors. The method conditionally corrects the prior predictions obtained from a data-driven ROM by assimilating observations in a low-dimensional latent space. In the offline stage, multi-scale Proper Orthogonal Decomposition and β -Variational Autoencoder (mPOD– β -VAE)compress the system into multi-scale latent spaces, significantly reducing both dimensionality and computational cost. During the online stage, forecast errors between the encoded observations and the ROM prediction are checked. When this error exceeds a dynamically determined threshold value, latent assimilation is triggered to update the prior latent state using an ensemble Kalman filter. The corrected latent state is subsequently decoded and reconstructed to obtain a more accurate state estimate. This methodology is demonstrated using a lab-scale fluidised bed reactor. The results show that the proposed framework achieves superior reconstruction of both observable and unobservable variables, reduces latent-state prediction errors through stable and well-conditioned assimilation updates, and delivers a substantial reduction of computational load. This approach reduces the computational complexity by 99.8% compared to conventional CFD-DEM and improves predictive accuracy by 44.4% over a standalone ROM, while maintaining a computational cost comparable to the standalone ROM. Overall, the proposed approach offers a promising tool for real-time prediction and monitoring in chemical engineering applications, paving the way towards a next-generation digital twin for gas-solid flow reactors.

title: Machine learning enabled fluorescence sensing platform via alginic acid carbon dots for ultrasensitive polyphenol flavonoid quantification
abstract: Flavonoids are a key class of natural polyphenols that serve an important role in human health; therefore, their accurate detection is crucial. However, their structural diversity and often low concentrations in complex media make their rapid, ultrasensitive detection and measurement very challenging. To address this concern, a fluorescence-sensing platform using Carbon dots (C-dots) has been developed. In this study, C-dots were synthesised using alginic acid via a hydrothermal approach. The synthesised C-dots exhibited brilliant blue emissions, and various characterisation methods were used to investigate their structure and shape. The fluorescence experiment further showed that the C-dots displayed selective and unique fluorescence quenching in the presence of polyphenol flavonoids (quercetin and rutin), with LODs of 0.0158 nM (15.8 pM) for quercetin and 0.005413 nM (5.413 pM) for rutin, respectively. Quenching behaviour at 360 nm can help identify flavonoid polyphenols, such as quercetin and rutin. Furthermore, Real-time analysis is conducted using red wine and onion juice, demonstrating the practical application of the prepared sensor. Moreover, it was possible to predict flavonoid concentrations with accuracy using a combination of several machine learning algorithms (RF, MLP, and XGBoost) with the sensor array. The Random Forest (RF) technique achieved 94% accuracy, outperforming the others. This increased prediction accuracy demonstrates the utility of these techniques for rapid, sensitive measurement, thereby improving flavonoid quantification.

title: Unveiling microbial sulfate reduction in Acid Mine Drainage Treatment using a Chained Environmental-Microbial machine learning approach
abstract: Expanded granular sludge bed (EGSB) reactors employing sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB) are widely used for treating acid mine drainage (AMD) characterized by low pH, high sulfate, and heavy metal content, owing to their excellent mass transfer efficiency and shock load resistance. However, conventional prediction models typically rely solely on operational and physicochemical parameters to evaluate sulfate removal efficiency, failing to adequately incorporate high-dimensional microbial functional data, which limits both predictive accuracy and mechanistic interpretation. To address these limitations, this study developed an Environment-Biology (EB) integrated model based on 120-day EGSB reactor experimental data, using FAPROTAX functional annotation to reduce the dimensionality of microbial features. This model achieved a prediction R2 of 0.76 for sulfate removal efficiency, representing a 31% improvement over environment-only models. Analysis revealed sulfate metabolism abundance as the most important predictor (42.7% contribution), with C/S ratio and pH jointly regulating the removal process. Furthermore, a staged modeling strategy was implemented: first establishing a predictive model between environmental parameters and sulfate metabolism abundance (R2 = 0.80), then using the predicted abundance as a biological proxy variable alongside environmental parameters in sulfate removal efficiency prediction. The final model achieved comparable performance (R2 = 0.78) to models using directly measured microbial data. This chained modeling approach enables reliable system simulation and optimization without high-throughput sequencing, providing a novel methodology for accurate prediction and control of complex biological treatment systems.

title: Deep learning-assisted chemiresistive sensor arrays for postharvest maturity identification via fruit-emitted mixed gas monitoring
abstract: Plants maintain continuous gaseous exchange with their surroundings, and the volatile organic compounds (VOCs) they emit can act as indicators of plant physiological status. As an important plant organ, fruit maintains active physiological metabolism, including during the postharvest stage. Therefore, the detection of volatile compounds in postharvest fruits can be used to evaluate the quality and monitor their spoilage during storage and transportation. However, current gas detection instruments are mostly benchtop devices that are bulky and costly, making them unsuitable for practical industrial applications. Thus, developing gas-based rapid maturation assessment technologies for fruits is growing increasingly essential. In this study, we developed an intelligent monitoring system for fruit ripening process monitoring, with mangoes chosen as the research subject. Specifically, ethylene, ethanol, ethyl acetate and dipentene were identified as four target gases based on the detection results of VOCs released by mangoes during storage via solid-phase microextraction combined with gas chromatography–mass spectrometry. To detect these signals, a 4-sensor array was constructed using SnO2 nanospheres functionalized with palladium nanoparticles, leveraging resistance variations to capture the dynamics of gases.
