Six regression algorithms were compared using a four-factor experimental dataset, and SHapley additive explanations (SHAP) were applied to the selected models to assess the contributions of operating variables to predicted removal efficiencies within the investigated range. Together, these findings support an adsorption-oxidation-fixation pathway at the process level. Ib-FeNPs also showed good reusability over five cycles and achieved 80.0% total arsenic removal in a fixed-bed experiment with acid mine drainage (AMD). Overall, Ib-FeNPs provide a plant-mediated platform for arsenic-contaminated water remediation, while the integrated machine-learning and characterization framework offers a transferable approach to developing bio-nano adsorbents from underutilized biomass.

title: Label-free SERS diagnosis of colorectal cancer assisted by machine learning and integrated with recyclable polyurethane sensor chips
abstract: Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) is widely used in cancer liquid biopsy due to its rapid, sensitive, and non-invasive nature. In this study, bimetallic silver and gold nanoparticles (Ag NPs/Au NPs) were uniformly deposited onto cellulose filter paper (CFP) via three-phase liquid-liquid interface self-assembly. Subsequently, a polyurethane (PU) coating was applied to the CFP surface to obtain a high-performance PU-Ag NPs/Au NPs-CFP SERS sensor for rapid colorectal cancer (CRC) screening. Sensor stability was improved by the PU coating, and the PU-Ag NPs/Au NPs-CFP substrate exhibited stronger SERS enhancement than the uncoated substrate under various conditions, including temperatures from −80 °C to 60 °C and hydrogen peroxide solutions (≤ 3.00%). After 270 days, 87.49% of the initial SERS signal was retained, indicating long-term usability. The substrate also maintained stable SERS signals over five cycles, with a relative standard deviation (RSD) of 3.08%, showing potential for recyclability. More importantly, the PU coating effectively reduced protein interference during serum detection. As confirmed by comparative spectral analysis, this allowed accurate identification of diagnostic metabolite fingerprints in the serum. SERS spectra of serum samples from 50 CRC patients and 50 healthy controls (HC) were acquired using a portable Raman spectrometer, and four machine learning (ML) algorithms were applied for classification. Among them, the support vector machine (SVM) model performed best. At the spectral level, it achieved 94.25% accuracy and 88.50% specificity; at the patient level, it achieved 95.00% accuracy and 90.00% specificity. This study integrates a recyclable and stable SERS sensor with ML, offering a new solution for efficient, non-invasive, and low-cost CRC screening.

title: Feature-fusion cascaded neural network (FFCCN)-assisted optical sensor array for simultaneous detection of multiple pollutants in edible oil based on four-signal fluorescent copper-based nanozyme
abstract: Rapid and reliable identification of diverse pollutants in edible oils remains challenging due to complex matrices and insufficient sensing dimensionality. Herein, we report a multifunctional copper-based nanozyme (Cu-TTPDC) constructed via coordination between Cu2+ ions and a thiadiazole-containing aromatic dicarboxylate ligand, which integrates intrinsic fluorescence with peroxidase (POD)-, laccase (LAC)-, and superoxide dismutase (SOD)-like activities within a single framework. Unlike conventional sensor arrays assembled from multiple sensing elements, Cu-TTPDC provides four complementary optical responses—three catalytic colorimetric channels and one fluorescent channel—thereby simplifying array construction while retaining multidimensional sensing information. The single-material array generates distinct response fingerprints for eight representative pollutants spanning heavy-metal, phenolic-compound, and pesticide categories, including lead(II) ions (Pb2+), gossypol (GSP), fenthion (FEN), aldicarb (ALD), glyphosate (GLY), flusilazole (FLZ), fluorodifen (DCF), and 2-cyclohexyl-4,6-dinitrophenol (DCP). To decode the correlated and nonlinear multichannel patterns, a feature-fusion cascaded classification network (FFCCN) was developed. The network learns a shared representation directly from the four response channels and concatenates this representation with the predicted pollutant-probability vector in the concentration branch, thereby conditioning concentration-level discrimination on pollutant identity without using the true pollutant label. Under four-fold nested cross-validation, the model achieved out-of-fold accuracies of 91.3% for pollutant identification and 88.1% for five-level concentration discrimination, with an 84.4% joint accuracy. Detection limits as low as 0.15 μg·mL−1. This single-material four-channel array coupled with cascaded learning provides a compact approach for multidimensional screening of chemically diverse hazards in edible oils.

title: Machine learning-assisted mixed-valence Fe/Cu nanozyme dual-channel sensing platform for high-throughput discrimination of antioxidants
abstract: Accurate identification and quantitative analysis of antioxidants in complex biological fluids are the keys to the early detection of severe diseases. The single-channel sensors suffer from weak specificity and critical multi-component signal crosstalk, which hardly meet the accurate analytical requirements. Herein, an intelligent colorimetric sensing platform of bimetallic mixed-valence nanozyme was integrated with machine learning (ML) to improve the analytical precision. Fe/Cu nanosheets of mixed valence were successfully acquired through Cu2O-coordinated anchoring in situ into iron porphyrin (TCPP(Fe)). This mixed-valence strategy effectively promoted the synergistic catalysis and valence cycling among the metal active sites, thereby significantly enhancing the peroxidase (POD)-like activity of the Cu2O/Cu-TCPP(Fe) (Vmax as high as 8.107 × 10−7 M·s−1 and Km as low as 0.913 mM). DFT calculations indicated that the introduction of Cu2O promoted strong Cu 3d and Fe 3d orbital hybridization and an upshift of the Cu d-band center, accelerating interfacial electron transfer and Fe/Cu valence cycling, thereby revealing the intrinsic mechanism underlying the enhanced catalytic activity. Taking the differential catalytic responses of the nanozyme with two different substrates, a highly sensitive dual-channel sensor array was designed with machine learning. Combined with algorithms of artificial neural network (ANN), random forest (RF), and support vector machine (SVM), etc., 100% accurate qualitative discrimination of six antioxidants was remarkably completed. Relying on the outstanding capability of the Random Forest (RF) algorithm to remarkable robustness in handling high-dimensional sample datasets, the sensor array successfully established a precise quantitative model for multiple antioxidants in complex samples, remarkably and intelligently sensing the diverse components in urine and serum. This work paved a new way for highly active bimetallic nanozymes to construct a trustworthy sensing platform as a diagnostic tool for the intelligent profiling of multi-component biomarkers in complex matrices.

title: Machine-learning-assisted multidimensional kinetics and reaction mechanism for degradative solvent extraction of low-rank coal
abstract: Degradative solvent extraction (DSE) is an effective approach for the mild demineralization and upgrading of low-rank coals. However, the inherent high dimensionality and nonlinearity of the DSE reaction system hinder identification of consistent relationships between key predictors and product yields, thereby limiting a deeper understanding of the process. To overcome this limitation, a machine-learning-assisted multidimensional kinetics (ML-MK) framework was developed. This framework combines the predictive capability of machine learning with the interpretability of lumped kinetic models for interpreting apparent pathway behavior. A predictive model for DSE yield was established (R2 = 0.92), enabling quantitative assessment of predictor contributions to model outputs and providing multidimensional insights into the reaction system. The model-derived patterns indicate a temperature-dependent shift in the relative contributions of different processes. The low-temperature response is consistent with solvent-assisted transport and physical dissolution at 25–300 °C. Thermally activated coal-matrix conversion becomes increasingly important at 300–360 °C, followed by greater competition between hydrogen-assisted radical stabilization and condensation above 360 °C. Within the 300–400 °C range, the fitted fractional pathway contributions suggest an approximate, model-derived crossover near 340 °C. Below this approximate crossover, URC cracking contributes more strongly; above it, EX–UCactual interconversion has the larger modeled contribution. Overall, the ML-MK framework provides a novel and effective approach for achieving an in-depth understanding of DSE reaction processes. Moreover, the framework has application potential in fields characterized by complex reaction networks and numerous real components, such as coal liquefaction, petroleum refining, and biomass thermochemical conversion.

title: Anti-swelling and antibacterial multifunctional conductive hydrogel for flexible sensing, intestinal palpation and machine learning-assisted recognition
abstract: Multifunctional conductive hydrogels show great potential for flexible bioelectronics, but their performance is often limited by trade-offs between mechanical strength, environmental stability, and functional integration. To address this, we propose a three-step preparation strategy combining thermal polymerization, freeze-thaw cycling, and LS post-treatment to regulate a multiscale network structure. This approach combines a chemically crosslinked polymer matrix, freeze-thaw treatment, and lignosulfonate (LS) incorporation to obtain a mechanically robust multicomponent hydrogel. An ethylene glycol (EG)/water binary solvent system further enhances the hydrogel's environmental adaptability. The resulting PPSH-L hydrogel exhibits optimized mechanical and functional properties, including high strength (0.86 MPa), large stretchability, excellent fatigue resistance, and remarkable anti-swelling and anti-freezing capabilities (down to −22.6 °C). Its stable conductive network ensures high sensitivity, broad response range, rapid signal response, and excellent stability under repeated deformation. The incorporation of zwitterionic SBMA and LS provides an antibacterial interface with >95% efficiency and good biocompatibility. Leveraging these advantages, the hydrogel supports multifunctional sensing for motion monitoring, non-verbal patient-clinician communication, intestinal tactile sensing, and abnormal tissue palpation. Combined with a Transformer model, it enables intelligent recognition of tissue mechanical properties, offering a new approach for minimally invasive diagnosis. In simulated colonoscopy applications, the hydrogel effectively detects mechanical changes in abnormal intestinal tissues, enhancing early-stage lesion detection. This strategy overcomes the performance trade-offs in hydrogels and advances their applications in intelligent healthcare and flexible electronics.

title: Dual-modal signal decoupling strategy based on cascaded machine learning for intelligent food freshness monitoring
abstract: Real-time monitoring of pH and humidity is essential for evaluating food freshness. However, changes in humidity can affect ion migration, interfere with resistive pH sensing signals, and significantly hinder simultaneous accurate quantification of the two parameters. To address this challenge, a dual-mode sensing patch that combines fluorescence and resistive sensing, coupled with a cascaded machine learning framework, was developed for monitoring food freshness. The fluorescence response unit consists of a cellulose/polyvinyl alcohol composite system embedded with AuNCs. Additionally, graphene electrodes were fabricated on both sides using 3D printing technology to facilitate the simultaneous acquisition of optical and electrical signals. The fluorescence intensity increases as humidity decreases, whereas the resistance signal exhibits a linear response within the pH range of 6.0 to 9.0. To mitigate cross-interference between the dual-mode signals, a cascaded machine learning framework was developed, including random forest model and Bayesian ridge regression. Humidity information was first extracted from fluorescence features and subsequently introduced as a compensation parameter for pH prediction based on resistance signals. This hierarchical analysis framework approach effectively decoupled the coupled humidity and pH signals, enabling accurate quantification of both parameters. This strategy enables intelligent food freshness monitoring and flexible multi-parameter signal decoupling.

title: Gram-scale de novo biosynthesis of phenylethanoid glycosides in Escherichia coli via mechanism-guided AI-assisted engineering of a BAHD acyltransferase
abstract: Phenylethanoid glycosides (PhGs), such as verbascoside and echinacoside, are valuable plant natural products with significant pharmacological potential. Their sustainable supply remains a challenge due to the limitations of plant extraction and chemical synthesis. In this study, we report high-level de novo production of complex PhGs in Escherichia coli from glucose by combining machine learning-aided enzyme engineering with systematic metabolic engineering. To overcome the catalytic bottleneck of the BAHD acyltransferase SiAT1, we developed a computational pipeline that integrated deep learning with mechanistic constraints to select candidate variants for experimental screening. Subsequent experimental screening and mechanistic analysis identified Lys30 as a critical acceptor-gating residue, and the SiAT1K30A variant exhibited a 243-fold enhanced affinity for salidroside. We systematically engineered the E. coli chassis by constructing a high-yield supply module for the key precursors salidroside and p-coumaric acid, optimizing the expression of SiCYP98A20 and its reductase AaCPR, expanding the intracellular UDP-sugar pool, and introducing the RgTALS9N/A11Y mutant to redirect flux toward p-coumaric acid and alleviate the upstream supply imbalance. This integrated platform enabled fed-batch fermentation in 5-L bioreactors to achieve gram-scale de novo production of verbascoside (1.84 g/L) and echinacoside (1.35 g/L), along with an unprecedented accumulation of the key intermediate osmanthuside B (12.91 g/L). This work establishes E. coli as a scalable industrial host for complex PhGs and provides a potentially generalizable, data-driven framework that synergistically combines AI-assisted enzyme engineering with systematic metabolic engineering for the biomanufacturing of high-value plant natural products.

title: Scale-up prediction of breakthrough curves via shape–timescale decomposition in a hybrid deep learning framework
abstract: Accurate prediction of breakthrough curves (BTCs) remains a major challenge in scaling up fixed-bed adsorption systems, as conventional models often fail to generalize across operating conditions. Here, we propose a hybrid deep learning framework based on explicit decomposition of BTCs into normalized shape and characteristic timescale components. The normalized BTC shape is learned using a bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) model in a dimensionless time domain, while the characteristic breakthrough time is predicted using a multilayer perceptron (MLP). The full BTC is reconstructed through a scaling-based mapping of these two components. Trained on lab-scale datasets, the proposed model achieved high predictive accuracy for unseen pilot-scale conditions (R2 = 0.975, RMSE = 0.053), reducing prediction errors by up to 3–5 times compared to conventional end-to-end models. Interpretability analyses using Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) and accumulated local effects (ALE) reveal that the characteristic timescale is primarily governed by influent concentration and hydrodynamic conditions, with nonlinear and interaction effects consistent with expected adsorption behavior. These results demonstrate that separating intrinsic dynamics from temporal scaling provides a structurally effective and interpretable approach for robust and transferable BTC prediction, offering a new pathway for data-efficient scale-up in adsorption-based water treatment systems.

title: AI-enabled wireless gas sensor based on mesoporous Cr2O3-In2O3 heterostructure for rapid detection of 3-hydroxy-2-butanone
abstract: The growing adoption of smart food packaging, processing, and storing units demands advanced sensing systems capable of real-time food quality monitoring to enhance safety and reduce waste. This research presents a wireless miniaturized resistive gas sensor based on a mesoporous Cr2O3-In2O3 heterostructure, engineered for the highly sensitive and selective detection of 3-Hydroxy-2-Butanone (3H2B), which is a key volatile organic compound (VOC) marker of microbial spoilage in perishable foods such as dairy and meat. The synergistic interface between Cr2O3 and In2O3 optimises charge transfer and surface reactivity, enabling outstanding sensor performance with a detection limit of about 50 ppb and rapid response times under 12 s, while maintaining measurable response across a wide humidity range. These results are achieved through interdigitated electrodes with a spacing of 100 μm, enhancing sensitivity and signal stability. The mesoporous nanostructure offers high surface area and interconnected pores for rapid adsorption and diffusion, enabling consistent detection across wide concentration ranges. Wireless connectivity integrates the sensor into IoT-enabled smart packaging, processing lines, and storage facilities, streaming data to mobile, cloud, and automated control systems. AI models for supervised classification deliver instant spoilage alerts, continuous QA, and predictive inventory management across industrial and commercial supply chains. By combining advanced nanomaterials with scalable fabrication and IoT integration, this work advances the vision of intelligent, waste-minimising food systems and offers a platform for broader applications in large-scale food processing and cold-chain logistics. Data collected from multiple devices is periodically aggregated on a central server to refine the detection models. It predicts remaining shelf life from thousands of data points in order to improve predictive food quality control and also support safer and more sustainable operations.

title: High-performance “brick-mortar” MXene/CNF/PVA aerogel pressure sensors for deep-learning-assisted gesture recognition and medical communication
abstract: Communication barriers faced by patients with laryngeal disorders due to voice limitations have become a significant challenge in clinical diagnosis, and medical-patient communication, which could be potentially addressed by the wearable sensors. However, currently reported wearable sensors generally suffer from high manufacturing costs, slow response time, and limited stability. Here, inspired by “brick-mortar” porous structures, we report a MXene/cellulose nanofibers/polyvinyl alcohol (MCP) aerogel-based pressure sensor and develop the wearable smart glove to assist real-time and efficient communication during medical interactions. The pressure sensor features an ultra-low pressure detection limit (3.3 Pa), fast response and recovery time (66 ms /64 ms), a wide detection range (0–80 kPa), outstanding stability over 8000 compression cycles, and excellent thermal insulation properties at temperatures around 1600 °C, surpassing existing MXene-based aerogels pressure sensors. Further, a wearable smart glove was developed by using prepared pressure sensor array to realize multifunctional applications such as synchronized human-machine interaction (HMI) and remote media control. Combined with deep learning algorithms, the smart glove system achieved 100% recognition accuracy of 10 hand gestures. These findings provide an effective solution to the communication challenges faced by patients with speech disorders.

title: Micro-CT-based permeability characterization of virgin and pyrolyzed wood using deep learning segmentation and image-based pore-scale simulations
abstract: Permeability governs gas transport in pyrolyzing wood and strongly influences predictions of devolatilization and internal pressure build-up as the pore network evolves. We present an image-based workflow to quantify how pyrolysis modifies the intrinsic permeability tensor of Pinus pinaster (maritime pine) earlywood using synchrotron micro-CT, deep-learning segmentation, and pore-scale flow simulations. Anatomically matched submicron microtomography volumes were acquired before and after in-situ pyrolysis under nitrogen, up to 525 °C. Orientation-robust 3D pore/solid segmentation was obtained using three 2D U-Net models trained on longitudinal, radial, and tangential slice sets and fused by majority vote. Steady incompressible creeping-flow simulations, with Re ≪ 1, were then performed in OpenFOAM using simpleFoam to compute the full permeability tensor. Sensitivity analyses and a permeability-based REV study selected a representative cube size of 390 µm, corresponding to 1300³ voxels. Pyrolysis slightly increased porosity and shifted local pore diameters toward smaller values. Longitudinal and radial permeabilities decreased by 47% and 24%, whereas tangential permeability increased by a factor of 5.86, substantially reducing anisotropy. These trends indicate that pyrolysis restructures transport primarily by modifying constrictions and transverse connectivity rather than uniformly enlarging conduits.

title: Self-assembled carbon dot-based biochip for ultrasensitive multiplex biomarker detection and machine learning-assisted diagnosis of esophageal carcinoma
abstract: Early diagnosis and timely treatment of esophageal cancer (EC) remain challenging due to the lack of ultrasensitive, high-throughput, rapid, and minimally invasive approaches for multiplex protein biomarker detection in biofluids. In this study, we developed a highly efficient carbon dots (CDs)-assembled immunoassay biochip for the simultaneous detection and evaluation of six EC-related biomarkers, including CEA, CA199, CA724, HSP70, IL6, and IL8. The assembled CDs enhanced the biochip substrate by enabling high-density immobilization of capture antibody barcodes through π–π stacking and hydrogen bonding, while their surface-proximity-dependent fluorescence quenching capability effectively reduced nonspecific background fluorescence. This design achieved both high capture antibody immobilization efficiency and efficient quenching of nonspecific signals. The immunoassay biochip enabled rapid multiplex detection with a total assay time of approximately 45 min, with limits of detection (LODs) reaching the pg/mL level. The combined biomarker panels exhibited superior diagnostic capability in terms of sensitivity and specificity, with the six-marker combination providing the highest diagnostic accuracy. Furthermore, machine-learning analysis demonstrated the diagnostic potential of the six-biomarker panel for distinguishing EC patients, including different TNM-defined subgroups, from healthy donors, with accuracies generally exceeding 90%. Owing to its excellent stability, ultrasensitivity, high throughput, and reproducibility, this immunoassay biochip holds great promise for minimally invasive EC diagnosis, disease-stage assessment, and evaluation of therapeutic outcomes.

title: Hyperbranched network engineering enables tissue-soft, low-hysteresis and ultrastretchable hydrogel strain sensors for machine learning-assisted fruit recognition
abstract: Hydrogel strain sensors are promising for soft robotics and wearable electronics, but their sensing accuracy is often compromised by hysteresis arising from irreversible chain rearrangement and energy dissipation. Here, we develop a multiple reversible physical crosslinking strategy to regulate polymer-chain topology and reinforce a polymerized network through reversible multivalent interactions, thereby producing a low-hysteresis and highly stretchable (LHS) conducting polymer hydrogel. The optimized hydrogel exhibits a low Young's modulus of approximately 17 kPa, comparable in magnitude to the modulus reported for soft brain tissue, together with an elongation at break of approximately 2200%, and an electrical hysteresis ratio of 0.76% at 400% strain. The resultant strain sensor provides reversible strain-dependent resistance responses, a maximum gauge factor of 2.4, and stable operation. When four sensors are integrated into a robotic hand, the multichannel signals capture fruit-specific grasping characteristics. Coupling these signals with a lightweight one-dimensional convolutional neural network enables the classification of five fruits with an accuracy of 98.66%. These results demonstrate that hyperbranched topology regulation offers an effective route for constructing low-hysteresis conducting polymer hydrogels for high-fidelity robotic perception.

title: Fidelity-aware machine learning for reliable screening of low melting-point molten salts from heterogeneous experimental data
abstract: Low melting-point salts may lower auxiliary-heating demand and increase the operational flexibility of thermal-energy-storage systems. Reliable machine learning (ML) screening of low melting point molten salts requires exploiting broad literature evidence while calibrating predictions against standardized measurements. Here, a fidelity-aware ML framework based on fidelity-separated fine-tuning is developed for nitrate/nitrite salts by pretraining a composition-based neural model on 5892 records from 593 publications and recalibrating only its final prediction layer using 107 unified-protocol measurements. Four neural data-utilization strategies and two regularized regression baselines are compared through composition-grouped cross-validation; the four neural strategies are further evaluated using an independent post-development measurement set comprising six predefined salt families (S1–S6). The conventional neural strategies show residual average bias or a larger fitted-to-held-out error increase on the standardized dataset. The fidelity-aware strategy achieves a held-out-group mean absolute error (MAE) of 17.9 °C, a mean signed error of +1.1 °C, and a 3.0 °C fitted-to-held-out MAE gap. At the predefined 150 °C cutoff for this screening task, it retains all five candidate families subsequently confirmed below the cutoff, whereas literature-only, standardized-data-only, and direct-mixing strategies would have rejected four, three, and two families, respectively. Among the four neural strategies assessed independently, only the fidelity-aware strategy retains salt families S3 and S4, which are experimentally confirmed with family mean transition temperatures of 130.9 and 99.2 °C. Across six independent family means, the model achieves an MAE of 19.9 °C and a root mean square error of 23.9 °C. These results support separating broad representation learning from standardized final-scale calibration for candidate retention in nitrate/nitrite screening on the measurement scale used here.

title: Machine learning-guided prediction and design of coal-based carbon materials toward enhanced specific capacitance for supercapacitors
abstract: Supercapacitors are promising energy-storage devices whose specific capacitance (SC) can be effectively improved through the proper design of electrode materials. Coal-derived carbon materials have attracted increasing attention as supercapacitor electrode candidates, yet their design remains heavily dependent on trial-and-error experimentation, making the optimization of SC performance inefficient and costly. Herein, a machine learning-assisted approach is proposed for SC prediction and regulation of coal-based carbon materials. Specifically, an XGB-SC model is developed to rapidly predict the SC, showing good predictive performance (R2 = 0.87, RMSE = 24.57 F g−1), thereby enabling the rapid screening of high-performance electrode candidates. Interpretable analysis methods further identify specific surface area (SSA) as the dominant feature governing SC prediction and reveal its favorable range, thereby providing guidance for the design of electrode materials. A workflow integrating the XGB-SC model, the XGB-SSA model and a coal property dataset is then constructed to demonstrate the data-driven design of high-SC coal-based activated carbon electrodes. Using this workflow, a Yulin coal sample is identified as a promising precursor among more than 100 coal samples. The resulting activated carbon delivers a SC of 354.5 F g−1 at 0.5 A g−1 in a three-electrode system and also exhibits favorable performance in a symmetric device. This work may facilitate the screening and development of coal-based carbon electrodes with high SC, while providing a useful reference for the rational design of supercapacitor electrode materials.

title: Physically constrained machine-learning design of high-entropy BaTiO₃-based ceramics for capacitive energy storage
abstract: Lead-free BaTiO3-based dielectrics are candidates for high-power pulse capacitors, yet the high-entropy (Ba,A)(Ti,B)O3 compositional space at 1 mol% resolution exceeds 105 plausible combinations, making exhaustive experimental screening impractical. Here, we integrate physical constraints, including composition windows, charge balance, tolerance factor, and configurational entropy, into a machine-learning workflow to navigate this compositional space. Using a dataset of 126 reported BaTiO3-based ceramics, we construct a 61-feature physicochemical descriptor set spanning A-/B-site elemental properties, local bonding, structural stability, and thermodynamic characteristics, and reduce it to 11 core descriptors by correlation filtering and recursive feature elimination. Compared with a field-only baseline, incorporating the intrinsic compositional descriptors increases the pooled out-of-fold R2 from 0.744 to 0.842 and reduces the mean absolute error (MAE) by 29.9%, demonstrating that the model captures composition-related information beyond the field-dependent trend. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis further identifies the applied electric field and B-site local bonding descriptors as the dominant predictors of recoverable energy density. The model-predicted optimal composition, (Ba0.65Bi0.30Ca0.05)(Ti0.70Mg0.15Zr0.15)O3, forms a pseudocubic perovskite with homogeneous elemental distribution and relaxor dielectric behavior, delivering Wrec = 6.6 J cm−3 and η = 91.7% at 540 kV cm−1. The ceramic exhibits stable frequency (10–500 Hz), temperature (20–180 °C), and cycling (104 cycles) responses, while Weibull breakdown analysis indicates reliable dielectric breakdown behavior associated with the dense microstructure and homogeneous solid solution. This work shows that physically constrained machine learning can effectively navigate high-entropy perovskite composition space, providing an interpretable and transferable route for designing lead-free ABO3 capacitive energy-storage ceramics.

title: Flexible temperature sensor based on SWCNT/Ni3(HITP)2 thermoelectric materials for respiratory monitoring and machine learning-assisted material identification
abstract: Flexible thermoelectric sensors that combine temperature sensitivity, mechanical compliance, and long-term stability are important for wearable electronics. Herein, we fabricated a flexible single-walled carbon nanotube (SWCNT)/Ni3(HITP)2-polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) film (SNPF) via an ultrasound-assisted, water bath-confined in situ growth method followed by single-sided PDMS encapsulation. Ni3(HITP)2 nanocrystals were anchored onto the surfaces of SWCNT forming an integrated conductive network. Benefiting from the unique interfacial structure of SWCNT/Ni3(HITP)2, the optimized SNPF exhibited a Seebeck coefficient of 44.7 μV/K. The SNPF device exhibited exceptional temperature sensing performance, featuring a high resolution (0.5 K) and outstanding long-term stability over 500 cycles, rendering it suitable for both contact/non-contact thermal source identification and passive respiratory monitoring. Furthermore, a multilayer SNPFs device constructed by vertically stacking and electrically connecting five films demonstrated an enhanced equivalent Seebeck coefficient of 221 μV/K. When worn on the arm outdoors, this device generated an open-circuit voltage of 1.33 mV and an output power of 0.67 nW. In addition, transient thermoelectric responses generated during contact with seven materials were analyzed using machine-learning algorithms. The ExtraTrees model achieved a test accuracy of 98.04% under the present recording-level data-splitting protocol. These results demonstrate that SWCNT/Ni3(HITP)2 composites can serve as flexible thermoelectric platforms for temperature sensing, low-level body-heat-derived signal generation, and thermoelectric material recognition.

title: Machine learning-optimized design principles for multiple-resonance TADF emitters in organic light-emitting diodes
abstract: The development of multiple-resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence emitters is critical for advancing organic light-emitting diodes. However, navigating the highly constrained chemical space of these emitters requires moving beyond empirical trial-and-error. Here, we present an experimentally validated, machine-learning-guided molecular-design workflow to accelerate the targeted optimization of double‑boron MR-TADF materials. We constructed a database of over 400 MR-TADF molecules from scratch and trained an XGBoost model (test R2 = 0.77) to establish a statistical framework. This framework systematically quantifies the multi-parameter trade-offs associated with boron substitution patterns, π-conjugation positions, and heterocycle conjugation degrees. To validate this predictive workflow, we synthesized a double‑boron derivative, DPAC-DB, which possesses a moderate experimental ΔEST of 0.14 eV, close to our estimated value of 0.17 eV. Vacuum-deposited OLEDs based on DPAC-DB achieved a maximum external quantum efficiency of 35.6%, significantly outperforming its mono‑boron parent. By successfully translating computational prioritization into a highly efficient physical device, this work establishes a robust, data-driven paradigm for the rational optimization of MR-TADF emitters.

title: One-pot, ultrasensitive duplex genotyping of ctDNA in lung cancer via machine learning-assisted SERS spectral decoding
abstract: Precision treatment of lung cancer relies on accurate mutation profiling. Although minimally invasive, liquid biopsy is constrained by low ctDNA abundance and insufficient sensitivity for low-frequency mutations. To address this challenge, a catalytic hairpin assembly (CHA)-triggered magnetic surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) system was developed to accurately identify dual EGFR mutation subtypes in serum samples simultaneously. Driven by a target-initiated CHA reaction, a core-satellite nanostructure is constructed, which integrates plasmonic magnetic nanoparticles (NPs) embedded with a silent-region Raman internal standard and SERS-encoded Au@gap@Au NPs. Integrating hierarchical hot spots with internal calibration enhances quantitative reliability, enabling a broad dynamic range and enzyme-free attomolar sensitivity within a 2-h isothermal reaction. To further improve analytical precision, the narrow Raman spectral footprints were coupled with an OPLS-DA algorithm, achieving exceptional classification accuracy with an AUC of 1.00 for distinct EGFR mutation subtypes in cellular assays. Clinical proof-of-concept validation in a serum cohort comprising 39 individuals showed reliable profiling performance, with concordance of next-generation sequencing results. Owing to its robust one-pot multiplexing capability, low instrumental demands and stable analytical performance, the machine learning-assisted, CHA-triggered magnetic SERS system offers a powerful strategy for ctDNA genotyping, holding significant promise for advancing personalized and precision medicine in lung cancer.

title: Volcanic rock-supported zero-valent Fe/Ni bimetal activated periodate for the degradation of sulfamethoxazole: Performance, mechanism, and machine learning application
abstract: This study employed plant extracts as precursors to synthesize a volcanic rock-supported Fe/Ni bimetallic nanocatalyst via pyrolysis for efficient activation of periodate (PI). The results demonstrate that, at a low catalyst dosage (0.1 g⋅L−1), the system effectively activates PI (1 mM), achieving over 95% removal of sulfamethoxazole (SMX, 2 mg⋅L−1) within 120 min. Quenching experiments and electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) analysis confirmed that singlet oxygen (1O2) is the dominant reactive species, indicating that the reaction proceeds mainly via a non-radical oxidation pathway. Volcanic rock support optimizes Fe/Ni nanoparticle dispersion and inhibits aggregation; structural characterization verified enhanced defect density and abundant active sites, while the constructed mineral-metal interface accelerates electron transfer and PI activation. Machine learning analysis further identified defect degree (ID/IG) and pore structure as the key factors affecting catalytic performance. LC-MS analysis revealed that SMX degradation mainly proceeds via sulfonamide bond cleavage, aromatic oxidation, and isoxazole ring opening. Application tests using real swine wastewater demonstrated that the catalyst maintains high stability and strong anti-interference capability under complex conditions, sustaining considerable degradation efficiency during continuous-flow operation and repeated cycles. This study offers novel insights into the design of mineral-supported bimetallic catalysts for advanced water treatment applications.

title: MACE-MAX: A fine-tuned machine learning interatomic potential for high-throughput screening and experimental validation of high-entropy M2AlC MAX phases
abstract: The vast combinatorial space of multi-element M2AlC MAX phases renders systematic experimental exploration intractable. Here, we fine-tune the MACE-MP-0 foundation model on a compact training set of M2AlC compositions with N = 1–3 M-site elements to obtain MACE-MAX, a machine learning interatomic potential that predicts the formation energies of N = 3–6 compositions with an MAE of 5.3 meV/atom at ~70-fold lower cost than DFT. Combined with Monte Carlo M-site sampling, MACE-MAX screens all 465 equimolar compositions in a nine-element (Ti, V, Zr, Nb, Hf, Ta, Cr, Mo, W) design space, identifies ten synthesis candidates and reveals valence electron concentration and atomic size mismatch as the dominant stability descriptors. Synthesis and characterization of the ten candidates and a Group VIB substitution series validate the predictions on three scales. The IVB/VB compositions with the lowest Ehull form the MAX phase as the main product, whereas none of the compositions containing a Group VIB element does; EPMA confirms the predicted decomposition pathways; and atomic-resolution HAADF-STEM and EDS resolve, for the first time, M-site solid-solution disorder in a six-element HE-MAX phase, (TiVZrNbHfTa)2AlC. MACE-MAX thus provides a validated computational–experimental framework for HE-MAX discovery and for selecting precursors of high-entropy MXenes.

title: Ionically conductive hydrogels containing PEG side chains for mechanical signal sensing, Morse code communication and machine-learning-assisted input
abstract: Ionically conductive hydrogels (ICHs) are promising candidates for flexible sensors and artificial skins, but their conductivity and comprehensive properties are poor in special sensing scenarios. Herein, ICHs containing poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) side chains are developed. In such ICHs, PEG chains exhibit high freedom of motion and hydrophilicity, providing abundant bonding sites for water and cations. The ICHs are prepared by a macromonomer copolymerization method and amphiphilic triblock copolymer is introduced to enhance their mechanical properties. Conductivity of such ICHs is increased by increasing feeding content and molecular weight of double bond end-capped PEG macromonomers and a conductivity of 57.9 mS/cm has been achieved. Interestingly, such ICHs are promising in constructing flexible mechanosensors exhibiting multi-mode response ability, fast response speed, high sensitivity and stability. On the basis of a signal processing model and a machine learning algorithm, piezoresistive pressure sensors of such ICHs are demonstrated in Morse code communication and input of various contents (e.g., letters and numbers). Overall, this work provides a new clue to develop high-performance ICHs by molecular structure design of hydrogel network and candidate materials for for flexible sensing devices.

title: AI-revealed metabolic fingerprinting of ophthalmic diseases via a 3D energy-amplified coral nanomatrix
abstract: The prevalence of irreversible vision-impairing ophthalmic diseases remains high, while current diagnostic methods heavily rely on expert experience, limiting their accessibility in primary care settings. To address this, the present study utilizes iron oxide semiconductor as a scaffold to precisely engineer a multidirectional energy-amplified coral nanomatrix. Combined with nanomatrix-assisted laser desorption ionization mass spectrometry (NMALDI-MS), this approach enables high-resolution metabolic fingerprint mapping of ophthalmic diseases in a single batch analysis. The nanomatrix integrates the semiconductor's superior band structure with a high-density three-dimensional(3D) synaptic tip array, which synchronously amplifies local electric fields across the entire matrix and enhances light absorption capability, significantly promoting the separation of photogenerated charge carriers. The 3D interlaced optical trap structure on the material surface extends the effective light path, further increasing light utilization efficiency. Abundant binding sites strengthen molecular–matrix interactions, accelerating ionization and deionization processes, achieving up to 103-fold signal enhancement compared with other iron oxide morphologies. Leveraging a neural network-based deep learning platform, high-throughput processing and diagnosis of metabolic fingerprint maps were rapidly completed for 398 patients with diverse ophthalmic diseases, leading to the identification of multiple potential metabolic biomarkers. This strategy provides a low-cost, high-throughput, and easily standardized universal diagnostic solution for ophthalmic diseases, demonstrating strong potential for large-scale deployment in primary healthcare institutions.

title: AI and additive manufacturing driven design of rGO-cobalt oxide nanocomposite electrodes for supercapacitors
abstract: This work couples statistical synthesis optimization with AI-guided electrode-design to boost the electrochemical performance of additively manufactured rGO-Cobalt oxide supercapacitor electrodes. The optimal synthesis conditions found using a full-factorial design of experiments (DoE), yielding a nanocomposite with well-dispersed Co3O4 and CoO domains embedded on a conductive rGO matrix to be further applied in inks. To decouple geometry-dependent effects from material contributions, 30 printed electrode architectures were systematically evaluated, producing specific capacitances of 59.7–96.2 F/g and establishing electrode topology as a first-order performance determinant. Machine-learning models based on Multiple Linear Regression (MLR) and Random Forest Regression (RFR) were developed using geometric descriptors extracted from the 30 architectures, yielding R2 values of 0.71 and 0.85 for MLR and RFR, respectively, with corresponding Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) values of approximately 8 and 6 F/g for MLR and 5.5 and 4 F/g for RFR, respectively. The RFR model was subsequently used to identify an optimized electrode architecture, which was experimentally fabricated and achieved a specific capacitance of 104.8 F/g by cyclic voltammetry, representing an approximately 9% improvement over the best-performing architecture in the original pattern library under identical conditions. The optimized electrode further delivered a rate-capability retention of ~92%, an estimated gravimetric energy density of ~12.5 Wh/kg. These findings demonstrate that coupling DoE-validated synthesis control with AI-generated electrode topology enables simultaneous improvement of capacitance, rate performance, and energy/power metrics without chemical reformulation, establishing a scalable and transferable digital-design framework for next-generation high-performance supercapacitor electrodes.

title: Machine learning reveals interaction-driven ecological responses of DNRA-associated taxa toward data-driven operation of anammox systems
abstract: Predicting the relative abundance of DNRA-associated taxa may support microbial monitoring in anammox-based systems. However, the suitability of different predictive models and their taxon-specific predictor contribution patterns under low-carbon, nitrogen-rich conditions remain insufficiently characterized. Here, we analyzed 1292 environmental observations and 94 microbial profiles collected over 62 months from laboratory-scale anammox reactors. Multiple machine-learning models were compared to characterize relationships between environmental conditions and taxon relative abundance. Across the evaluated random train–test splits, ensemble models generally outperformed linear approaches, although the best-performing model varied by taxon. Multiple linear regression predicted Candidatus Kuenenia best, whereas random forest or extreme gradient boosting models predicted Candidatus Jettenia, Fimbriimonadaceae, Limnobacter, and Alicycliphilus best under their respective splits. This contrast revealed distinct predictive response structures among taxa within the same engineered environment. SHAP analysis identified taxon-specific predictor contribution patterns: predictions for Candidatus Jettenia and Limnobacter were primarily associated with influent NH4+ and NO2−, whereas Fimbriimonadaceae and Alicycliphilus showed broader distributions of SHAP contributions. Nitrogen loading rate and inorganic nitrogen species (NH4+, NO2−, and NO3−) were important predictors within the fitted models, but their individual contributions were interpreted cautiously because of predictor collinearity. Organic carbon variables showed comparatively limited predictive contributions within the low-carbon operating conditions represented in the dataset. Overall, this study provides a comparative evaluation of taxon-specific abundance prediction models and a descriptive interpretation of their predictor contributions. The findings support hypothesis generation and the selection of variables for microbial monitoring, while independent and temporally structured validation is needed to assess model transferability, and controlled experiments are required to evaluate ecological mechanisms.

title: Data-driven multi-parameter optimization of molecularly imprinted polymers for pico-level vitamin C detection
abstract: Molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP) technology has emerged as a promising alternative to conventional biological recognition elements because it provides molecular selectivity, chemical stability, and cost-effective fabrication. However, the performance of MIP-based electrochemical sensors remains sensitive to multiple interdependent fabrication parameters, making one-factor-at-a-time optimization inefficient and unable to resolve interactions between variables. Herein, we report a joint Bayesian surrogate-modeling framework for MIP-based electrochemical sensors, demonstrated for vitamin C detection, in which o-phenylenediamine (o-PD) concentration, template concentration, cyclic voltammetry (CV) cycle number, and rebinding pH are modeled jointly rather than independently, and a single-round, uncertainty-aware Bayesian recommendation step is used to select an untested fabrication condition. Twenty-five fabrication conditions generated by Latin hypercube sampling were used to train a four-dimensional Gaussian process regression (GPR) surrogate model, benchmarked against polynomial, support vector, and random forest regression by leave-one-out cross-validation. GPR was retained not for superior point-prediction accuracy but for its native predictive uncertainty, which enables an Expected Improvement acquisition function to recommend fabrication conditions that have not been measured; a recommended condition absent from the training set was confirmed experimentally, and, at five further GPR-recommended conditions, GPR's predictions remained close to the measured responses (R2 = 0.863) while predictions from the fixed, untuned PR and SVR models deviated more substantially under this GPR-conditioned validation. SHAP-based analysis quantified the relative contribution of each parameter to the predicted response, and two-dimensional response surfaces of the joint model visualized conditional response patterns between parameter pairs. Under the identified conditions, the sensor exhibited a linear range from 10 nM to 1 mM, a calculated limit of detection of 778 pM, and high selectivity against structurally related interferents. Detection was demonstrated in human serum and artificial urine, and a preliminary proof-of-concept in real urine collected after vitamin C intake showed good agreement with a commercial ELISA assay. Coupling joint multi-parameter modeling with uncertainty-guided recommendation offers a data-efficient route to the rational optimization of MIP-based electrochemical sensing interfaces.

title: Machine learning-assisted optimization of sewage sludge hydrothermal liquefaction for balanced biocrude oil yield, quality, and energy recovery
abstract: Hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) of sewage sludge offers a promising route for waste valorization and renewable fuel production. However, existing machine learning studies on sewage sludge HTL remain constrained by insufficient sludge-specific analysis, inadequate multi-output prediction and optimization, and poor model interpretability. To address these gaps, this study developed a machine learning-assisted framework integrating model development and optimization, model interpretation, feature elimination, and Pareto-based multi-objective optimization using a PRISMA-guided literature-derived HTL dataset comprising 594 data points from 120 peer-reviewed studies. Statistical analysis revealed that substantial variations in both input features and output variables among the four clearly defined sludge types, highlighting the importance of sludge-specific characteristics. The optimized models achieved reliable multi-target prediction, while SHAP analysis identified temperature, sludge type, and H content as the dominant predictors for yield, oil quality indicators, and energy recovery, respectively. Feature elimination reduced input variables by 38.9–66.7% while preserving predictive performance and maintaining consistent dominant features and response trends, demonstrating the robustness and interpretability of the simplified models. Pareto-based multi-objective optimization further identified a balanced HTL condition at 353.79 °C, 12.29 min, and a liquid/solid ratio of 41.01 mL/g, corresponding to a predicted biocrude oil yield of 43.76%, HHV of 34.63 MJ/kg, energy recovery of 90.14%, nitrogen and oxygen contents in oil of 2.84% and 19.55%, respectively. This work provides new insights and a data-driven strategy for accelerating engineered HTL toward desired biocrude oil production, offering a valuable reference for sustainable sewage sludge management, waste valorization, and renewable fuel development.

title: Interstitial hot-volume plasmonics for machine learning-assisted urinary SERS diagnosis of pancreatic cancer
abstract: Early detection of pancreatic cancer is hampered by the lack of a sensitive, non-invasive diagnostic platform. Although SERS-based approaches have been proposed for pancreatic cancer diagnostics, most volumetric SERS substrates rely on deeply confined hotspots near polymer templates, where limited analyte accessibility and substrate-derived Raman background can compromise spectral fidelity. Here, we introduce an interstitially localized plasmonic nanostar (IPN) platform that redistributes electromagnetic enhancement into analyte-accessible hot volumes above a three-dimensional Au/polystyrene architecture. Selective nanostar localization within interstitial regions enhances analyte–field overlap while suppressing polymer-derived Raman interference, enabling uniform, reproducible, and trace-level SERS detection. To resolve the complex signals of urine spectra, statistically selected Raman features were integrated with a logistic regression classifier, enabling discrimination between pancreatic cancer patients and healthy controls with an AUC of 0.991 and an accuracy of 96.0%. In parallel, spectral deconvolution using a reference library of urinary metabolites estimated metabolite-associated spectral contributions linked to cancer-related metabolic alterations. This integrated IPN-based SERS–machine learning strategy provides a practical route for non-invasive urinary pancreatic cancer screening and interpretable analysis of complex biofluid spectra.

title: A machine learning-driven pipeline uncovers superior electrolyte additive for high-voltage sodium-ion batteries
abstract: The discovery of electrolyte additives for high-voltage sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) remains constrained by the inefficiency of empirical trial-and-error screening across vast molecular landscapes. Here we report a machine learning (ML)-driven pipeline that bridges this gap, integrating RDKit molecular descriptors with a multilayer perceptron (MLP) regressor trained on 87,301 molecules to predict molecular oxidation potential (OP). Under a standardized benchmarking protocol spanning 11 regression algorithms, the MLP model achieved an R2 of 0.97 on the held-out test set and showed the lowest errors and the least severe underestimation in the sparsely populated high-OP region among the evaluated algorithms. Deploying this model across 1.03 million PubChem entries yielded 2291 candidates with predicted OP values of 4.0–6.0 V. From this pool, ifosfamide (IFO) was selected for experimental validation. The cells incorporating the IFO-containing electrolyte delivered 107.23 mAh g−1 after 100 cycles at 120 mA g−1, surpassing the baseline electrolyte (99.82 mAh g−1). SHAP analysis, parallel coordinate visualization, and 2D partial dependence plots revealed that the MLP model integrates fragment-level descriptors, molecular topology, conformational flexibility, and surface electronic properties to render its predictions, providing molecular-level insight into candidate prioritization. These findings highlight the effectiveness of ML in narrowing down large chemical libraries and identifying experimentally viable electrolyte additives for SIBs.

title: A physics-guided neural network with McAllister-inspired multibody aggregation: Generalizing viscosity prediction to unseen organic components in strongly non-ideal mixtures
abstract: Reliable design of multicomponent fluids requires property-prediction methods applicable to unmeasured mixture systems. Kinematic viscosity is a challenging prediction target because of its sensitivity to intermolecular interactions and non-ideal composition effects. We developed a physics-guided, McAllister-inspired neural network that combines explicit, permutation-invariant n-body composition aggregation with a shared nonlinear mapping from molecular descriptors and pure-component properties to interaction contributions. We evaluated extrapolative performance on ternary mixtures spanning regular solutions and strongly non-ideal water-containing systems using nested leave-one-component-out (LOCO) validation that excluded each of 20 organic components from model development. Diagnostic fits showed that the McAllister n-body form accurately represented composition dependence, whereas a compact shared parameterization constrained the generalized McAllister model's expressiveness. The best-performing 4-body excess-log-viscosity neural network achieved component-macro average absolute relative deviations of 6.47% overall under LOCO and 9.98% for challenging water-containing systems. Under identical data and validation conditions, its errors were approximately half those of two representative general-purpose machine-learning baselines. Ablation analysis identified permutation invariance as the largest source of improvement, with an additional gain from explicit McAllister-type n-body aggregation and a suggested benefit of 4-body interactions in water-containing systems. Combining nonlinear interaction representations learned from molecular structure and pure-component information with physically structured composition aggregation enabled accurate, broadly applicable modeling of non-ideal mixtures. The architecture can accommodate additional components without increasing its trainable parameter count and may provide a general design principle for data-driven prediction of non-ideal mixture properties.

title: Data-driven fiber morphology optimization and phase-engineered piezoelectric nanogenerators for sustainable intelligent transportation monitoring
abstract: Biodegradable self-powered sensing systems are highly attractive for intelligent logistics and smart packaging. However, their sensing performance is often limited by inadequate control of fiber morphology and insufficient utilization of the piezoelectric responses associated with different crystal phases. In this work, a strategy combining machine learning with crystal phase engineering was developed to fabricate high-performance cellulose acetate (CA)/Ba(Zr0.2Ti0.8)O3-(Ba0.7Ca0.3)TiO3 (BCZT) piezoelectric nanogenerators (PENGs). A machine-learning prediction model was developed to correlate electrospinning parameters with fiber diameter, providing quantitative guidance for regulating fiber morphology. The resulting fibrous structure was associated with relatively uniform dispersion of BCZT fillers, increased interfacial contact, and improved stress transfer, potentially contributing to enhanced interfacial polarization and electromechanical coupling. Among the investigated compositions, the CA-R5T5 composite exhibited the highest piezoelectric output. An intelligent packaging system was further constructed by placing tetragonal-phase PENGs on the top and bottom surfaces to monitor vertical impacts, and rhombohedral-phase PENGs on the sidewalls to detect vibration and tilt. The integrated sensing system achieved real-time transportation monitoring without an external power supply. This work provides an effective strategy for developing sustainable piezoelectric sensing materials by coordinating the optimization of processing parameters, microstructure, and crystal phase, offering promising potential for intelligent packaging and logistics monitoring.
